SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed persistently and in some cases specifically (HI liquid vaporiser share back to 10% in 2022 and +300bps in Q1 FY25; Exo moving from low single digit to double digit share in the East), but the gains are uneven — Pril share declined, HI revenue is still down 1.3% in FY26 — and recent dishwash share is being held with MRP cuts and grammage that shrank segment margin from ~18% to ~10%, which is share bought with profitability.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have maintained the market share, and we are growing, in fact, in many markets

CULTURE.rationale: Family-led and stable (M.R. Jyothy as MD throughout), debt-free with INR1,000 crore cash, and the HI turnaround promised '3, 4 quarters before' has visibly delivered — losses cut from INR25 crore to about INR5 crore with coil share down to one-third; they also owned the Bangladesh JV failure openly. Against that, the 2022 promise to be 'back to 15 to 16%' margins and the 16-17% EBITDA guidance were not held in FY26 (15.3%), and the cash has sat idle for years while 'scouting' acquisitions.
CULTURE.quote: we thought it prudent to cut our losses and discontinue that operation... we tried a number of things

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing described would stop a funded entrant: management's own account is of local players undercutting on liquid detergent, multiple players dropping MRPs in dishwash, and its defence being distribution reach plus A&P — all rebuildable. The only articulated barrier is direct distribution, which competitors of similar scale already possess.
MOATTEST.quote: the intensity was there from local players as well... you'll have to fight the competition, there's no escape from that

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four calls management never discusses AMC/service revenue share, attach rates, renewals or deferred revenue; the economics are the opposite of customer-funded — long build cycles keep inventory and receivables high and operating cash flow went negative in FY25, with 'positive cash flow' still an aspiration into FY26.
RECURRING.quote: The operating cash flow is negative. And if I look at our balance sheet, there is a sharp increase in the trade receivables

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct to end-industrial buyers (Airbus ecosystem, HAL, Bharat Forge, Tata, EMS contract manufacturers) through the company's own 29 sales and service offices — no prescriber/installer channel, and buyers themselves audit and approve the product.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We have a direct sales and marketing in India. We have close to 29 sales and service centers

TOLLROAD.rationale: A CNC machine costing INR50 lakh to INR20 crore is a major capex line for the customer, not a sub-1% consumable, and management explicitly says it cannot pass cost inflation through on existing contracts — the opposite of toll-road pricing indifference.
TOLLROAD.quote: We are not able to pass on the increase any cost to the customer there

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated Vision 2025 is lowest-cost/highest-quality, backed by a genuinely hard-to-copy vertically integrated base (own foundry, machine shop, sheet metal, paint) and planned backward integration into controllers that are 10-25% of machine cost — but the model is high-margin (27-31% EBITDA), not the low-margin/high-asset-turn shape the pattern describes.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are producing the highest quality, the lowest cost, easy-to-use product for our customer

PRICING.rationale: FY26 shows real conditional pricing power — raw material up 2-3% and prices raised from 1 May on new orders, with EBITDA margin rising from 22.5% (FY24) to 27% (FY25) and 26.8-31.9% in FY26 amid an 18-month waiting list — but management concedes the existing fixed-price backlog cannot be repriced, so margin gains lean on mix and operating leverage as much as price.
PRICING.quote: From 1st of this May, we have increased our prices for the new -- to our new customers and new orders

BRAND.rationale: There is genuine heritage and third-party validation — Huron making milling machines since 1827 and 5-axis since 1905, plus 'Best Brand in the Metal Cutting Industry' from Economic Times for seven consecutive years and 135,000 machines installed in 60 countries — but no A&P spend, distributor leverage or consumer-style premium pricing is ever discussed.
BRAND.quote: for the seventh consecutive year, the award for Best Brand in the Metal Cutting Industry by Economic Times

INNOVATION.rationale: R&D is a repeated, cadenced theme across all calls with named products and traceable revenue: the Leonardo Da Vinci centre (2008, 140+ engineers), 200+ variants across 44 verticals, 7th SENSE (2017), PreciProtect (2019), VST160 for EV (2022), seven launches at IMTEX 2025 and a patented HUMA panel — and the Tachyon developed pre-emptively for EMS delivered a 13% revenue segment on first entry in Q3 FY24.
INNOVATION.quote: In 2025, we have launched 7 new products in January 2025 in IMTEX exhibition

FORWARD.rationale: Jyoti sells and services direct rather than through dealers, with 29 owned sales/service offices across 12 states, subsidiaries in France, Germany, Canada and Turkey, and a US entity being staffed in FY27 — genuine forward integration for a capital-goods maker, but there are no stores, franchising, royalties or D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: Within Q1 now we are, let's say, appointing all our sales team and our tech centers

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Revenue compounded from INR1,330cr (FY24) to INR1,818cr (FY25) to ~INR2,100cr consolidated FY26 with an import-substitution runway, but management gives no explicit share numbers beyond 'third position' in India, and FY26 order book growth slowed to ~5.5% because capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint — share gain is asserted rather than evidenced.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the Indian CNC machine tools market continued to be largely served through import

CULTURE.rationale: Positives are real — leadership stable since inception with key managers of 20+ years, the ~25% margin guidance repeated in 2025 was met or beaten, and the FY26 promise of turning cash flow positive was delivered and the Huron export-control investigation plus INR67cr revenue reversal disclosed promptly; against that, the Feb 2024 promise of becoming debt-free in two to three years was reversed by a INR300cr Union Bank term loan, and answers on quantifying FY27 execution are deflected.
CULTURE.quote: the last year, we were into negative cash flow to we entered into positive

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are hard to rebuild — Huron's 190-year 5-axis precision lineage, a fully integrated plant down to its own foundry, 29 service offices and 15,000+ customers, plus aerospace/defence qualification — but the company itself concedes dependence on Siemens/FANUC controllers (10-25% of machine cost) and that mastering motion control took those incumbents decades, so the deepest layer of the moat is one Jyoti is still trying to buy rather than one it owns.
MOATTEST.quote: in a decade this Japanese and German manufacturer has developed this product and they have made mastery

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 17 calls the model is one-off product sale of tiles/bathware/adhesives — no licence fees, AMC, subscriptions, attach rates or renewal language anywhere; working capital is positive and discussed as a drag (57 days in Jul-2022, 59 in Jul-2024, 64 in Dec-2025, 51 in Mar-2026), the opposite of customers funding the business.
RECURRING.quote: working capital days increased by 8 days to 64 days compared to 56 days on 30th of September '25, mainly due to increase in receivables

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through a dealer/showroom channel rather than end-consumer direct, and by Jan-2026 management made the specifier community an explicit strategic thrust, but there is no evidence of trade training programmes or professional lock-in over the 5-year record.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we are putting a major thrust on the architect and interior designer community... a very solid team all over India whose job is only to service these architects and interior designers and get products approved

TOLLROAD.rationale: Management makes the classic small-share-of-customer-cost argument in Apr-2026 to defend a 12-13% price hike, but tiles are anything but a rational oligopoly — Morbi alone has 500-600 plants — and the company itself concedes prices don't rise with so many players.
TOLLROAD.quote: tile is a very small segment in the entire real estate project. So just for that price increase, they will not stop their construction

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine cost culture only appears late, under 'Kajaria 2.0' (FY26): itemised savings (INR5 crores from scrapping the Thailand dealer meet, renegotiated ad vendors, SKU rationalisation, line conversions) lifted EBITDA from ~12.8% to 17-19%; but Kajaria is a premium-priced brand, not a low-price/high-turns operator, and it does not pass savings to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: we have not done one annual dealer meet, we used to do in Thailand. So that has -- we have saved around INR5 crores. So -- and we have negotiated well with our existing advertisement vendors

PRICING.rationale: The record shows price deflation, the pattern's disqualifier: own-manufactured realisation fell ~9% from Rs.401/sqm in Q3FY23 to Rs.365/sqm in Q3FY26, discounts were given in Q3FY26 to clear SKUs, and the FY26 12-17% hikes were pure gas-cost pass-through, not value capture.
PRICING.quote: prices of tiles are not increasing in the market with so many players there... it has fallen from 401 square meter in Q3 of FY '23 to right now at 365 square meters

BRAND.rationale: Brand equity is repeatedly the stated lever for both price and share (2% hike in May-2022, share gains in a flat industry), backed by sustained A&P of ~Rs.100 crores a year, ~1,700 dealers with 380 exclusive showrooms, and stretch into bathware (Kerovit), adhesives and plywood under the same name — though the ply adjacency was shut by FY26, showing the stretch has limits.
BRAND.quote: we have leveraged our brand equity to drive a 2% price increase in May 2022 which enabled us to maintain our margins at 15% plus

INNOVATION.rationale: There is regular product/technology upgrading — Continua+ slabs from Sacmi at Srikalahasti (2022), GVT mix shift, conversion of a 9.1 msm Gailpur ceramic line to GVT (FY26) — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed, no pipeline or industry-R&D-share language, and the innovation is capex-led capability rather than margin-funded invention.
INNOVATION.quote: This plant has the most advanced technology Continua+ from Sacmi Italy for slabs manufacturing in South India

FORWARD.rationale: Forward movement is via exclusive dealer showrooms (380 of ~1,700 dealers in 2022, ~50 added that year) and control of display shelf-space, which management says is decisive; but there are no company-owned stores, no franchise royalties and no D2C revenue disclosed across five years.
FORWARD.quote: In our industry, what is visible is sold. If I have displayed certain, if I am a dealer of X... somebody comes to me and offers 10%-15% less, even then I cannot sell because I cannot display

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is a constant stated ambition and was delivered in some years (grew when the industry was flat in FY24), but the promised '15%+ volume growth' of Jul-2022 was not sustained — FY25 guidance was cut to low-double-digit and Q3FY26 volumes were flat — and no hard share percentages are ever given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: even if the industry doesn't grow, which has happened in the past, the industry didn't grow but we took the market share... despite the number one company, we are -- our market share is very less

CULTURE.rationale: Positives are real: stable family leadership with succession under way (Chetan/Rishi to Vice Chairman/MD, grandson Kartik on calls), debt-light balance sheet funding capex from internal accruals with a 40-50% dividend policy, and prompt disclosure of a subsidiary fraud with an E&Y forensic audit and tightened signing authority; against that, guidance was repeatedly missed and eventually abandoned, and the fraud itself is a control failure.
CULTURE.quote: guidance, as you are aware, I have always given, right? It didn't work out... So my request will be going forward not to give any guidance

MOATTEST.rationale: Articulable barriers exist — a national multi-location plant footprint that Morbi single-site players cannot match on gas/logistics risk, brand, and dealer display economics — but a single competing line costs only ~Rs.100-120 crores and 24 months, and 500-600 Morbi plants plus falling realisations show the advantage is contestable rather than un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: Kajaria and other players who have multi locational plants will have a great advantage as we go forward

RECURRING.rationale: The gold savings scheme is a persistent, advance-funded revenue stream disclosed consistently — Feb 2026 quantified it at 18-20% of revenue and 'very active over the last many years' — and management links older stores' higher SSSG to scheme maturity, but there is no post-sale licence/AMC/renewal economics of the classic pattern.
RECURRING.quote: Gold savings, the exchange gold usually is in the range of +30%; and it has been 1% or 2% more in Q3... Again, gold saving scheme usually is in the range of 18% to 20%, which remains the same.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Jewellery is a large discretionary ticket for the end consumer, not a tiny-but-critical input; the calls show demand swinging with gold prices, customs duty cuts and promotions rather than price-insensitive, non-negotiated purchase.
TOLLROAD.quote: post the duty cut, again, when the price comes down by 7%, 8% customers who were waiting would have come in immediately

PRICING.rationale: Realisations track the gold price rather than management pricing decisions; across FY25-FY26 the response to high gold prices was to trim inventory volume, push 18/14/9-karat lower-value product, and run exchange offers and promotions, and in Aug 2024 they raised ad spend rather than price to hold share, missing the PBT target that quarter.
PRICING.quote: we have constant promotions at the store level, which will happen, dull season, off-season drivers, exchange offers

BRAND.rationale: Sustained ~1.8-2% of sales on advertising through every call, brand trust cited as the reason they will not sell unstable-priced lab-grown diamonds (Aug 2024), and the name is stretched into adjacencies — Candere omnichannel (110 stores, PAT-positive FY26), a new regional brand, and UK/US pilots — while non-South share rose from ~30% (2022) to 49% (2024).
BRAND.quote: customer is buying those diamonds because they trust Kalyan as a brand. So if the price goes down, they will feel very offended.

INNOVATION.rationale: There is regular product/format renewal — fresh festive collections, a push into 18/14/9-karat studded lines, the Candere digital-first platform and a new regional brand — but no R&D disclosure or industry-R&D-share argument; innovation here is merchandising, not a funded innovation engine.
INNOVATION.quote: there are certain states especially South India, where 18-karat acceptance will be much slower... where we have launched many collections in 18-karat

FORWARD.rationale: The clearest pattern in the record: from the first franchise pilot in Aurangabad (Aug 2022) to franchisee-funded capex (Aug 2024, '0.25% margin growth'), 129 showrooms opened in FY26, 150 planned for FY27, Candere D2C-to-omnichannel, and an announced Middle East FOCO conversion drive with Arab investors — third parties fund the store growth.
FORWARD.quote: The rest of the showrooms, the franchisee partners will put the capex fit out also.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Repeated, quantified share gain across four years: new customers in excess of 35% of revenue, non-South mix 30%→34%→49%, SSSG explicitly described as ahead of listed peers and taking share from unorganised and named regional players, plus US/UK/Middle East expansion — and it is accompanied by rising PAT (FY26 PAT +89%) and falling debt, not bought growth.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we would have gained market share from the existing players... there has been a strategic misstep taken by two players in South

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in old calls were delivered in later ones — the 2022 franchise pilot scaled into the core growth engine, non-GML India debt cut from INR1,300cr to INR300cr over three years, Candere turned PAT-positive as guided, and a dividend policy was honoured; leadership (Ramesh Kalyanaraman, Sanjay Raghuraman, Swaminathan) is unchanged across all 17 calls and they own misses openly, as in Aug 2024 on the PBT shortfall.
CULTURE.quote: the operating leverage we thought would come from marketing, did not come. And that is why the PBT did not grow more than our revenue.

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but not un-replicable barriers: multi-decade brand trust, a dense showroom network whose visibility itself lifts SSSG ('network effect'), a large gold-savings customer base and a vetted franchisee pool — yet the calls also show well-funded competitors contesting the same markets with marketing, forcing Kalyan's ad spend up, so a copycat with capital is slowed rather than blocked.
MOATTEST.quote: More number of showrooms, more expansion, thereby meaning more visibility for Kalyan and thereby helping generate more footfalls and revenue.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all nine calls management discusses paint volumes, mix and services, but never licence fees, AMCs, renewal rates, attach rates or deferred revenue/customer advances as a funding source. The evidence is silent on a recurring-revenue model.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Every call is built around the trade influencer: painters, architects/interior designers, contractors, dealers and A-class auto body shops choose or apply the product while the homeowner or OEM pays. The influencer programme is repeatedly quantified (architect reach in 40+ cities in FY25, painter 'extraction' rising, services at >5% of decorative by FY26) and management explicitly says brand, distribution and painter relationships 'take time' to build — the switching cost.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: the market takes time to build brand, distribution and the painters, it takes time

TOLLROAD.rationale: The industrial/auto side has toll-road traits — approvals-gated (WRAS, fusion-bonded epoxy, coil-coat approvals), 200–300 technical staff embedded on customer lines, 50%+ four-wheeler share, and competition described as performance- not price-driven — but management never frames the coating as a sub-1-2% share of customer cost, and the decorative half of the business is plainly price-contested.
TOLLROAD.quote: performance-driven rather than purely price-driven... more than 200–300 technically competent people deployed on customer lines

LOWPRICE.rationale: The strategy is the opposite of low-price-plus: they deliberately exited low-margin performance-coating business over 1–1.5 years, let putty volumes go negative rather than chase price, and target premiumisation and niche segments. Cost work exists (cost-reduction efforts aiding FY24 margins) but as margin defence, not a scale/low-price model.
LOWPRICE.quote: we decided to exit some low profit business... we wanted to replace that business with a premium

PRICING.rationale: Nine calls contain no instance of raising price above cost inflation while holding volume; average selling price is held up by mix, not price, and putty shows outright deflation. Revenue growth of 1.5–3.5% with 'marginally negative to flat' decorative and PBT down 4% YTD FY26 is the signature of absent pricing power.
PRICING.quote: on putty... pricing definitely is a challenge in the marketplace... in our case, it is negative

BRAND.rationale: Real heritage and sustained A&P — a 100-year model, a three-decade jingle refreshed in FY26, Asia Cup/World Cup spends, ad spend up 20% in Q2FY24 — and self-described 'second most recognized brand' on equity index. But the pattern's test (share gain plus premium pricing) fails: they are No.3 overall, decorative share is 'about same', and brand has not prevented Grasim-led redistribution.
BRAND.quote: We proudly hold the position of a second most recognized brand in terms of the brand equity index nationwide

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches appear in every single call with disclosed revenue impact — Beauty Little Master Sheen and Crystal Seal (FY24), 20+ products including Wow Whites (FY25), Excel Everlast 20 and Total Floor Coat plus BTX-free monocoats and low-bake CED (FY26) — with Paint+ salience crossing 10% of decorative and new-product contribution in double digits, funded by Japanese parent technology and an internal innovation programme.
INNOVATION.quote: Paint+ group of products... their contribution to overall decorative business is greater than 10%

FORWARD.rationale: Genuine movement toward the customer — NXTGEN Shoppe/shop-in-shop/Paint Zone network from 300+ in FY25 to 600+ by FY26, painting-as-a-service with digital lead generation now >5% of decorative revenue and 'control on that particular business' — but no owned-store economics, franchise royalties or D2C share disclosed; the core remains a dealer-distribution model.
FORWARD.quote: we are generating the digital leads and we are having the control on that particular business

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is real and repeated in industrial/auto ('increasing market share in automotive even on the high base', 50%+ four-wheeler, auto-refinish and high-performance coating growing above industry), but decorative share is flat at best across FY25–FY26 and the company remains No.3 nationally, over-indexing on selected zones and towns rather than gaining broadly.
SHAREGAIN.quote: industrial, we are able to grow market share. And in case of decorative, it will be about same market share

CULTURE.rationale: Management owns misses candidly (a service complaint on the FY24 call, 'we were a little slow on this initiative... maybe it got delayed') and delivered milestones it promised years earlier — Paint+ and new-business salience reaching double digits, services hitting the 5% critical-mass target, 80+ project towns — while holding EBITDA guidance and avoiding price wars. Against that: leadership has turned over (Chairman Shah and MD Anuj Jain both exited FY2024–25, MD now Pravin Chaudhari), so the long-tenured-stewardship element is not evidenced.
CULTURE.quote: Initially, we were a little slowed on this initiative. We were not on target

MOATTEST.rationale: Industrial coatings pass the cost-to-replicate test as management articulates it — supply chain, OEM approvals, line support, global track record, eight plants, 'a long time before competition poses a serious threat'. Decorative fails it: a well-funded entrant (Grasim) built distribution and took share within two years, and management's own answer is that its rival's approach 'is not very different from what we have been doing'.
MOATTEST.quote: This is not a business that can be entered easily, as it is performance-driven rather than purely price-driven

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Origination genuinely runs through intermediaries — the NEO/open market channel, DSAs, connectors and DSTs, co-lending NBFCs and BNPL partners (DSA commission is a named opex line by FY26) — but the lock-in the pattern requires is absent: no trade training or professional reputation moat, and customers are visibly price-sensitive.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Business is sourced through channel partners, connectors and DSTs

TOLLROAD.rationale: Credit is a large, openly negotiated cost for the borrower, not a sub-1% critical input; across FY25–FY27 calls management repeatedly loses or retains accounts purely on rate, the opposite of 'customers don't switch once converted'.
TOLLROAD.quote: allowed a few accounts to be taken over by others due to lower pricing

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is half-present: relentless cost discipline (cost-to-income guided below 50% and delivered 56%→46% in FY23 and 42% for FY26, opex up only 2.45% in FY26) and genuinely high-quality loans (GNPA 3.97% in Sep-22 to 0.74% by Jun-26, net NPA 0.19%, unsecured just 1.81%), but the cheap-deposit leg is the acknowledged weak spot — CASA growth lags, deposit costs rose through FY25–26 and NIM is defended by asset mix, not funding cost.
LOWPRICE.quote: For full year under review, opex had gone up by 2.45% over previous year.

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly concedes it cannot raise price without losing volume — the May-26 and Jul-26 calls say they must 'compromise on margins' in MSME and to retain existing LAP/commercial customers, and FY27 NIM guidance is set below the current 4.26% exit level.
PRICING.quote: even for the retention of existing customers somewhere it is becoming necessity for us to compromise on the margins

BRAND.rationale: There is real regional heritage (Tamil Nadu bank since 1916) and sticky multi-decade relationships management leans on for win-backs in bulk deposits and jewel loans, plus retail households at 72% of deposits — but no A&P spend, no premium pricing, and depositors keep leaving for better yields elsewhere.
BRAND.quote: they are all our customers for decades... It is literally homecoming for them

INNOVATION.rationale: Steady incremental product and digital output is named each year — digital lending platform and co-lending (FY23), 24 new CASA variants (FY25), GST surrogate and open term loan, LAP, loan against mutual funds, relaunched credit cards, API-first Transaction Banking, DLite app with 2.5mn MAU and 98% digital transactions (FY26–27) — but there is no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-R&D, and none of it commands pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: 2.5 million monthly active users for our DLite app and 7 million DLite downloads

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has been consistently above system (advances 16–17% y-o-y, RAM verticals +18%, retail +25%, total business INR1.7lakh cr in Jun-24 to INR2.27lakh cr by Jun-26) with an explicit 1–2% above-industry credit growth target, and critically the share is not bought with credit standards — slippages under 1%, corporate cut from 45% to 14% of book. But no explicit market-share numbers or named-competitor comparisons are given, and growth is deliberately moderated when pricing turns unfavourable.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our guidance for credit growth of 1% or 2% over the industry growth will continue

CULTURE.rationale: Across all 17 calls the same MD (Ramesh Babu, in post since 2020) sets three metrics — growth, profitability, asset quality — and delivers: ROA 0.86%→2.11%, GNPA 3.97%→0.74%, NIM guidance of 3.7–3.75% beaten at 3.97%, credit cost within guidance, no capital raise needed as ploughback funds growth, and prudential provisioning of INR163 cr taken ahead of geopolitical stress. Management also owns past errors plainly (the corporate book it built and then unwound) and flags bad news itself — the Q1 FY27 caution that front-loaded growth should not be extrapolated.
CULTURE.quote: going back to again, corporate for the purpose of our system growth will defeat the purpose of the whole exercise we have done in the last few years... not to commit our earlier mistake

MOATTEST.rationale: The replicable-in-a-few-years test is only half passed: a century-old Tamil Nadu branch and retail-household deposit base (72% of deposits) plus a demonstrably rebuilt underwriting culture would take a newcomer years, but the calls themselves show the advantage being competed away on price in LAP, housing, MSME and commercial, and the deposit franchise is the acknowledged constraint rather than a fortress.
MOATTEST.quote: LAP segment is experiencing strong pricing competition, making both customer retention and new acquisition a bit challenging

RECURRING.rationale: Kaynes is a project/order-book EMS business with no license, AMC, subscription or attach-rate disclosure across 17 calls; far from customers funding it, working capital is a chronic drain (135 days in FY23, 139 days in Q3FY26, 122 days FY26) with metering annuities parked in non-current assets that management is trying to discount away.
RECURRING.quote: working capital days stood at around 122 days in FY '26

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No evidence either way: sales are direct B2B to OEMs and AMISPs, and no trade professional, installer or prescriber channel or training programme is ever discussed.

TOLLROAD.rationale: There are real approval/qualification gates — approved-meter lists with only a few 'preferred suppliers', agency approvals for Kavach safety-critical designs, FSA approval under ISM — but Kaynes supplies the whole assembly (a large share of customer cost) and competes with four to five named device players, so it lacks the tiny-cost-share, non-negotiated toll economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: if you go to the list of approved meters, there are a large number, but not all of them are actually preferred suppliers

LOWPRICE.rationale: The calls contain no cost-culture narrative, itemised savings or no-frills positioning; the only cost remark is that long order books allow cheaper component buying, which is a procurement effect rather than a low-price strategy.

PRICING.rationale: Across all calls management never cites a price increase; margins are explicitly explained as product-mix swings in a high-mix bespoke business with non-cancellable fixed-price orders booked one to two years ahead, and value-added mix — not price — is the stated route to margin.
PRICING.quote: we are a very high mix company... sometimes, the margins will go up and down, but it's not significant

BRAND.rationale: Management states outright that there is no Kaynes-branded product; even in smart meters they sell under a licensed Iskraemeco brand owned by the foreign parent, with no A&P spend, heritage story or consumer pull anywhere in the record.
BRAND.quote: we still remain an ODM and EMS company. We don't have a Kaynes branded product.

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a credible and repeated push up the value chain — OSAT at Sanand, HDI multilayer PCB at Chennai, and a May 2026 target to take NPD-led/value-added solutions to ~30% of revenue with R&D and co-development investment — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed, no named products with revenue impact, and gross margins (EBITDA ~15-16%) are too thin to fund innovation-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: steadily increase the contribution of NPD-led and value-added solutions to nearly 30% of the total revenue

FORWARD.rationale: The strategic direction is explicitly backward integration (PCB fabrication, OSAT), and when an analyst framed the Iskraemeco deal as forward integration management rejected it, confirming scope stays manufacturing-only with no own stores, franchising or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: Scope of work exactly the same as before, where it is manufacture and -- it's manufacturing. It's EMS work actually.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Revenue compounded hard (57-62% in FY23, 33% in FY26) with a stated ambition to become India's largest smart-meter EMS and an order book at INR9,000 crore, but management never cites its own market share numbers, much of the gain came via acquisitions (Iskraemeco, August Electronics), and the metering push stalled — FY26 growth came ex-metering while guidance was missed.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our objective, as I stated, is to become the largest EMS in the smart meter area.

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-led with a conservative balance sheet (D/E 0.28 in FY23 to 0.2 in FY26) and unusually candid ownership of misses in the May 2026 call, but the delivery-versus-promise record is poor: FY26 guidance went INR4,500cr to INR4,000cr to INR3,626cr while being reaffirmed on TV 75 days into the quarter, working capital reduction promised since Feb 2023 remained unmet (85-day target versus 139 days in Q3FY26), and the top team churned (CEO Rajesh Sharma and MD roles reshuffled).
CULTURE.quote: we sincerely understand and appreciate that the guidance what we have given, we could not meet

MOATTEST.rationale: Some articulable barriers exist — 30+ years of qualification with 300-plus customers, high-mix programmes that are hard to shift, customer design approvals, and now INR1,500 crore of HDI PCB plus OSAT capital with ISM subsidy — but EMS capacity is fundamentally buildable with money, the company itself admits others in the sector benefit from the same China+1 tailwind, and it holds no un-replicable data, location or brand asset.
MOATTEST.quote: It's not very easy to shift these businesses, and it's very difficult to develop these businesses.

RECURRING.rationale: KEC is a lumpy tender-driven EPC contractor with no licence, AMC, subscription or attach-rate revenue discussed in any of the 16 calls; instead of customer advances funding the business, working capital absorbs cash — net debt including acceptances rose from ~INR3,418cr (Jun-22) to INR6,722cr (Mar-26) despite record profits.
RECURRING.quote: our net debt, including acceptances is at INR 6,722 crores

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Orders come from direct competitive tendering with utilities, PGCIL, TBCB developers and private clients — no prescriber/installer channel, no trade training programmes; management repeatedly describes bid counts, not channel relationships.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: In some tenders, we have seen 13, in one of them, I saw, 41 bids coming in

TOLLROAD.rationale: EPC contracts are a large share of the client's project capex, awarded by L1 price tender rather than being a tiny critical input; there is no certification/standards anchoring or 'don't switch once converted' language across the four years of calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: We have clearly defocused on the Civil projects in the country, because of intense competition

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is mechanisation/cost-optimisation talk (automation initiatives in FY23, the FY26 execution-excellence programme with a global consultant), but this is price competition without the hallmark of the pattern — returns are modest (FY26 operating PAT margin 2.6%) and the balance sheet is debt-heavy rather than high-turn and cash-generative.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are making good progress in deploying several mechanization, automation and utilization initiatives across projects

PRICING.rationale: Roughly half the order book is fixed-price, so margins are set by commodity and labour inflation rather than by KEC raising prices — FY23 margins collapsed on committed high-cost orders and FY26 guidance was cut mid-year from 100bps improvement to 'maybe 7% to 7.5%'.
PRICING.quote: roughly I'll say 50% or so would be on fixed and the balance would be on variable

BRAND.rationale: KEC carries real industry standing — the PGCIL award for maximum circuit-km added in FY24, marquee private and international clients, RPG-group identity — but reputation buys pre-qualification and invitations to bid, not premium pricing or share-plus-margin expansion.
BRAND.quote: KEC received an award for executing the maximum circuit kilometer addition transmission line in India for FY '24 from PGCIL

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady cadence of named new capabilities across the calls — signalling cables and jumper dropper wire (FY23), aluminium conductors and UL export approvals (FY25), elastomeric and E-Beam cables plus HVDC converter stations and KAVACH (FY26) — but R&D spend is never disclosed, gross margins are thin, and most 'innovation' is capability/pre-qualification building rather than proprietary product.
INNOVATION.quote: we have developed and launched new products such as signaling cables and jumper dropper wire through this facility

FORWARD.rationale: The integration described runs the other way — cables/conductor plants built to feed KEC's own railway and T&D projects — and there are no own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C channels anywhere in the record.
FORWARD.quote: This strategy of backward integration is helping us make cables business a strategic enabler for our railways business

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Sustained expansion is visible — T&D revenue +24% in FY26 to INR15,883cr with segment mix rising 59%→68%, record order intake of INR25,280cr, SAE growth of 36%, and new geographies (Australia tower supply, Saudi 380kV GIS, first Africa oil & gas project) — but management never quotes its own market share, and the share it does cite (private players at 75-80% of TBCB) is the clients', while civil and transportation are being deliberately shrunk.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we continue to scale up our presence with private sector clients and have secured orders of INR 3,600 crores from private players and SEBs during the year

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable (Kejriwal MD and Aggarwal CFO across FY22-FY26) and bad news is disclosed candidly — SAE Brazil losses, cable margins below market, water-project payment stress, hedging guidance downward in Jan-26 — but the delivery-vs-promise record is weak: the Aug-22 promise of debt back to ~INR2,500cr and 'targeting' double-digit margins by FY24 ended instead with 7.0% EBITDA and INR6,722cr net debt in FY26.
CULTURE.quote: our cable margins are at least 200 to 300 bas is points lower than the market... I think we have been a little bit underinvested in this busin ess

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are real and slowly built — HVDC converter-station execution, 765kV/GIS credentials, Saudi Aramco approval, SAE's US/Mexico/Brazil tower plants and pre-qualifications that take years to accumulate — but the same calls show 41 bidders in civil tenders and six new private entrants in TBCB, i.e. large parts of the business are contestable by any well-funded contractor.
MOATTEST.quote: It has also received approval from Saudi Aramco for biddi ng for onshore oil and gas pipeline projects. The business continues to focus on building required pre -qualifications

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 15 calls KEI describes one-time product sales — order books, tenders, dealer stocking — with no license, AMC, subscription or renewal stream; working capital runs positive (2.5-4 months inventory carried, retention money, acceptances), the opposite of customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: we are carrying 2.5 months plus inventory in our floor and 1-month inventory during the transit period

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run heavily through a 2,000+ dealer/distributor channel and through end-user approvals and EPC contractors rather than consumer advertising, but management describes channel expansion, depot stocking and 'exchanging from weak hands to stronger hands' rather than professional training or prescriber lock-in; dealer churn of 10-12% a year argues against strong switching costs.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: every year, 10% to 12% is the churning of dealers, some dealers leaves and some new are added

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cable is a small share of a project's cost yet indispensable and time-critical, and management repeatedly notes buyers cannot defer purchases despite copper spikes; but this is a competitive, tender-driven commodity market with new entrants (Torrent, Surya, Roshni, Luker), not a rational oligopoly with switching lock-in.
TOLLROAD.quote: prices really do not affect the project... ultimately, that product has to be purchased to complete the project

LOWPRICE.rationale: The excerpts contain no cost-obsession culture, itemised savings, or no-frills positioning; margin improvement is attributed to scale, product mix and capacity, not a low-cost model.

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is explicitly a pass-through of copper/aluminium, revised fortnightly up or down and built into tender price-variation clauses — not price increases above cost inflation; the Feb 2026 '15% wire, 10% cable' rise was purely metal-driven.
PRICING.quote: Whenever copper goes up, price goes up; copper goes down, price goes down. It's a normal practice adopted by all the industry players.

BRAND.rationale: Management cites 'our brand strategy' and end-user approvals as the dealer differentiator and B2C share rose from 38% (Q1 FY23) to 56% (Q4 FY26), but there is no heritage narrative, no disclosed A&P spend, and no evidence of price premium — brand functions as availability plus approvals rather than pricing power.
BRAND.quote: it is the approvals with the various end users and also our brand strategy, the stocking of wires and cables in our depots

INNOVATION.rationale: There is genuine technical capability build-up — EHV up to 400 kV, National Grid UK qualification, electron-beam solar wires commissioned at Sanand, in-house PVC/LT-XLPE compounds — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed, and management says new products carry 'similar margin', so innovation is capability-led rather than margin-funding.
INNOVATION.quote: KEI is the only Indian company to qualify in National Grid UK framework agreement for maximum voltages up to 400 kV

FORWARD.rationale: KEI sells through independent dealers and 26 depots with no own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C; the B2C shift is distributor-led wholesaling, not forward integration to the end customer.
FORWARD.quote: The total active working dealers of the company as on 31st March '26 was approximately 2,125.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Consistent above-industry growth over the whole period — net sales INR8,104cr (FY24) to INR11,746cr (FY26), dealers 1,800 to 2,125, exports up 58%/79%/45% with country-specific UL and European certifications, EHV growing 82-85% — and share gained with rising, not falling, margins (EBITDA 10.42% in Q1FY23 to 12.21% in Q4FY26) and near-zero net debt.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our present growth is in spite of all these co[mpetitors]... exports to Australia, US, Europe... growth in export is 45%

CULTURE.rationale: Anil Gupta has led through the full 5 years with the same CFO, guidance has been repeatedly met (17-18% growth guided in 2022 and delivered; 20%+ delivered FY26), capital is allocated to organic capex (Sanand INR2,000cr) funded from cash with borrowings of only INR134cr against INR700cr cash, and bad news is disclosed plainly — the six-month Sanand delay, flat aluminium volumes, lost March export shipments.
CULTURE.quote: our Sanand plant was commissioning of first phase was delayed by around 6 months

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but partial barriers: decades of end-user and utility approvals, plant-specific and country-specific type tests, BIS licences, and EHV qualifications that management says take years and delay each new plant's ramp — yet the wire segment is being entered by well-funded copycats (Torrent, Surya, Roshni, Luker) within a year, so the moat holds in EHV/institutional cable but not across the business.
MOATTEST.quote: when we set up a new plant, it takes a little while to get that plant approval -- specific plant -- plant-specific approvals also from the customers

RECURRING.rationale: Core RTA economics are annuity-like fees on an installed base of AUM/folios that compound as SIP flows accrete, plus platform licences (mPower, XAlt, data lakes) with renewals — e.g. Jan-2025 call notes a renewed mPower fund-administration contract from its largest AMC client, and management repeatedly points to the 'sticky' compounding retail book. Advance billing / deferred revenue as a funding source is never discussed, but the recurring-stream-on-installed-base evidence is consistent across all five years.
RECURRING.quote: SIP inflows... the retail book which is usually sticky and compounding is something that we believe will overtime help KFin Tech's overall AUM share to increase

TOLLROAD.rationale: KFin is one of only two meaningful mutual-fund RTAs and one of three licensed CRAs for NPS — a regulator-anchored oligopoly whose fee is a few basis points of an AMC's cost base yet is mission-critical record-keeping, so transitions take 'two to three quarters' and client losses are rare enough to be named individually (Navi, Feb-2023). Management explicitly frames wins as licence/mandate-based and regulatory-anchored across all 17 calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have secured the license to become the second central record keeping agent for National Pension System

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real cost culture — 'frugal engineering', headcount reduction alongside 15-28% volume growth via tech transformation (Feb-2023), and explicit undercutting of incumbents on price to win share in NPS and internationally — but management never itemises savings as a system, and margins are premium (44-45% EBITDA) rather than thin-margin/high-turn.
LOWPRICE.quote: extremely compelling cost propositions

PRICING.rationale: The evidence points the other way: telescopic AUM-linked pricing means yields fall as assets grow, and the April-2025 pricing discounts are cited in May-2026 as the reason 21% AUM growth converted to only ~11% revenue growth. Value-added solutions and the NPS shift to basis-points pricing partly offset, but there is no instance across 17 calls of price increases taken above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: part of that was the pricing discounts that were given in the month of April 2025

BRAND.rationale: Heritage since 1985 and reputation clearly win mandates — 80% of Q1 FY27 main-board IPOs by market cap, admission to BlackRock's nine-firm global Aladdin administrator list, and 'right to win' language in international bids — but this is B2B institutional credibility with no A&P spend, distributor leverage, or consumer brand stretch.
BRAND.quote: our right to win has been consolidating both in terms of the cost optimization we are able to offer

INNOVATION.rationale: Named proprietary platforms arrive nearly every year with attributable revenue — Hexagram/mPower fund accounting, XAlt for alternatives, data lakes (eight contracts by Jan-2025), mPower Wealth (five mandates within three months of October-2024 launch), India's first gig-economy pension platform — and management ties win rates directly to them. Absolute R&D spend and share-of-industry R&D are never disclosed, which is the only gap.
INNOVATION.quote: probably the only player in the country who have a proprietary fit-for-purpose platform, a fully integrated transfer agency and fund administration together

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gains are explicit, quantified and persistent across the whole 2023-2026 record: MF AUM share 30.7%→31.7%→32.4%→33%; Issuer Solutions by Nifty-500 market cap 43%→49%→52%; AIF share 30%→33%→37-38%; NPS 0%→10% in four years growing 3-3.5x industry; international clients 22→70→~500 post-Ascent. Gains are mandate-won rather than bought, though the FY26 equity-AUM share dip and the April-2025 discounts show some price was paid.
SHAREGAIN.quote: in a limited period of 4 years, we moved from 0% market share to now close to 10% market share

CULTURE.rationale: Same CEO (Sreekanth Nadella) and CFO (Vivek Mathur) through all 17 calls; the FY2021-stated strategy of getting non-MF revenue toward 50% was tracked publicly and reached ~40% by Jul-2026, and the NPS breakeven promised for years was delivered and then sustained at ~15% EBITDA. Bad news is disclosed promptly and specifically — equity AUM share erosion, margin compression from Ascent, tepid Issuer Solutions, folio erosion — alongside a net-cash balance sheet.
CULTURE.quote: four years back, when this strategy was unveiled, there was a fair amount of skepticism... but lo and behold, in a matter of four years, a near 40% of the revenue comes from businesses which are beyond

MOATTEST.rationale: A new entrant would need a SEBI RTA/CRA licence, mission-critical record-keeping systems for ~225 million folios and 10,500 corporate clients, and would have to persuade AMCs to undertake 2-3 quarter migrations of their entire investor book — barriers that have produced a stable duopoly for decades, plus scarce credentials like being the ninth firm globally on BlackRock's Aladdin administrator panel.
MOATTEST.quote: to sign with BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager to be in their list of marquee fund administrator, only eight, and we are the ninth one across the globe

RECURRING.rationale: Nothing in any of the 17 calls describes licence fees, AMC/service contracts, subscriptions, attach rates, renewals or deferred revenue as a funding source; the discussion is entirely occupancy, ARPOB, ARPP and payer mix.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Growth is repeatedly attributed to onboarding and retaining consultants rather than end-patient marketing — Sunshine's ramp-up depended on attracting clinical talent (Aug 2022), Telangana's FY24 miss was blamed on delayed senior-doctor hiring, and doctors are even offered equity in projects (May 2026) — but the payer is increasingly an insurer/state scheme negotiating price hard, which cuts against the low-price-sensitivity leg of the pattern.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: There has been some delay in hiring in the Telangana cluster because a lot of these hirings are towards senior doctors

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification/standards, magic-ingredient or tiny-share-of-customer-cost economics appear; NABH accreditation is discussed only as an operational box, not as a moat.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management consistently frames capital and operating frugality — minimising operational capex by keeping unstaffed beds closed, low per-bed investment in tier-2 AP, acquisitions 'at a very lucrative valuation' — producing sector-leading ~30% mature-unit EBITDA at ARPOBs well below metro peers, but there is no explicit low-price-to-customer positioning and no itemised cost programme.
LOWPRICE.quote: All the expansion and acquisition were done in a very prudent manner and at a very lucrative valuation which is reflected in the industry leading EBITDA margin and ROC

PRICING.rationale: ARPOB/ARPP rise every year (ARPOB +12.1% in Q4FY24, +20.5% in Q3FY26, +14% for FY26) and annual price hikes are an acknowledged routine, but management itself attributes most of the lift to case mix, geography mix and shorter ALOS, and admits insurers push back hard on rates during empanelment.
PRICING.quote: it's a little bit of everything, case mix, pricing and the payer mix

BRAND.rationale: The KIMS name is clearly portable — Sunshine was rebranded to KIMS within a week of control and management says the brand is building in Maharashtra — plus 20-year heritage and heavy awareness campaigns, but there is no evidence of brand-driven premium pricing; new units still stall until insurers empanel them.
BRAND.quote: in the entire Maharashtra, the KIMS brand is also putting up

INNOVATION.rationale: Each year brings named clinical/technology firsts with real ARPOB impact — first-in-India AR+AI brain surgery (FY24), Tulsa Pro, MRgFUS, South India's first Gamma Knife, 500+ robotic surgeries in 2025 — but this is technology adoption and clinical programme building, not disclosed R&D spend or a share of industry R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: Launch of India's first Tulsa Pro for Prostate Cancer care treatment

FORWARD.rationale: The calls are silent on the forward-integration constructs of the pattern — no franchising, licensing, own-store economics or D2C channel build-out; asset structures discussed (lease, revenue share, O&M) are property arrangements, not channel integration.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Footprint has expanded from ~3,600 beds in two states (2022) to 25 hospitals across 5 states with 7 launches in 2025 and FY26 revenue +28.2%, but no explicit market-share figures are ever cited, and the core Telangana cluster is conceded to be mature at high-single-digit growth against heavy competitor bed addition.
SHAREGAIN.quote: just having mature hospitals to grow at a double-digit number from that cluster will be difficult

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-family leadership (Bhaskar Rao and Abhinay Bollineni) has been stable across all 17 calls and several promises were delivered — Sunshine margin convergence, Nagpur turning EBITDA-positive as guided — and management owns misses candidly on empanelment delays; against that sit promoter share pledges, repeated CFO/chairman churn, a swing from net cash to ~INR 3,000 crore debt, and a INR 1,500 crore QIP announced within weeks of saying debt had peaked and would trend lower.
CULTURE.quote: what we underestimated is the time it takes to now get insurance empanelments vis-a-vis how it was before

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets exist — two decades of transplant and neurosurgery programmes (100 heart/lung, 430 renal transplants in 2025; 10,000+ brain tumour surgeries) and near-zero doctor attrition at Kondapur — but management's own commentary shows well-funded rivals rebuilding capacity quickly in the same micro-markets, and new KIMS units themselves ramp within a year, which is the definition of replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: close to 3,000 beds got added in the last 4 years, 5 years

RECURRING.rationale: Management repeatedly flags a services/AMC/framework/subscription layer attached to installed pumps — 110+ sites under multi-year management contracts, remote diagnostics and AR sold as subscriptions, and explicit 'recurring revenue upfront cash payments' language from Nov 2022 through FY26 — but it remains a modest, UK-concentrated slice that shrank when customer plants idled, and no attach or renewal rates are ever disclosed.
RECURRING.quote: the company scaled up the subscription platform, spare and maintenance busine ss considerably which provides scalable recurring revenue upfront cash payments

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The small-pump business runs through multi-generational dealers and distributors whom management actively protects financially ('we do not want to just push out equipment and have them have a cash flow situation and destroy their business'), and the APOEM programme is framed around dealer/distributor engagement — but the end-farmer/contractor is price-sensitive and no professional-training/prescriber lock-in is described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: These dealers are long -term dealers working with us for many generations. Some of them are with us for 4 generations.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Pumps are large capital equipment competitively tendered — orders hinge on government funding release (JJM), EIL approved-vendor lists and tender participation, and revenue is lumpy and project-dependent; nothing suggests a small-share-of-cost, non-negotiated spend.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have to choose from the approved vendor list that EIL publishes in the tender

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management positions explicitly on efficiency and premium realisation rather than low price ('we do get premiums for our orders even against multinational companies'); cost work is described as internal rationalisation and ERP-driven efficiency, not a price-passing volume model.
LOWPRICE.quote: we do get premiums for our orders even against multinational companies who don't have such products

PRICING.rationale: By May 2026 Sanjay Kirloskar claims premium realisation tied to lowest life-cycle cost and European efficiency norms, and the company enforces advances/LCs rather than discounting — but there is no discussion of regular above-inflation price increases, and margins swing with product mix and commodity prices (14.4% in Q3 FY26 vs prior-year moderation) rather than showing steady pricing-led expansion.
PRICING.quote: customers have starte d understanding lowest life cycle cost... And therefore, we do get premiums for our orders

BRAND.rationale: The Kirloskar name carries genuine Indian heritage and international recall (SPP, Rodelta), and management cites 'strong brand recall' plus a Government of India 'Appliance of the Year' recognition — but there is no sustained A&P disclosure, no market-share-plus-premium evidence across the 14 calls, and industrial demand is driven by tenders and order boards rather than brand pull.
BRAND.quote: This resilience is a clear testimony of the company's operational excellence, diversified produ ct offering and strong brand recall.

INNOVATION.rationale: The company self-funds R&D in genuinely hard areas — sodium pumps for the Fast Breeder Reactor, in-house primary heat transport pumps with India-controlled IP, AI/AR/VR service tools, new US product launches — but R&D spend is never quantified or shown growing, and there is no named-product revenue attribution or share-of-industry-R&D framing.
INNOVATION.quote: the company has developed certain pumps using its own money. So we've invested in new designs... And so the IP is controlled in India.

FORWARD.rationale: The model runs the other way — sales flow through dealers, distributors and contractors, with no own-store count, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share mentioned in any call; management explicitly declines to take government orders directly, routing them through dealers.
FORWARD.quote: we do not take any orders directly from the state government or the central government... We do this with our dealers.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Q3 FY26 offers one concrete share claim — small pumps growing 10% y/y 'compared to competition' whose growth is KUSUM-supported — and international order books grew 13-21% y/y, but across 14 calls there are almost no explicit share percentages tracked over time, and FY26 consolidated revenue grew just 1% with domestic revenue down 3%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: I think that has grown compared to competition. It has grown by 10% year -on-year.

CULTURE.rationale: Family-led with stable leadership through a public promoter dispute, management consistently owns bad news on calls (JJM shortfall quantified at Rs.50-100 crores, the foundry ERP botch quantified at ~Rs.50 crores and 700-to-200 castings/day), refuses to book unconfirmed orders or push inventory onto dealers, and delivered the multi-year margin turnaround it promised from 7.7% EBITDA in Q2 FY23 to ~13.7% in FY26.
CULTURE.quote: we place priority on cash flow, profitability and revenues in that order

MOATTEST.rationale: Some assets are genuinely hard to replicate — captive foundries, decades of nuclear/defence qualification with DAE and NPCIL, and an installed base underpinning exclusive UK water-utility framework contracts across all brands of pumps — but the core pump business faces multinationals and Indian competitors on tender, and 14 calls surface no articulated reason a funded entrant could not compete in the mainstream segments.
MOATTEST.quote: we manage the framework contracts, which is the framework contracts for most of the water companies exclusively, except Thames Water. And we manage all brands of pumps for them

RECURRING.rationale: Across the years management builds an annuity layer on top of the genset sale — Aug 2024 describes maintenance/annuity contracts on a ~15-year genset life, and by FY26 Distribution & Aftermarket is the highest-ever quarter at INR238-281 crores growing 14-20% with AMC penetration explicitly rising. No deferred-revenue/customer-advance funding is claimed, so the negative-working-capital leg is absent (receivables ~41 days, payables ~60 days).
RECURRING.quote: increasing the number of AMCs as well as ensuring adequate capability for breakdown SRMs

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: A large part of B2B revenue is specified by genset OEMs and construction OEMs rather than end customers, with an 18-month joint approval/proto-testing cycle and service channel partners being trained up; but there is no trade-training programme or professional-prescriber economics of the classic pattern.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: customer acquisition is a long-drawn process, involving technical alignment, product fit assessments and often engineering tweaks

TOLLROAD.rationale: The genset is a small share of a data centre's capex yet gates its uptime certification, and OEM engine designs-in are sticky once qualified — but management repeatedly frames the market as price-competitive rather than a rational oligopoly extracting toll-like pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: Gensets are critical for data centers for their uptime certifications or data center certifications

PRICING.rationale: Margin gains across FY26 come from mix (HHP/Optiprime), operating leverage and cost pass-through, not from price rises above inflation — gross margin has stayed flat at ~35% and management describes the industry as aggressively priced with cost leadership as one value proposition.
PRICING.quote: as this industry is marked by aggressive and dynamic pricing

BRAND.rationale: The Kirloskar name carries heritage and management prefers building the brand internationally over contract-manufacturing for Caterpillar/Generac, but no A&P spend, premium pricing or consistency promise is quantified on any call.
BRAND.quote: To become a strong brand globally, our product, channel and service processes must be fit for the market

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year — iGreen 2.0/R550 (2022), CPCB 4+ and natural-gas certification (2024), Optiprime and 2,500-3,000 kVA HHP plus a 6.3 MW nuclear genset (2026) — and four 'technology tracks' are disclosed, but R&D spend is never quantified and management declined to describe the pipeline in May 2026.
INNOVATION.quote: we are an engineering company, which also manufactures and sells, and our focus on R&D will stay

FORWARD.rationale: Movement toward the customer is via owned service/aftermarket ecosystem and 'being international' with local offices and hiring rather than exports through agents; there are no own stores, franchising or D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: Being international means building a genuine business in that geography, hiring locally, setting up comprehensive offices

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is explicit and quantified over successive calls: FY26 DG market grew 18% to ~179,000 units while KOEL grew 41% to over 50,000 units, HHP share went from negligible to approaching double digits, and international sales crossed INR1,000 crores — achieved alongside rising EBITDA margin (12.2%→13.1%), not bought with profitability.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the overall annual diesel generator market grew 18% to approximately 179,000 units, including telecom, KOEL grew by 41%

CULTURE.rationale: Family-owned with stable Kirloskar leadership through the period; the 2X-3Y ambition set in FY23 was substantially delivered and rolled into a stated 2B2B FY30 goal, bad news is disclosed (LGM margin failure and 'that is our learning', FMS degrowth, construction/mining softness, flat Arka PAT), and the balance sheet stayed net cash (INR552 crores) with capex/R&D funded organically.
CULTURE.quote: the margins were immensely under pressure... That is our learning and we have made corrective actions

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but not insurmountable barriers: one of the largest CPCB 4+ certified portfolios, 18-month OEM design-in cycles, an installed service network and defence/nuclear qualifications — yet the competitors named are Caterpillar, Cummins-class global players who already possess these, and management concedes cost leadership as a possible positioning.
MOATTEST.quote: We now boast one of the largest CPCB 4+ certified portfolios in the industry

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four calls management describes a growing O&M/aftersales annuity on an installed base of 1,000+ CNG stations, and repeatedly cites customer advances as a working-capital funding source (NWC fell from INR316cr to INR202cr in H1 FY26); but no attach rates, renewal rates or AMC revenue share are ever quantified, and a INR2cr O&M bad-debt write-off was taken in Q2 FY26.
RECURRING.quote: The O&M service business continues to grow with the installed base growing... This is on the back of strong receivable management and significant advances from the customers.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Only the Apr 2026 Zephyros go-to-market plan describes selling through specifiers rather than end customers; elsewhere KPCL sells bare-shaft compressors to OEM packagers, but there is no evidence of trade training programmes or channel-reputation lock-in across the five-year record.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Our go-to-market strategy here would really be engaging with all the stakeholders, whether that is consultants, architects, installers.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Compressors are large capex items for customers, not a sub-1% critical consumable, and the Oct 2025 call explicitly documents customers switching down to cheaper alternatives in CNG packages and boosters — the opposite of 'don't switch once converted'.
TOLLROAD.quote: there is a clear down trading in this sector where they have all gone down to cheaper products and they are acceptable to them

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost programme — backward integration into Nashik forging/foundry, solar at all plants holding power cost flat, import substitution making Zephyros 'economically cheaper' — but management explicitly refuses the low-price route, walking away from booster and screw-compressor volume rather than cutting price.
LOWPRICE.quote: We also took a measured approach in markets with lower margins like boosters and screw compressors and did not get into any price wars here.

PRICING.rationale: FY26 shows real margin expansion (raw material/sales down 3.1%, EBITDA 21.7% vs 19%) from IP-led, less-contested products and orders declined on price; but the record is mixed — Calana was shipped 'at a near zero margin' in FY25, share was lost to cheaper CNG products, and management guides margins back down to 18-20%.
PRICING.quote: If we could get an order with the margins we wanted, we took it. And if not, we let it go.

BRAND.rationale: The Kirloskar Group name and 50-year heritage carry weight in Indian industrials and support the family-succession narrative (Rahul Kirloskar as Chairman, Aman Kirloskar as MD), but the calls contain no A&P spend, no distributor leverage and no consumer-brand pricing evidence — new products win on engineering, not name.
BRAND.quote: A Kirloskar Group Company

INNOVATION.rationale: Every call names new products with revenue impact — Tezcatlipoca, Khione, Calana, Jarilo, Tyche, Janus D, Hydrino, Zephyros, the A800 frame — and the IP record compounds from 106 filings at Dec 2025 to 128 by Mar 2026 (57 filed in FY26 alone), with CII recognition and a PLI application backing it; management explicitly ties the FY26 margin expansion to 'less contested spaces based on our own IP'.
INNOVATION.quote: our highest ever IP filings of 57 for the year, taking us to over 128 IPs filed... KPCL has been awarded a top 30 IP-driven organization by CII

FORWARD.rationale: The strategic direction over the five years is explicitly backward, not forward — in-house forging, foundry, castings and precision machining at Nashik/Saswad, plus a new Precision Engineering division selling components; there are no own stores, franchises, royalties or D2C channels anywhere in the record.
FORWARD.quote: manufacture in-house as much as we can using technology as a differentiator

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Clear share gains in some lines — Tezcatlipoca crossed 100 units and became 'the industry standard', Tyche taking share from the 1,000+ imported compressors, air compressor share still only ~5% with room to run — but this is offset by admitted share loss in process gas, and FY26 revenue growth of ~12-14% fell short of the 20%+ run rate.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we seem to have lost market share in terms of the CNG packages and the boosters

CULTURE.rationale: Candour is genuine — the Oct 2025 call opens by owning 'a significant level of disappointment' and calls the process-gas misread 'our poor call judgment' — and the balance sheet is conservative (debt-free, INR460cr net cash, rising dividends, HR awards, orderly succession from K. Srinivasan to Aman Kirloskar); but the delivery-vs-promise test is weak, with the INR500cr Q2 FY26 sales target missed at INR378cr and FY26 guidance cut from 20%+ to 15% to 12-14%.
CULTURE.quote: That is our poor call judgment of what is happening in the market.

MOATTEST.rationale: There is an articulable barrier — 128 IPs, ~200 engineers, patented ammonia semi-hermetic architecture, and end-to-end in-house forging/foundry/machining that a copycat would need years and heavy capex to assemble, plus a serviced base of 1,000+ CNG stations; but the CNG down-trading episode shows the moat is not uniform and customers do defect on price where the product is undifferentiated.
MOATTEST.quote: Being in most cases, the only domestic producer end-to-end, the strong order inflow in a way reflects a better conversion ratio coming from our competitiveness.

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is entirely project-based percentage-of-completion work won through tenders, with no licence/AMC/subscription stream; the only annuity-like assets (HAM SPVs, the small Bihar toll collecting ~INR10-12 crores a quarter) are being sold off to Indus Infra Trust rather than compounded. Working capital is positive and rising (60 days in Jun-22, 78-82 days in FY26 with INR670 crores of Telangana debtors stuck), the opposite of customer-funded negative working capital.
RECURRING.quote: almost INR670 crores of debtors is pending... from government of Telangana irrigation project, where we have stuck with some of the debtors

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: There is no professional intermediary recommending KNR; work is awarded by NHAI, MoRTH and state governments through open price-competitive bidding, and across 17 calls the discussion is entirely about bid counts and L1 aggression, not channel relationships or trade training.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: almost about INR 7,000 -INR 8,000 crores we have quoted as of now, sir. Waiting for those results to come down

TOLLROAD.rationale: KNR's contract IS the customer's cost base — the road or irrigation project itself — not a tiny critical input, and clients re-tender every project rather than 'not switching once converted'. No certification, standards or oligopoly language appears; management repeatedly describes the field as crowded.
TOLLROAD.quote: below that, it's highly crowded and there is no good bid that is happening there

LOWPRICE.rationale: KNR historically positioned on above-industry margins (18.5-21.8% standalone EBITDA in FY23-FY25) and explicitly refused to chase cheap orders ('I do not have to rush and hurry for taking up an order'); when it did bid to fill an empty book, margins collapsed to 5.2-5.3% rather than being defended by a cost culture. There is no itemised cost-savings discipline on the calls — only idle-overhead complaints.
LOWPRICE.quote: the overheads are higher because the staff and equipment, everything is being maintained in the same level and the turnover has come down

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is set by competitive tender, and the trajectory is outright deflation: standalone EBITDA margin fell from 18.5% (Q1FY23) to 21.8% (Q1FY25) to 5.2% (Q3FY26), with management guiding only to 9-10% for FY27 and admitting new wins are being bid at 11-12%. Price adjustment is a pass-through clause from MoRTH, not pricing power.
PRICING.quote: I think EBITDA, if you talk about EBITDA, I'm very shameful to say that it is around 10 kind of level now we are getting

BRAND.rationale: KNR carries a genuine execution reputation — a CRISIL AA/A1+ rating reaffirmed through the downturn and larger contractors seeking it out for back-to-back subcontracting — but this reputation neither commanded premium pricing nor prevented share loss, and there is no A&P, heritage or adjacency-stretch dimension.
BRAND.quote: we are the people most wanted by the bigger contractors. I'm doing a back-to-back arrangement. Many people are there to ask me.

INNOVATION.rationale: The calls are silent on R&D spend, product pipelines or named innovations; discussion is confined to bidding, order book and execution.

FORWARD.rationale: KNR does move toward asset ownership — captive HAM SPVs generated 37-48% of the order book at times, it collects toll on the Bihar asset, and it recycles equity by selling four SPVs to Indus Infra Trust for INR1,543 crores against INR566.8 crores invested. But this is asset-ownership/monetisation, not own-stores, franchising or D2C, and the captive share is falling (16% by Dec-25).
FORWARD.quote: the company executed Share Purchase Agreement with Indus Infra Trust for the proposed sale of its 100% shareholding

SHAREGAIN.rationale: The trajectory is persistent share loss: order book fell from INR9,350 crores (Jun-22) to INR4,922 crores (Jun-24) — described by an analyst as 'critically low' — and standalone revenue fell from INR890 crores in a single quarter (Q1FY23) to INR2,097 crores for the whole of FY26. Order-inflow targets of INR6,000-8,000 crores (FY25) were repeatedly missed and rolled forward to INR10,000-12,000 crores by Sep-27.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we'll be able to achieve the target which we set forth last year, but they are not getting fulfilled in entirely last year

CULTURE.rationale: Strong on candour and conservatism — the same Executive Director (K. Jalandhar Reddy) fronts all 17 calls with CFO Haritha Varanasi since FY22, net debt/equity held at 0.41-0.66x throughout, IT-search and stuck Telangana receivables disclosed unprompted, and management owns bad news bluntly rather than spinning it. But the promise-to-delivery record is weak: order-inflow guidance was missed year after year from FY23 through FY26.
CULTURE.quote: First time, we are unable to say what we are going to do this year. That's the major thing because we are mainly depending on the works which are coming up.

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing here a funded entrant could not replicate — the same NHAI/state tenders are open to all bidders, and management's own explanation for collapsed margins is that anyone can and does bid aggressively when awarding slows. Owned equipment and a Southern-India execution base are assets, not barriers, and became a fixed-cost drag when volumes fell.
MOATTEST.quote: because the aggression in the market is very heavy here

RECURRING.rationale: The group's fee engines are genuinely recurring and prepaid-in-nature — AMC AUM/SIP flows, life insurance renewals, custody and distribution income compounding over five years — and the bank is funded by customer deposits (CASA 41-43%, cost of funds down to 4.54%), but management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates or deferred revenue as a deliberate model.
RECURRING.quote: Our SIP inflows as of September '24 grew 23% YoY to Rs.17.6 billion , a growth of 3.2 x in the last five years

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Large parts of the lending book (tractor, CV/CE, car finance via Prime, mortgages) are sourced through dealers/DSAs with upfront brokerage, and group products are pushed through bankers rather than end-customer pull — but the calls repeatedly say the end customer IS price sensitive, which is the opposite of the pattern's core claim.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: there is a higher brokerage we should pay in tractor finance, which is accounted upfront

TOLLROAD.rationale: Across all 13 calls credit is priced competitively and management repeatedly flags irrational pricing and spread compression; there is no certification, standards-body or 'tiny share of customer cost' character to the business.
TOLLROAD.quote: We continue to focus on credit substitutes to combat irrational pricing pressures

LOWPRICE.rationale: This is the classic bank variant delivered consistently from FY23 to FY26: industry-leading low-cost deposits (CASA 52.8% in FY23, still 43.3% in FY26 with CA +23% and fixed-rate SA +18%), falling cost of funds (5.01%→4.54%), cost to assets down 27bps to 2.75% while growing the balance sheet without headcount growth, and high-quality assets (GNPA 1.2%, net NPA 0.25%, credit cost 39bps).
LOWPRICE.quote: The Bank 's NIM continues to be healthy at 4.54%, supported by our low cost of funds.

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory is price deflation, not pricing power: NIM fell from a record 5.75% in Q4FY23 to 4.54-4.67% in FY26, with management citing competitive pricing pressure, price-sensitive home loans and repo pass-through it could only 'partially mitigate' via deposit costs.
PRICING.quote: The Home Loan market continues to be price sensitive

BRAND.rationale: Kotak has real trust equity — Euromoney India's Best Private Bank 2026, strong affluent brand recall, the AMC's 'most trustworthy' North Star, and a sustained group brand campaign with rising marketing spend — and stretches the name across bank, AMC, life, securities and capital; but the brand does not deliver premium pricing and did not prevent deposit-share pressure.
BRAND.quote: Brand recall for affluent segment remains very strong for Kotak.

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches appear every year with disclosed traction (FYN, ActivMoney, 811 and 811 Super, Solitaire, Air+/Cashback+ card restack, API developer portal) and tech spend is disclosed at ~13% of opex, but much of this was catch-up remediation forced by the RBI tech embargo rather than an innovation-led lead over the industry.
INNOVATION.quote: tech spend for the full year at about 13% of the total opex

FORWARD.rationale: Kotak owns its route to the customer — branches plus a digital-first 811 franchise adding 250-300k accounts a month at low acquisition cost, virtual banking, and in-house distribution of group AMC/insurance/broking products through the bank — which is real control of the customer relationship, though there is no franchising or royalty economics to point to.
FORWARD.quote: Our distribution strategy continues to deliver omni -banking experience by leveraging physical, digital, and virtual channels.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified gains in asset management (total AUM share 6.5%→7.1%, pure equity 4.5%→6.5% over five years) and top-2 tractor financing, but bank-side share was interrupted by the FY25 embargo (unsecured mix fell to 11.3%, cards frozen) and tractor share slipped to 10.9%, with CV share only ~5%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our pure equity AUM market share grew to 6.5% . Over the last five years , it has increased by two percentage points from 4.5 % to 6.5%.

CULTURE.rationale: Across the 13 calls management flags bad news early and unprompted (MFI overleveraging, credit card vintage stress, retail CV, the RBI embargo) and then delivers what it said — the 1.5-2x nominal GDP growth commitment made in Apr 2023 was still being met at 16% advances growth in FY26, guided credit-cost normalisation landed 93→79→63→39bps, and capital adequacy stayed 22-23% throughout; offset only by the embargo itself and heavy leadership turnover (Uday Kotak, Gupta, Manian, Shah all exiting).
CULTURE.quote: We said we would grow gr adually and responsibly, with the unsecured assets growing in absolute terms in the first instance. And that's exactly what we have done

MOATTEST.rationale: There are genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — a scarce Indian bank licence, a decades-built low-cost CASA base, 19 wholly owned subsidiaries, and a private bank serving ~60% of India's top 100 families — but the calls also show the moat is contestable: deposits must be bought back with propositions, lending pricing is 'irrational', and a regulator can freeze a growth engine for a year.
MOATTEST.quote: The Private Bank manages the wealth of around 60% of India's top 100 families

RECURRING.rationale: There is a genuine annuity layer — 25-year GUVNL PPAs on the IPP side and O&M/lease income of ~Rs.10 lakh per MW per year on CPP, described consistently from the Jun-2023 call ('annuity income at 325 per annum... for 25 years') through May-2026 ('strengthening the company's recurring revenue base'). But it fails the capital-light, customer-funded test: growth is funded by debt and equity capex (interest peaking near Rs.300 crores, inventory of Rs.1,400 crores), not by advances or deferred revenue.
RECURRING.quote: Our expanding IPP portfolio is expected to generate more than 390 crore units annually, strengthening the company's recurring revenue base

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Eight calls contain no discussion of intermediaries, installers, prescribers or trade training; sales are direct B2B/B2G (GUVNL, SJVN, CIL, Adani, private captive customers).
