INNOVATION.quote: The head hardened rail is still under trial

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, D2C or retail-channel economics are discussed; the only downstream move mentioned is conversion agencies and marketing RINL/NMDC third-party steel, which is not forward integration toward the end customer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Analysts explicitly flagged share loss in Nov 2024 (H1FY25 sales -6.3% while Indian consumption grew 13.5%); the FY26 recovery to 19.9 MT includes ~1 MT of resold RINL/NSL volumes, so underlying share gain is not established.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our performance is much worse. So what is the likely reason for this? Any reason why we are losing market share versus peers

CULTURE.rationale: Later years show delivery on stated goals — borrowings down INR8,150 crores in FY26, inventory down ~1 MT, cost of borrowing 7.3%→6.2%, and a balance sheet 'clean from qualifications' after decades — but earlier calls show thinning disclosure, refusal to disclose COGS, and 40 MT of aged iron-ore fines carried without write-down.
CULTURE.quote: the balance sheet of '25-'26 is totally clean from the qualifications… after a pretty long time

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuinely un-replicable assets exist — captive iron-ore mines in Odisha/Chhattisgarh/Jharkhand with ~32 MT of sub-grade fines and met-coke self-sufficiency — but these coexist with a high-cost legacy structure and commodity price-taking, so they cushion rather than confer durable advantage.
MOATTEST.quote: It is not going to impact still because we have our own capacity, which is equivalent to our requirement

RECURRING.rationale: Not a license/AMC model, but the 'follow-the-molecule' structure plus dedicated FTE contracts creates an annuity-like base: discovery/development work converts into long-duration commercial supply (34 commercial molecules, 11 in Phase III, ~155 early stage by May 2026). No discussion of deferred revenue or customer advances funding the business — in fact capex is funded by accruals and debt.
RECURRING.quote: dedicated FTE contracts with multiple pharma companies that will naturally scale up at Sai once the development stage is complete

TOLLROAD.rationale: Strong switching-cost/certification traits — 100% regulatory inspection record, 35 customer audits with zero critical observations, validation cycles of 15-18 months for an oligo molecule — and customers stay once qualified. But the toll-road economics are absent: pharma buys on open-book pricing, so Sai does not price as an unnegotiated supplier.
TOLLROAD.quote: 35 customer audits and 3 regulatory audits... with zero data integrity deviations and zero critical observations

LOWPRICE.rationale: India cost arbitrage plus explicit cost/productivity culture — global consulting firms benchmarking cost and productivity, an AI-first automation roadmap, and 450bps of employee-cost operating leverage in 9M FY26 — but this is a science-led premium-service positioning, not a no-frills low-price model.
LOWPRICE.quote: India is set to emerge as a major player... with the ability to match China's scale while maintaining the cost efficiencies

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly describes open-book pricing with pharma that caps margins at 25-30%, and on the May 2026 call said cost inflation recovery from customers 'may not always be contemporaneous' — margin gains came from operating leverage and mix, not price increases.
PRICING.quote: with pharma generally there's an open-book pricing... the margins tend to remain between the 25% to 30%

BRAND.rationale: Reputation-as-brand in a B2B setting — founded 1999, works with 19 of the top 25 global pharma, unblemished regulatory record, and management attributes wins to 15-year trust — but there is no heritage/A&P/distribution brand machinery, and no premium pricing follows from it.
BRAND.quote: these are really coming from years of trust building exercise and when you come into India you choose a partner obviously, you're going to pick one you have a long history with

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent capability investment named call-by-call — flow chemistry at commercial scale, ADC linker chemistry, phosphoramidite oligo validation, peptide pilot plant, AI retrosynthesis, with 25% of the FY27 INR1,100-1,300cr capex to capability/AI. But R&D is customer-funded service work, not proprietary: no disclosed own R&D spend, no owned products.
INNOVATION.quote: As a rule, Sai will never have a standalone product by itself... We are not a product company we are a services company

FORWARD.rationale: The model runs the opposite direction — deliberately no owned products, no stores, no D2C; Sai is a contract partner sitting behind its customers' brands.
FORWARD.quote: We will only work with our customers on their custom projects. That's our specific strategy

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Repeated, quantified share gain across all six calls: large-pharma revenue share rose 28% (FY22) to 49% (FY26), top-25 pharma clients from 18 to 19, commercial molecules 31 to 34 with 7 added to late-stage/commercial in FY26, and FY26 revenue +29% while peers were hit by destocking — growth funded by capex, not by discounting or credit.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The revenue contribution from our 19 pharma clients went up from 28% FY22 to 49% this FY26

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in Feb 2025 (28-30% EBITDA, 15-20% CAGR, debt repayment from IPO proceeds, 100KL capacity adds) were delivered and beaten by FY26 (30% EBITDA 'ahead of schedule'), yet guidance was not opportunistically raised; management repeatedly warns on lumpiness, admits it can be 'blindsided' by customer destocking, and calls out the consulting spend as a one-off. Founder-rooted, stable Kanumuri/Chittor leadership since IPO.
CULTURE.quote: CDMOs as an entity do not control stocking or destocking. We probably get to know it at the time when it actually happens and kind of lot of times get blindsided

MOATTEST.rationale: Articulable barriers exist — 15-year multi-service relationships, regulatory qualification embedded in customers' filings, an unblemished inspection record, and integrated discovery-to-commercial breadth that management says few Indian peers offer — but capacity, talent and technology are fundable by well-capitalised rivals (Sai itself is adding 70% capacity), and the moat is relationship-based rather than structurally un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: For customers looking purely for commercial work, they may have multiple options. But for development-plus-commercial, we are probably ahead of the curve

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 13 calls revenue is transactional room-nights measured by RevPAR/ARR/occupancy, repriced daily; there is no discussion of licence fees, AMCs, renewal rates, attach rates or deferred revenue/customer advances funding the business — in fact SAMHI pays fees to brand owners rather than collecting them.
RECURRING.quote: our ability to reprice hotels on a daily basis 3 times a day is very, very strong

TOLLROAD.rationale: Hotel spend is discretionary and highly event-sensitive: management quantifies four separate one-off shocks (India-Pakistan conflict, monsoon, December airline crisis, Middle East conflict) cutting FY26 revenue by INR 45-52 crores, the opposite of a critical, un-negotiated micro-cost.
TOLLROAD.quote: These onetime events compressed our full year revenue by approximately INR 45 crores to INR 52 crores

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost/capital-cost culture — buying underperforming assets at a discount to replacement cost, mid-teens ROCE guardrails, fixing the ACIC cost structure to lift margins from 32% to ~40%, and a no-frills mid-scale (Holiday Inn Express) core — but the model is asset-heavy with low asset turns, not the high-turn scale economics of Low Price Plus.
LOWPRICE.quote: We want to maintain discipline of discount-to-replacement cost. We want to maintain the discipline of underwriting mid-teens ROCE.

PRICING.rationale: Repeated across FY24-FY26: same-store RevPAR up 14-16% for many consecutive quarters with occupancy flat (Q3 FY26 ADR +15.9%, occupancy 73%), rebranded assets repricing 2x (Greater Noida, Trinity Bangalore INR 5,900 to INR 8,000-10,000), and GST loss-of-ITC being passed through in corporate renegotiations; caveat is that this is cycle- and supply-driven rather than brand-owned.
PRICING.quote: hotels, which have an average rate of INR 13,000 are already priced for INR 20,000 in the month of February

BRAND.rationale: SAMHI owns no consumer brand — it licenses Marriott, IHG and Hyatt brands and even moved ACIC from Marriott franchise to Marriott managed, so the heritage, A&P and loyalty distribution sit with the operators; SAMHI's identity to investors is 'smart hotel investments', not a consumer promise.
BRAND.quote: we have been able to leverage the power of strong global hotel brands which sit on top of our hotels... these brands are a bridge to the customer

INNOVATION.rationale: The only innovation asset disclosed is the proprietary SAMHI Intel asset-management analytics tool (Nov 2023) used for demand-compression yield insights; there is no disclosed R&D spend, product pipeline or named annual launches driving pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: our in-house and proprietary asset management tool that we've built, which we call SAMHI Intel

FORWARD.rationale: SAMHI moves away from the customer, not toward them — it hands operations and distribution to Marriott/IHG/Hyatt, converting ACIC from franchise to fully managed, and has no owned-brand D2C channel; the RARE India stake is a platform investment rather than forward integration of its own product.
FORWARD.quote: completing the transition from "Marriott Franchise" to "Marriott Managed"

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Real inventory-led share gain — third-largest room owner in India within 12 years, dominant share of specific brand systems (71% of India's Holiday Inn Express, >40% of Fairfield), 4,800 to 4,900 operational rooms with 1,900 more under development toward INR 3,000 crores revenue by 2030 — but the gain is bought with acquisitions and capital (GIC, Ingka leases) rather than shown as persistent competitive share numbers against named rivals.
SHAREGAIN.quote: about 71% of all Holiday Inn Express hotels in India were owned by SAMHI

CULTURE.rationale: The multi-year record shows promises kept and bad news disclosed early and quantified: the FY24 pledge to cut net debt/EBITDA from 8.7x to ~3.5x was met and beaten (3.0x by FY26), FY26 guidance of 9-11% revenue growth delivered at 12.3%, and management itemised the GST hit (INR 14 crores), FF&E charges and each disruption rather than burying them; long-tenured professional team (8-10 years), ~50% independent board, and explicit ROCE/replacement-cost guardrails.
CULTURE.quote: we set 2 specific commitments to our shareholders... Despite revenue disruptions and active future growth, we have delivered both

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real barriers — scarce prime micro-market sites (HITEC City, Whitefield, Navi Mumbai), long and litigious development cycles, and a 12-year proprietary sourcing/turnaround track record buying below replacement cost — but the assets themselves are replicable by any well-funded buyer, and SAMHI's own strategy proves hotels can be bought and repositioned within a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: We want to maintain the discipline of not investing in long-lead greenfield assets

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is contradicted: funding is expensive and rating-dependent (8.5% on co-lent book, 9.5% on-balance-sheet in Aug 2024), and management admits it cannot profitably hold prime loans, so it originates-to-sell; the 'lowest cost of funds' is still an aspiration handed to it by IHC's Mar 2026 capital and the subsequent CRISIL/CARE/ICRA upgrades, not a self-built cost culture.
LOWPRICE.quote: For an NBFC to long-term hold loans, which are, let's say, 8% to 9.5%, even 10% on its balance sheet is not really very RoE accretive

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is pure floating-rate pass-through of RBI repo moves (Aug 2022 call: +140bps retail, +160bps wholesale), and the May 2026 product grid shows yields set by segment competition (8.5-10% prime, 11-13.5% affordable) rather than any ability to price above the market; the company is a price-taker whose spread depends on its own borrowing cost.
PRICING.quote: over 99% of our advances are o[n] floating rate basis, wherein we pass on the rate increase almost instantaneously

BRAND.rationale: Heritage was actively discarded rather than compounded — Indiabulls was rebranded to Sammaan in 2024 and the Indiabulls brand name was later sold back to the ex-promoter to distance the company from the PIL; the 'Sammaan' brand is a reputational reset, and lenders/rating agencies were won by IHC's capital, not by brand equity.
BRAND.quote: The company has also from a materiality of distancing itself, even sold the brand name Indiabulls back to Mr. Gehlaut companies.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: The trajectory is contraction, not share gain: AUM fell from Rs.73,047 crore (Jun 2022) to Rs.44,000 crore growth AUM (Dec 2025) and Rs.53,160 crore total (Mar 2026), while the Aug 2024 promise of Rs.1 trillion retail AUM and Rs.5,000 crore quarterly disbursals by FY27 was never approached — disbursals were still only Rs.3,115 crore in Q1FY25 and co-lending restarted from a low base in Jan 2026.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the target of Rs. 1,00,000 crore or Rs. 1 trillion of retail AUM by Fiscal '27

CULTURE.rationale: Genuine positives — a stable long-tenured team (Banga since the Indiabulls era), the delivered deleveraging of ~Rs.1.3 lakh crore net since 2018, pre-funded FCCB/ECB repayments, and full disclosure of the PIL — sit against repeatedly missed promises (FY23 'Rs.15,000 crore disbursals', FY27 Rs.1 trillion AUM and mid-teens ROE), a Rs.2,132 crore consolidated 9M loss in FY25, and presentation NPAs shown on AUM (2.68%) versus 3.4% in the statutory filing.
CULTURE.quote: the management team has stood together. And now the management team has seen cycles, learned from our mistakes

MOATTEST.rationale: Management's claimed moat — the sold-down Rs.1.03 lakh crore pool with 0.54% 90+ DPD across 24 bank relationships — is an origination-and-distribution track record any well-capitalised lender can rebuild; the company's own survival depended on external rescue capital (IHC's $1bn, Mar 2026) and the ratings upgrades that followed within 50 days, which is the opposite of an un-replicable barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: This is a brilliant moat that the company has created for itself.

RECURRING.rationale: The call describes one-off branded OTC/Rx product sales through pharmacies; no licence fees, subscriptions, AMC/service contracts, deferred revenue or customer advances are discussed anywhere.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is initiated by doctors and pharmacists who recommend while the patient pays — the entire growth plan's first lever is doubling face-to-face HCP reach with a 350-strong medical rep force targeting paediatricians, allergologists and chest physicians, plus pharmacist education at point of sale; post-recall recovery was credited to HCP loyalty.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: all four brands in the portfolio today are spoken to with the HCPs... So, we plan to double our doctor reach face to face

TOLLROAD.rationale: No discussion of being a small-but-critical input to a customer's cost base, certification/standards anchoring, or oligopoly dynamics; this is a consumer-facing branded healthcare business.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost culture is not a theme — the narrative is about raising A&P from low single digit to mid-teens and increasing investment, with only a passing mention of a lean supply chain; no itemised savings or price-led volume strategy.

PRICING.rationale: No price increases, elasticity, premiumisation or realisation discussion at all; growth is framed entirely as volume, penetration and category expansion, and management declined forward-looking commentary.

BRAND.rationale: Heritage brands hold top-five positions in their categories with essentially no advertising support for years — Combiflam stayed top-five despite 15 years of no HCP or consumer investment, Avil is the volume leader — and management is now stepping A&P up to mid-teens plus stretching into adjacencies (Allegra D, Combiflam cream).
BRAND.quote: we had not gone to the HCPs to speak about Combiflam for the last 15 years and still continued to be amongst the top five brands

INNOVATION.rationale: One named launch (Allegra D, a vacant-space pseudoephedrine formulation) and access to Opella's global R&D network plus an in-house team, but management gave no R&D spend, no quantified pipeline and no share-of-industry-R&D evidence when explicitly pressed by Nippon on quantifying the effort.
INNOVATION.quote: there was no brand for congestion out there with the pseudoephedrine formulation... which is why we launched Allegra D last year

FORWARD.rationale: Some movement toward the customer — direct retail coverage to be doubled for control over stores and range selling, plus e-commerce/modern trade listings — but these remain single-digit contributors and there are no own stores, franchising or D2C economics discussed.
FORWARD.quote: We have started work on e-commerce and modern trade, but it's still in single digit in terms of contribution to the business

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Market share is an explicit leadership KPI and management commits to growing faster than the market, but the recent record is share recovery after a year of recalls rather than persistent gain — FY25 domestic growth of 22% falls to 11% ex-recall, and no share numbers were disclosed.
SHAREGAIN.quote: it's top line, market share, bottom line... by market share, it's very clear we'll have to grow faster than the market

CULTURE.rationale: Management openly owned the product recalls and their year-long share loss, put quality ahead of sales, and cited B-Corp certification and a KPI-driven culture — but this is a two-year-old demerged entity with a brand-new leadership team, so there is no multi-year record of promises made in old calls being delivered in later ones.
CULTURE.quote: we had some unfortunate recalls that we did in abundant caution because for us it was very important that quality remains paramount

MOATTEST.rationale: The strongest replicate barrier articulated is decades-old brand recall built without spend — Avil recognised across the Heartland, Combiflam top-five after 15 years of neglect, so management says it need not build awareness — but no capital, data or location barrier is claimed, and the recall episode showed rivals could take shelf space within a year.
MOATTEST.quote: we don't need to build brand awareness to that extent, I think it's really about just reminding people about the strength that we have

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four sampled calls (Aug 2022–May 2026) management discusses order books, peak annual revenues and lifetime backlogs — never licence fees, AMC/service revenue, attach rates, renewals or customer advances as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sansera sells direct to OEMs (Tata Motors, Force Motors, Volvo, Toyota Industries, Saab, Triumph); no intermediary professional, installer or prescriber channel is mentioned in any call.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Con-rods, crankshafts and aerospace/semicon parts are small-value but functionally critical, and entry requires long validation/FAI and certification cycles that lock in an approved supplier — but management never claims customers pay without negotiating, and pricing is clearly negotiated with OEMs.
TOLLROAD.quote: mass production of this facility is expected to start from FY24 because we need to go through a lot of validation and certification process

LOWPRICE.rationale: The Aug 2022 call frames India's ancillary edge as quality plus 'clear cut price advantages' under China+1, and the CFO itemises cost initiatives (renewable packaging, logistics consolidation, 80% renewable energy at Bangalore); later calls lean on operating leverage and mix rather than a deep, hard-to-copy cost culture.
LOWPRICE.quote: appreciated for their work in the area of component development, consistent quality and clear cut price advantages

PRICING.rationale: Margin gains across FY23–FY26 come from product mix, operating leverage and capacity utilisation, never from price; commodity increases must be negotiated customer-by-customer and one export price rise was explicitly outside contract, and Q4 FY26 flags inflation in steel, aluminium, energy and freight as a pressure to absorb.
PRICING.quote: we were able to secure a price increase though it was not part of the standard contract

BRAND.rationale: No consumer or heritage brand exists; beyond supplier awards from Toyota Industries there is no A&P spend, premium pricing or adjacency-under-one-name discussion in any call.

INNOVATION.rationale: Capability investment is real and recurring — 4,000-ton press, aluminium forging, 5-axis machining up to 4–5 metre parts, MMRFIC radar stake — but it is capex- and process-led, with no disclosed R&D spend, no named-product revenue impact and gross margins around 40% rather than innovation-grade.
INNOVATION.quote: From earlier, it used to be limited to 1.5 meters was the maximum component size we could handle. Now we can handle up to 4 meters, 5-axis machining

FORWARD.rationale: Sansera is a pure B2B tier-1 supplier across all 16 calls; expansion is plants (Pantnagar, Bidadi, ADS facility, a possible US unit) and a Nichidai JV, with no stores, franchising, licensing or D2C anywhere.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Consistent wallet-share and content-per-vehicle gains are claimed from FY23 to FY26 — new customers (Tata, Force, Saab, Triumph), 2W crankshaft outsourcing, ADS revenue up 155% in FY26 — but gains are described as customer share-of-business rather than measured industry share, and the North American EV customer fell 50% while new order booking went soft in Q4 FY26.
SHAREGAIN.quote: more than 60% of Indian automotive 2-wheeler industry still manufactures these crankshaft assemblies in-house. There is an interest shown by all of them to gradually outsource

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable (Preetham and CFO Vikas Goel through the whole period), bad news is disclosed promptly (the ~INR3,000cr North American contract withdrawal, the Sweden/Volvo lean patch, the deliberate pause in tech-agnostic orders), FY26 delivered the ADS guidance and improved ROCE to 18% with debt reduced; but the FY23 promise of 40% non-auto/tech-agnostic within three years was only ~30% by FY26 and the 20% EBITDA goal is still unmet.
CULTURE.quote: we have taken a pause in taking the newer orders... There is a very clear decision that we had taken, which I had also communicated in my previous calls

MOATTEST.rationale: There are articulable barriers — integrated forging plus surface-treatment technology, heavy capital, and multi-year OEM/aerospace qualification — and management argues aluminium forging is not open to anyone with capital; but it remains a contested precision-forging industry where a funded entrant with time can qualify, and management itself expects competitors to enter.
MOATTEST.quote: I don't think this is that much easy and straightforward that anybody with capital investment can get into this... But over time, I am sure that you will see many players looking at the thing

RECURRING.rationale: Nothing across the 18 calls describes recurring licence/AMC/subscription revenue or customer advances funding the business; Sapphire is a franchisee that pays royalties out rather than collecting a recurring stream.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is driven entirely by direct consumer marketing and value offers (INR 99 burger meal plus advertising, BOGO buckets, aggregator ratings on Swiggy/Zomato), with no professional/prescriber channel or trade training anywhere in the record.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: it's a combination of advertising and this everyday value that is driving change of consumer behavior

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification, standards, or critical-small-input economics discussed; if anything Sapphire is the customer being cross-subsidised by its own suppliers, not a toll collector.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Consistent cost-efficiency culture across all years — Q1FY23 delivered record restaurant EBITDA despite gross-margin compression via 'cost efficiency programs', and FY26 held gross margin while rolling out a permanent INR 99 value layer — but returns are unimpressive (adjusted EBITDA 7.6% FY26, Pizza Hut at -3.3%), so scale-driven high-turn economics are not demonstrated.
LOWPRICE.quote: our overall cost efficiency programs enabled us to deliver amongst our best ever restaurant EBITDA

PRICING.rationale: The record shows the opposite of pricing power: price increases repeatedly lag inflation (9% vs mid-teens in FY23), 2.5 years of negative SSSG, and the FY26 recovery was bought with a permanent value layer, BOGO offers and vendor cross-subsidy rather than price.
PRICING.quote: our price increase was 9% while inflation was well into double digits into mid-teens

BRAND.rationale: KFC is genuinely powerful (Sri Lanka is the No.1 QSR with steady share consolidation, and management says they win 'really, really strong' in direct competitive fights), but the brands are licensed from Yum! rather than owned, Pizza Hut has posted negative SSSG for most of FY24–FY26, and premium pricing is absent.
BRAND.quote: we continue to retain and consolidate our number 1 QSR position in the country

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches appear every year with revenue commentary — Flavour Fun pizzas (FY23), Melts and Momo Mia (FY25), Dunked, ShaWOWrma and Double Chicken Dynamite (FY26), plus digital kiosks in 73–75% of stores — but there is no disclosed R&D spend, and management deliberately limits innovation pace; it has not translated into pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Typically we used to run 3 to 4 innovations in a year. We have upped our innovation intensity.

FORWARD.rationale: Sapphire sits on the wrong side of this pattern: it is the franchisee funding Yum!'s growth with its own capex (1,074 own-operated stores), pays royalties out, sub-franchises nothing, and its store plans are set 'with Yum! on a calendar year basis'.
FORWARD.quote: that's how we operate with Yum! in terms of store expansion plans

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Sri Lanka shows durable share leadership and six consecutive quarters of double-digit SSSG, and KFC India doubled its store count from Dec-21 to Dec-24 as promised; but India same-store sales were negative for roughly ten quarters and Pizza Hut ceded ground to a more aggressive Domino's, so system growth came from new stores rather than winning share.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we would double the count by December 24, and we should be close to 500, so that's on track

CULTURE.rationale: Purohit and Jain have fronted every one of the 18 calls since FY22; bad news is disclosed promptly and without spin (Maldives impairment taken in Q2FY25, Pizza Hut losses called out quarter after quarter, 'it has taken us time to find the right marketing mix'), guidance given in Dec-21 was delivered by Dec-24, and management refuses to chase M&A or store growth without meeting stated criteria.
CULTURE.quote: we were not getting positive SSSG... We tried various campaigns, but things were not clicking.

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real barriers — exclusive Yum! territory rights, six years of waiting for the Phoenix Palladium site, and a 1,000+ store operating base a newcomer cannot rebuild quickly — but the brands are contractual, not owned (Yum! is selling Pizza Hut globally), and fried-chicken/pizza competitors demonstrably entered and pressured SSSG.
MOATTEST.quote: they were unable to find a space for us to six years

RECURRING.rationale: No product-plus-service recurring stream exists (no attach rates, AMC, renewals or customer advances anywhere in 15 calls), but the energy pivot has built genuine long-duration contracted revenue: a 40-year PPA for Rehar hydro at INR7.42/unit, and in Feb 2026 200MW medium-term plus 100MW long-term IPP offtake described as 'providing stability to cash flows'.
RECURRING.quote: supplying power to Chhattisgarh Power Distribution Company Limited under 40 -year long-term power sale arrangement at fixed generic tariff

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The calls are entirely about commodity tonnage, prices and clearances; no professional, installer or prescriber channel is ever mentioned.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Ferro alloys and pellets could superficially look like 'magic ingredients', but management repeatedly describes oversupply, price corrections and switching between domestic and export markets purely for realisation — the opposite of an unnegotiated toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: Ferro alloys prices may also remain subdued due to oversupply on account of fall in global steel production and capacity additions.

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a consistent, itemised cost-obsession across all years — captive coal and washery, captive power, solar, energy-efficient TG sets, railway siding for cheaper coal movement, and diverting captive power to merchant sale when steel margins are thin — but this is commodity cost insulation, not low price paired with differentiation or scale advantage.
LOWPRICE.quote: we expect the coal prices to be down by about INR200 to INR250 per metric ton. So, we should be able to save about 15 paisa per unit of the power cost.

PRICING.rationale: The company is an explicit price taker across steel, ferro alloys, pellets and merchant power; every quarter's result is explained by realisations moving with the cycle, and Q3 FY26 saw steel at five-year lows and IEX power at INR3.33 vs INR3.79.
PRICING.quote: steel also touched 5-year low prices

BRAND.rationale: No brand, A&P spend, heritage narrative or consumer-facing positioning appears anywhere in the transcripts.

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or named new product is ever disclosed; capex discussion is capacity and efficiency (TG sets, solar), not innovation.

FORWARD.rationale: Asked directly in Nov 2025 whether the group would forward-integrate to escape steel cyclicality, management said there is no immediate focus and that further expansion would likely be in power/hydro assets instead — sales remain B2B commodity offtake with no own stores, D2C or franchising.
FORWARD.quote: we've had the brainstorming, which is always ongoing as a process in the group. And right now, we don't have any immediate focus.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Market-share data cited on the calls is always India's share of global steel production, never Sarda's share versus named competitors; the company's own share is never quantified in any of the 15 calls.

CULTURE.rationale: Across FY23–FY26 the same family/CFO team promised and then delivered: Vizag third furnace ahead of schedule (Aug 2022), Rehar hydro commissioned July 2025 as guided, record production of coal/pellet/ferro alloys/power, ratings upgraded CRISIL A+ → AA- and outlook to Positive, and net debt cut from ~INR1,500cr to under INR500cr while funding capex from accruals; they also provided prudently for the disputed CSPDCL transmission charge rather than deferring it, and refuse to give guidance in a cyclical industry.
CULTURE.quote: Consolidated net debt as of 31st December 2025 was below INR500 crores, significantly reduced from approximately INR1,500 crores as of 31st March 2025.

MOATTEST.rationale: The energy/mining side has real time-based barriers — six coal blocks won at auction, hydro sites with 40-year PPAs, and clearances management says take a minimum of two years plus forest clearance — but the steel, pellet and ferro alloy assets are conventional secondary capacity a funded entrant can rebuild, as management itself notes secondary players keep expanding.
MOATTEST.quote: it will take minimum two years because forest clearance also is there apart from EC

RECURRING.rationale: Licensing is an annuity off an owned catalogue — management repeatedly guides to a 5-year payback followed by '55 to 75 years' of returns, with fixed-fee and minimum-guarantee platform deals that renegotiate upward, and events funded by ticketing-partner advances; but there is no attach-rate/AMC/renewal-rate or deferred-revenue disclosure, and Carvaan (the product-upfront leg) is being deliberately shrunk.
RECURRING.quote: whatever you spend today across all languages, in a maximum of 5 years we will get our money back, and then we have anything between 55 to 75 years to make money from that content

TOLLROAD.rationale: Music IP is a critical, non-substitutable input to every streaming platform and Saregama is deliberately un-dependent on any single buyer ('we have very consciously worked in a fashion that there is no overdependence on any one player'), with the catalogue framed as an inflation-linked infrastructure asset; but content is the largest, not a <1-2%, cost line for its customers, so the classic toll-road economics only partly apply.
TOLLROAD.quote: Music catalogue globally is increasingly being treated as an infrastructure-like inflation-linked asset

PRICING.rationale: Pricing power is largely derivative — realisation rises as platforms push free users behind paywalls and raise their own subscription prices (Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls on the free-to-paid transition, India at <3% paid penetration), plus upward renegotiation of minimum guarantees noted in Aug 2022; Saregama does not itself raise a price list, and per-stream realisation was described as a fixed ~Rs 0.10.
PRICING.quote: its value keeps on going up as platforms keep on increasing their own subscription prices

BRAND.rationale: Genuine heritage (the Lata/Kishore-era catalogue, 'the richest IP catalogue' in India) and name-stretch into adjacencies — Carvaan, Carvaan Live, Yoodlee, the UN40 festival — but the brand does not command consumer premium pricing; monetisation runs through platforms and artists rather than the Saregama masterbrand.
BRAND.quote: a company which not only thrives on the richest IP catalogue that it owns but is also a company, which is building the IP for tomorrow

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D line is disclosed, but there is a repeatable innovation culture in the operating model: data mining and predictive modelling to price content acquisitions (Aug 2022), GenAI video tools cutting catalogue-video turnaround from 10-15 days to under 3 (Feb 2026), and a dedicated AI efficiency team (May 2026); the innovation is process-side, not margin-funded product R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: use of generative AI video generation tools for these older songs has helped us drastically reduce both time and cost

FORWARD.rationale: Saregama does own the direct channel in places — its own YouTube channels, Carvaan sold D2C, live events and now brand partnerships selling straight to consumers and advertisers — but it is retreating from physical retail (Aug 2024 exit from individual stores) and its big 2026 move, the Bhansali Productions stake, is integration backwards into content supply, not forward to the customer.
FORWARD.quote: by going directly to the customers, which we do by selling a Carvaan or a live event

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share ambition is explicit and quantified across the whole period — 'no. 2 label to the no. 1 label', a stated goal of 25-30% of all new Indian music releases, no.1 in Bhojpuri/Gujarati (Aug 2022), leadership in Haryanvi via the Nav deal, artists managed rising 150→270→300+ — and it is share bought with discipline, not price, as shown by refusing Dhurandhar 2 on payback grounds.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the acquisition team stood its ground and refused to buy the album because of the pricing

CULTURE.rationale: Strong candour and stability — Vikram Mehra MD and Pankaj Chaturvedi CFO throughout, public admission that the Punjabi strategy 'never worked out' twice, Pocket Aces breakeven promised in Aug 2024 and delivered in FY26, and an on-call commitment to add rolling-12-month disclosure after an analyst challenged the narrative; offset by the Aug 2024 promise of 30% ex-Carvaan CAGR and doubled PBT being quietly reset to 20-23%, and by the 2022 extension of content useful life from 6 to 10 years that flattered PAT.
CULTURE.quote: I'll be honest and confess that our strategy never worked out

MOATTEST.rationale: The 180,000-song catalogue accumulated since 1946 is the clearest un-replicable asset in the evidence — no funded entrant can re-record the Lata/Kishore-era masters — and management argues AI raises rather than lowers the value of authenticated human-created music with provenance; the newer content book (~5,500 releases a year, Bhansali exclusivity for A/B+ Hindi albums) extends the same time-based barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: 180,000 song catalogue growing at 5,500 new releases per year, is exactly the kind of asset that compounds value over decades

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all calls SBFC originates in-house through its own branches and salespeople rather than via DSAs, brokers or professional intermediaries; the Jul 2026 call explicitly restates the direct model and the Sep 2023 call describes in-house origination where 'the salesperson goes visits the customer'.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We are largely a direct model, we will continue to be a direct model in all the states that we operate in.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Management itself frames the business as an undifferentiated commodity where the firm cannot dictate terms, the opposite of a toll-road supplier; the Jul 2026 call also notes competitors 'showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts' forcing SBFC to walk away from business.
TOLLROAD.quote: Lending is a commodity business, and we are all price takers, not price setters.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The cost culture is real and itemised — opex/AUM cut from 5.42% (Q1FY24) to 3.93% (Q4FY26), a cumulative 161bps against 150bps promised, plus a 48-83bps cut in cost of funds — but SBFC lends at ~17.6-17.9% yields, so it competes on availability and cost structure, not on low price to the customer.
LOWPRICE.quote: the lowest cost producer wins... against the 150 basis points promised, we delivered a 161-basis point reduction

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly denies pricing headroom — in Jan 2025 Dayani said MSME yields 'will be largely stable... no opportunity to increase', and by FY27 yields were down 9bps Y-o-Y with the stated goal being to defend a 9% spread via lower funding cost, not higher prices.
PRICING.quote: I do not think that there's opportunity to increase or inch it up beyond from what we are already charging.

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, product pipeline or named annual launches in any call; asked directly in Jul 2026 whether new products were needed for the INR 10,000cr-to-20,000cr journey, Dhru declined, and technology investment is process digitisation (LOS, multilingual PD app, branch risk-rating) rather than innovation-led differentiation.
INNOVATION.quote: we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new. We will continue doing what we are doing.

FORWARD.rationale: SBFC owns its entire distribution — 162 branches in Sep 2023 growing to 256 by Jun 2026, with direct customer contact deliberately non-digitised — which gives control of origination and pricing, but this is standard NBFC branch banking rather than a manufacturer capturing downstream margin, and ~20% of book runs through an ICICI co-origination partnership.
FORWARD.quote: What doesn't move digitally is ensuring that the personal discussion with the customer or originating the customer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: AUM compounded from INR 5,327cr (Jun 2023) to INR 11,922cr (Jun 2026) at 27-30% Y-o-Y with share gain explicitly targeted in FY27, and the gains look clean — screens were tightened, login-to-disbursal fell 42%→34%, and they walked away from business rather than chase it — but no explicit market-share percentages versus named competitors are ever given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: you will see us now growing a lot more in geographies and taking significant market share in some of these states

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance given at the 2023 roadshow (5-7% QoQ growth, 50bps annual opex reduction, 80-100bps credit cost) was repeated and then measurably beaten over 12-14 calls; management flagged sector stress early ('canary in the coal mine', Apr 2024), owns mistakes openly, provisions at ~2x IRAC, runs 1.9x debt/equity with 32-33% CRAR, and executed an orderly internal succession from Dhru to Dayani.
CULTURE.quote: Cumulatively, against the 150 basis points promised, we delivered a 161-basis point reduction.

MOATTEST.rationale: There is an articulable barrier — a localised, in-house underwriting model built over 5+ years, ~250 branches across small towns where 3/4 of customers are first-time property borrowers, and now cycle-tested PD/LGD data replacing market benchmarks — but management concedes the product is a commodity and competitors regularly undercut on price, so a well-funded entrant with time could replicate the branch-and-underwriting build.
MOATTEST.quote: In our earlier stages of operations, we had to rely on market benchmarks as our data had not matured. Now that we have seen cycles play out...

RECURRING.rationale: The card is effectively an annuity — an installed base of 1.92cr (2024) to 2.26cr (Jul 2026) cards generating annual fees, spend-based interchange and interest on a 54-55% interest-earning receivable book — but management never frames it as attach/renewal rates or deferred revenue funding the business, and the funding is borrowed wholesale at 6.4-7.5% rather than customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: Interest-earning assets remained stable at around 55% and revolver rates were 22%

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Roughly half of all sourcing runs through SBI's own bank branches ('Banca', 42-46% of new accounts across the calls), where branch staff recommend the card to the bank's existing depositors rather than the customer responding to direct marketing; but there is no independent professional channel, training programme or trade-relationship investment of the classic kind.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our share from open market and banca channels in FY '26 stands at 54% and 46%, respectively

TOLLROAD.rationale: Nothing about the toll-road setup applies: cardholders hold multiple competing trade lines, switch to cheaper personal loans, and the credit product is a large, keenly-priced share of the customer's cost, not a trivial-but-critical input; the Jul 2026 call explicitly discusses NBFC consumer-durable lending cannibalising their EMI book.
TOLLROAD.quote: if he has an option of lower -priced personal loan, he will take a personal loan for that purpose

LOWPRICE.rationale: The record is the opposite of a cost-obsessed model: cost-to-income deteriorated from ~49% (Q1 FY25) to 55-58% guided (FY26/27), and as a non-bank issuer it has no deposit franchise, funding itself at 6.4-7.5% wholesale rates.
LOWPRICE.quote: we expect the cost to income to be in the range of 55% to 58% for the next year as well

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly declines to raise price — refusing to lift the revolver rate off 3.5%/month in Aug 2024 and again resisting reward cuts or a 3.75%-to-4% hike in May 2026 — while interchange is regulated and spend-based fee yield fell from ~1.6% pre-COVID to ~1.4%; earnings levers are volume and credit cost, not pricing.
PRICING.quote: we would not like to take at this point of time, take action in terms of increasing the interest rate

BRAND.rationale: It leans on SBI's parent heritage and repeated brand recognition ('Best BFSI Brands' three consecutive years, Abby/ET Brand Disruption awards, 25th anniversary) and can attract premium co-brand partners (Tata Neu, Flipkart, Indigo, PhonePe, BPCL crossing 5mn cards), but the brand delivers distribution and partner pull, not premium pricing.
BRAND.quote: our core brand BPCL SBI Card crossed the 5 million milestone

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a regular, named product cadence across the calls — Aditya Birla SBI Card (2022), SBI Card MILES (2024), Tata Neu/Flipkart/Indigo/PhonePe cards and the SBI Card Sprint digital onboarding platform plus AI/ML investment (FY26) — but no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-innovation claim, and the launches are incremental and largely partner-led rather than margin-funded proprietary innovation.
INNOVATION.quote: we launched several co-branded credit cards such as Tata Neu SBI Card, Flipkart SBI Card, Indigo SBI Card and PhonePe SBI Card

FORWARD.rationale: It has built direct-to-customer digital channels — instant issuance on YONO/Internet Banking (2024), SBI Card Sprint digital onboarding and a highly-rated app that converts spends to EMI (2026) — giving control of acquisition and experience, but this is channel digitisation, not the own-store/franchise economics the pattern describes.
FORWARD.quote: if you open our mobile app, which is very highly rated. 4.5 and 4.6 on both iOS and Play Store

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Cards-in-force share has been essentially flat over four years (18.4% in Q1 FY23, 18.5% in Q1 FY25, 18.6% in FY26/27) and spends share actually fell to 15.9% in Q1 FY25 before recovering to 19.5% by Q1 FY27 — a share recovery achieved by deliberately slowing acquisition for credit quality, so gains are real but recent and not persistent.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our spend market share has grown to 19.5% versus 18.1% in FY26

CULTURE.rationale: Management disclosed the credit-cost deterioration promptly and in detail (Aug 2024: credit cost up to 8.5%, over-leveraging diagnosed, limits cut on 5 lakh customers) and then delivered what it promised — credit cost down to 6.5% and GNPA to 2.04% by Q1 FY27, acquisition landing at 9.17 lakh against a stated 9 lakh-1mn target — but leadership is SBI-deputation-driven with three MDs and four chairmen turning over in five years, so long-tenured stewardship is absent.
CULTURE.quote: we will target acquisition of 9 lakh to 1 million for the quarter, and we have ended this quarter with around 9.17 lakhs

MOATTEST.rationale: The one genuinely hard-to-replicate asset is privileged access to SBI's branch network and depositor data, which uniquely lets it underwrite new-to-credit customers (20-30% of Banca sourcing) that open-market rivals cannot see — but the card product itself, co-brand tie-ups and digital acquisition are all replicable by a well-funded issuer, and the moat is borrowed from the parent rather than owned.
MOATTEST.quote: It is only in Banca where we have view to the customer statements and debits and credits that we look at NTC and NTCC

RECURRING.rationale: Every call quantifies the renewal book as the funding engine: renewal premium rose from INR57.6bn (51% of GWP) in Q1FY23 to INR587.3bn (58% of GWP) in FY26, growing 17-19%, with 13th/49th month persistency tracked and improving each year (85.6% to 87.9%) and AUM compounding from INR2.6trn to INR5.2trn. The installed base of in-force policies, not new sales, carries the economics.
RECURRING.quote: Renewal premium grew by 19% to INR587.3 billion, which accounts for 58% of the gross written premium.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are almost entirely intermediated — 59,000-60,000 certified SBI/RRB bank facilitators contributing 47-63% of APE plus ~2.6 lakh agents — and management's growth levers are channel investment and training (Agency 2.0, then 'agency next', 120 new branches in FY26, branch/agent productivity metrics) rather than end-customer marketing. Commission structures for corporate and individual agents are discussed as the key channel lever post-regulation.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we have gone into a huddle with our main Banca partner SBI... As of now we are not planning any commission structure change for our corporate agents or for our individual agents

TOLLROAD.rationale: Life insurance is a large discretionary savings decision for the buyer, not a sub-1% critical input, and the calls repeatedly show customers switching between ULIP, par and non-par by market conditions and lapsing policies (61st month persistency ~59-69%, a COVID cohort dip acknowledged). No certification/standards or 'don't switch once converted' language appears.
TOLLROAD.quote: Growth in ULIP is attributed to positive movement in equity market and change in customer preferences.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost leadership is the explicit self-description and is evidenced quarter after quarter: opex ratio 7.2%→6.6%→6.1%→5.3% and total cost ratio ~10.5-10.8% on a INR1trn premium base, with management arguing regulatory surrender-value changes hurt them least because of it, and in Jul 2026 refusing to cut costs further because they are already lowest.
LOWPRICE.quote: SBI Life being the lowest cost operator... we will be the least affected Company

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory is the opposite of pricing power: VoNB margin fell from 30.4% (Q1FY23) to 26.8% (Q1FY25) to 26.2% (Q1FY27), and management twice describes absorbing costs rather than passing them on — first the interest-rate drop on non-par, then the GST change (INR2.3bn hit in one quarter) offset by product mix, not price.
PRICING.quote: the impact of yield movement was absorbed by the Company instead of being passed on to the customers

BRAND.rationale: There is real trust equity — 25-year heritage, the SBI parentage, industry-lowest misselling ratio of 0.02-0.04%, 98.7-99.4% claim settlement, first-in-industry internal ombudsman — but it converts into distribution reach rather than premium pricing, and no sustained A&P spend or brand-led premiumisation is discussed.
BRAND.quote: Our misselling ratio stands at 0.02%, which is one of the lowest in the private industry

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur with quantified impact (Smart Annuity Plus and Smart Platina Plus contributing INR6.1bn in Q1FY23; child, protection and par launches driving 133% par APE growth in FY26; rider attachment on 45-50% of ULIPs), and automated underwriting rose 40%→42%→57%→67%. But this is product/process iteration with no R&D disclosure or industry-R&D-share claim.
INNOVATION.quote: we have very good product launches in all three, non-par segment, par segment and also in the Protection segment

FORWARD.rationale: The company is building owned distribution — 120 new agency branches in FY26 plus 11 more in Q1FY27, online channel +47% APE in FY26, direct/other channels rising from 19% to 28% of NBP — but bancassurance through a third-party bank still supplies roughly half of APE, so control of the customer relationship is only partially owned.
FORWARD.quote: We opened 120 new branches this year. This expansion is aligned with our vision to create infrastructure that supports the long-term development of our agency channel.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Individual APE growth has outpaced the industry (12.9% 3-yr CAGR vs 8.5%; 14% vs 13% in Q1FY27) and leadership is retained, but the actual share numbers have drifted down over the four years — individual rated private share 24.0% (Q1FY23) to 22.4% (Q1FY25) to 22.2% (Q1FY27), total NBP private share 21.9% to 20.5% — so this is share defence, not persistent gain.
SHAREGAIN.quote: retaining our leadership position with a 22.2% private market share

CULTURE.rationale: Bad news is disclosed plainly (COVID-cohort persistency dip, GST and labour-code drag quantified, margin misses explained) and FY26/FY27 guidance was met as promised, with conservative solvency of 1.90-2.21x throughout; but the top job rotates on SBI deputation (Sharma to Jhingran within the period), so long-tenured owner-like leadership is absent even though the CFO/actuary bench is stable.
CULTURE.quote: on both the fronts, IRP as well as margin, we have delivered what we had promised around 14%, 15% growth

MOATTEST.rationale: The hard-to-replicate asset is privileged access to SBI's branch network — 59,000-60,000 trained facilitators and SBI branch productivity of INR6.0mn APE — which no newcomer can rebuild with money alone; but management itself fields the open-architecture question, showing the barrier is regulatory rather than structural.
MOATTEST.quote: the Department of Financial Services Secretary, where he yet again raised the topic of banks should be open architecture

RECURRING.rationale: The deposit franchise is genuinely customer-funded (39.46% CASA, savings rate cut to 2.5%), and cross-sell/trail income recurs off the installed base, but management never discusses attach rates, renewals or deferred revenue in a product-upfront sense.
RECURRING.quote: the trail income from the mutual fund has gone up... CVE is basically the cross-sale income

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No discussion across the 16 calls of professionals, prescribers or trade intermediaries choosing the product on behalf of a paying end customer; distribution is own-branch, YONO and DSA-sourced.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Nothing in the calls frames SBI as a tiny-share-of-cost critical input with certification or standards anchoring; the evidence is silent on this pattern.

LOWPRICE.rationale: This is the classic bank variant across all four sampled years: cheapest deposits in the system, explicit cost obsession (moderating overheads, Project Saral, 10,000 Seva Sarathis to lower cost to serve), and best-in-industry loan quality with GNPA 1.49% / NNPA 0.39% by FY26.
LOWPRICE.quote: 39% CASA at this level is also contributing to bringing down the costs. We got the full benefit of Savings Bank reduction in interest rate to 2.5

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is externally set — EBLR/repo-linked loan books reprice down with rate cuts and management guides NIM merely to ~3% through the cycle, with Q4FY26 NII explicitly hit by pass-through, the opposite of raising price above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: the impact of 25 basis point rate cut which is reflected in the EBLR portfolio and 5 basis point cut which we have done in the MCLR is fully factored in the Q4

BRAND.rationale: Management repeatedly and deliberately trades short-term economics for franchise value — refusing to cut the savings rate to the formula-derived level in FY23, and citing savings balances at three times the next largest bank in FY25 — with trust language sustained through FY26.
BRAND.quote: we do not use this formula to the disadvantage of people... because we value our franchisee

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent named platform investment across years — YONO 2.0 in FY23, analytics-underwritten business in FY25, new YONO / CHAKRA / Analytics 2.0 in FY26 — but no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-R&D framing, and the innovation drives cost-to-serve rather than pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: registrations for our new YONO crossing the 3 crore mark within a short period of one month since its launch

FORWARD.rationale: Not addressed as a pattern — a bank is already direct-to-customer, and the calls contain no own-store/franchise/D2C economics of the kind this pattern tests.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit multi-decade share numbers given on the FY25 call (savings share 20.2% in 2004 → 22.3% in 2014 → 26.27%), plus credit growth consistently above system through FY26 (16.87% YoY) with asset quality improving rather than bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our market share is 26.27%. In 2004, it used to be 20.2%... We have always gained market share while others have lost

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance discipline is real — 1% ROA, ~3% exit NIM and 50bps credit cost promised and delivered through FY26, with the Chairman openly owning a wrong internal bond-yield call — but leadership is state-appointed and churns fast (four chairmen and a dozen MDs across five years), so the long-tenured owner-operator element is absent.
CULTURE.quote: Our internal guidance which has gone wrong earlier, we felt that the bond yields probably would be moving up to 6.75

MOATTEST.rationale: The concrete un-replicable asset is the deposit base — savings balances three times the next largest bank including private peers, 10 crore YONO users and Rs 59 trillion of deposits — which no funded entrant can rebuild, evidenced by SBI sustaining >1% ROA on a Rs 76 trillion balance sheet.
MOATTEST.quote: SBI is among the very few global financial institutions capable of sustaining a ROA of over 1% at this scale

RECURRING.rationale: The Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket) vertical is a genuine post-sale annuity on OEM-fitted content — BS-VI parts flowing back through garages — but it is only ~12% of sales, and across all 14 calls management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates, service contracts or deferred revenue/customer advances; working capital is positive (17.9–19% of sales), the opposite of customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: now that all the vehicles come back to the garages and mechanics for service and repair

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The aftermarket model runs squarely through mechanics and workshops — REPXPERT technical training vans revived in Q2 CY26 and 7,000 Koovers workshops acquired in 2023 — but this channel-through-the-trade dynamic covers only the 12% VLS segment, while the bulk of revenue is direct OEM and industrial contracting.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we revived the use of the REPXPERT vans, which is going to travel across the country, covering close to 8,000 kilometers to be in very close contact with the mechanics and to upskill them in terms of training

TOLLROAD.rationale: Bearings and clutches are small-ticket but mission-critical components in a rational global oligopoly, and the calls show certification-style anchoring — a zero-PPM award from Toyota Kirloskar, valued-supplier status for insulation-coated bearings on Indian Railways and Metro — yet management never quantifies the product as a tiny share of customer cost, and the Jul 2026 call shows customers do negotiate on price.
TOLLROAD.quote: insulation coated bearings that we have been supplying to Indian Railways and the metro applications

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost work is framed purely as internal margin protection (overhead management, portfolio recalibration where they consciously walked away from low-margin industrial revenue in Q1 CY26), not as savings passed to customers; 19% EBITDA and premium technology positioning are the opposite of the low-margin/high-turns model.
LOWPRICE.quote: our commitment as always being on focusing on our operational cost management and overhead cost management

PRICING.rationale: Across the recent calls pricing is negotiated, lagging and incomplete — Jul 2026 explicitly reports input, LPG, freight and FX costs hitting the bottom line with recovery still under discussion, and the Q1 CY26 analyst question on indexation drew no claim of automatic pass-through; gross margin gains come from mix and localisation, not price increases.
PRICING.quote: our input costs have gone up, which is yet to be compensated by the customers, which we are still in discussions with them

BRAND.rationale: There is real heritage and B2B trust — 75 years of the Schaeffler group, INA brand extension into the aftermarket, and a steady stream of customer awards each quarter (six in Q1 CY26) — but no A&P spend, no consumer pull, and no evidence the name commands a price premium.
BRAND.quote: driving forward ground -breaking invention and developments in the field of motion technology for over 75 years

INNOVATION.rationale: Every call lists named new-product business wins with revenue impact — hydraulic cam phasers, planetary gear shafts, double clutches for tractors, overrunning alternator pulleys, e-axle localisation — and customers award them for new product development; however R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and the India entity is largely a localiser of group technology rather than the R&D source.
INNOVATION.quote: an award given to us by Voith Turbo P rivate Limited for excellence in new product development

FORWARD.rationale: The 2023 Koovers acquisition (INR 142 crore, 100% cash) was an explicit move toward the end customer — owning a B2B e-commerce platform, 7,000 workshops and market data rather than selling only through distributor shelves — but three years on it is still sub-scale and loss-making (INR 79 crore revenue, -13.4% EBITDA in Q2 CY26), so the integration has not yet delivered control of pricing or economics.
FORWARD.quote: it is also the existing network of the 7,000 touch points and over 1.8 million parts

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has consistently outrun end-markets — Automotive Technologies +30.8% in Q1 CY26 against ~15% underlying auto production, with management attributing it to rising content per vehicle, and industrial described as growing ahead of market in Q2 CY26 — but no explicit share numbers or named-competitor comparisons are given, and industrial share was deliberately given up during the CY26 recalibration.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have grown ahead of the market growth there

CULTURE.rationale: Harsha Kadam (MD/CEO) has led throughout the period with promises tracked and delivered — the 30–50% dividend payout policy honoured at 45% in a weak year, e-axle localisation followed through, localisation reaching 80% — while bad news is disclosed promptly and repeatedly: Koovers' continuing losses each quarter, 'earnings quality definitely could have been better', and 'free cash flow... we have work to do here'.
CULTURE.quote: we have stayed our commitment and the course of announcing dividend payout ratio between 30 % and 50%

MOATTEST.rationale: The barriers described are real but not obviously un-replicable: 80% localisation, decades-long OEM co-development cycles ('right from the product development stage till the securing of the business'), and zero-defect qualification at customers like Toyota Kirloskar create multi-year switching friction — yet the calls give no evidence of a barrier a well-funded global bearing peer (SKF, Timken, NSK) could not match.
MOATTEST.quote: we have also increased our localization levels, and our localization levels have reached up to 80%

RECURRING.rationale: Across the 2022 and 2026 calls management repeatedly points to lifecycle/services revenue off the installed base (services was 14% of the Jun-22 backlog; Q4FY24 lists 'more services… modernization, digital services and remote asset monitoring'; Q3FY26 cites a data-centre order taken 'along with the subscriptive maintenance contract'), but no attach rates, renewal rates or deferred-revenue-as-funding disclosure is ever given.
RECURRING.quote: it is because of the installed base in the submarines that we are getting the pull-through revenue

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run partly through panel builders and distributors, and the Q3FY26 call notes being 'prescribed' in TBCB tenders — i.e. specified by consultants/utilities — but there is no discussion of trade training programmes or channel-loyalty investment, and most large wins are direct project sales.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: promoting our business relationship with partners who are the distributors and panel builders, in those cases where we cannot go directly to the customer

TOLLROAD.rationale: Switchgear and transformers are a material capex line for utilities, data centres and steel plants, not a sub-1% consumable, and management describes an openly competitive tender market with raw-material inflation only partly passable — the opposite of toll-road price indifference.
TOLLROAD.quote: The margin improvement comes from pricing but it is always a competitive market.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated positioning across every call is premium and digitalised ('superior quality', 'hero offer', 'most stringent… endurance class'), not low price; cost work discussed is restructuring and fixed-cost leverage, with no no-frills proposition or savings passed to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: balanced business models, superior quality and efficient supply chain

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly says inflation can only be partly passed through and attributes the FY24 gross-margin gain of 4.4 points to raw-material normalisation and mix rather than price; by Q4FY26 copper/aluminium up 30% and steel up 10% are flagged as headwinds to defend against, not to price over.
PRICING.quote: we continue to pass on the impact to the customers as and where we are possible. So, partial impact is going to customers, partial is impacting the P&L

BRAND.rationale: The Schneider/EcoStruxure parent brand, Golden Peacock and FICCI awards, LinkedIn top-employer ranking and large self-run Innovation Summit (5,000 attendees) show real B2B brand pull and customer testimony, but no A&P spend, premium pricing or share-with-premium evidence is offered.
BRAND.quote: we just want to share with you as to how our brand has been performing

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year — the digitalised primary-distribution range (FY24), GMSeT indigenised gas-insulated switchgear, Trihal dry-type transformer, One Digital Grid with an AI assistant, and the award-winning EcoStruxure XR Operator Advisor (FY26) — but R&D spend is never disclosed and the technology is largely imported from the parent under licence, so innovation intensity cannot be verified as self-funded.
INNOVATION.quote: GMSeT, which is a primary distribution gas-based equipment, which is made fully in India

FORWARD.rationale: There is no own-store, franchise or D2C element; the company sells through EPCs, distributors and panel builders and explicitly acknowledges cases where it cannot reach the end customer directly.
FORWARD.quote: in those cases where we cannot go directly to the customer

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has consistently outrun end-market capex — FY24 sales +24.2% and orders +26.9%, 9M FY26 orders +37% with backlog up over 50% and the first INR1,000 crore quarter — but management never cites a market-share number or names competitors, so share gain is inferred rather than evidenced.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have an order backlog growth around more than 50%

CULTURE.rationale: Delivery has matched the promises made in 2022 — the bad-debt/terms-and-conditions clean-up became record profits, free cash flow and repayment of intercompany borrowing by FY24 — and bad news (Q4FY24 risk provisions, the INR25 crore gratuity charge, the tax-litigation settlement) is disclosed plainly, but leadership is not stable: MD and CFO both turned over in FY25 and the CFO changed again by FY26.
CULTURE.quote: built on the philosophy of good governance and sustainable growth

MOATTEST.rationale: Barriers cited are real but not un-replicable: parent-derived global designs with large global installed bases, four Vadodara plants, utility/TBCB prescription and long-lived installed-base service relationships — yet the same assets are held by a handful of equally-funded rivals, and no argument is made that a well-capitalised entrant could not qualify over time.
MOATTEST.quote: we have actually supplied close to 170,000 units worldwide across 100 countries

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is voyage/spot and time-charter freight, not an installed base with attached recurring streams; management confirmed the 40 managed government vessels contribute almost nothing (cost-plus management fees only), and in May 2026 disclosed ~60% of the tanker fleet is on voyage (spot) with 40% on time charter, with revenue recognised on percentage-of-voyage-completion rather than billed in advance.
RECURRING.quote: We get only some management fees

TOLLROAD.rationale: Ocean freight is a very large, actively negotiated line item for customers — management sized India's outbound freight bill at ~US$80bn and the top OMCs' at ~INR40,000 crore — and rates are set by global indices with owners 'competing for the available cargo', the opposite of an unnegotiated toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: nearly US$80.00 billion is going out of country in terms of freight

PRICING.rationale: SCI is an explicit price-taker: charters are index-linked with plus/minus, floor and ceiling formulas, VLCC Worldscale swung from WS48 to WS100+ to TD3 460 on war news, and the liner segment's FY26 revenue fell from INR1,036cr to INR784cr and profit from INR166cr to INR75cr purely on freight-rate moderation.
PRICING.quote: definitely it will be linked to the some market indexes

BRAND.rationale: SCI carries genuine institutional standing — Navratna status, 'national carrier', first Indian owner to clear a gas carrier from Hormuz — which is why the government routes demand aggregation (59 oil vessels, 51 container vessels) and the Bharat Container Shipping Line MoU through it; but there is no premium pricing, no A&P, and pricing is wholly index-driven, so the brand is sovereign standing rather than commercial brand power.
BRAND.quote: it is a national carrier and has consistently maintained India's supply line

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D disclosure or product pipeline; fleet growth is by buying 15.5-year-average-age tonnage and second-hand VLGCs built by Hyundai, with the only technical initiative a single government-funded methanol dual-fuel PSV pilot ordered from Mazagon Dock.
INNOVATION.quote: we will be purchasing second-hand vessels also

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is announced rather than yet delivered: the JV aims to capture 25-30% of OMC freight and 51 container vessels are planned to 2047, but the owned fleet stood still at 58 vessels across both calls, the liner segment lost revenue in FY26, and the flagship JV was still 'under active consideration of our Ministry' six months after the Nov-2025 MoU.
SHAREGAIN.quote: currently this is to capture basically maybe 25% to 30% of that component

CULTURE.rationale: Positives are real — conservative balance sheet through the cycle (D/E 0.29, INR2,676cr cash, DSCR 4.61), a stated 10-12% IRR hurdle with project-by-project board approval, rising dividends and 16%+ ROE, and Nov-2025's promise of a stronger tanker H2 was delivered (FY26 tanker profit INR680cr to INR1,190cr) — but leadership is unstable (three chairmen/MDs in five years, the CFO changed between these two calls), management could not answer a basic dry-docking schedule question, and the 'at least 2x-3x revenue at 50% operating margin' JV target was volunteered with no supporting workings.
CULTURE.quote: if IRR is making commercial sense, then only our board approves this

MOATTEST.rationale: There is one un-replicable element — sovereign ownership plus cabotage giving an effective monopoly on coastal crude movement and privileged access to PSU demand aggregation and the Maritime Development Fund — but the core earning assets are globally tradeable second-hand ships any funded entrant can buy, and management concedes its 15-year-old fleet earns less than newer competing tonnage.
MOATTEST.quote: SCI has got a monopoly there

RECURRING.rationale: The Swarna Yojana monthly installment scheme (80,000 customers, ~Rs.200 crore of deposits in Q1FY24) and later 'customer advances with gold rate getting fixed' (Feb 2026) are customer-funded advances, but there is no licence/AMC/renewal stream and working capital is negative-signed the wrong way — inventory of Rs.5,296 crore at 186 days funded by borrowing and trade payables (Jun 2026).
RECURRING.quote: our monthly installment scheme, the Swarna Yojana... the kind of deposits that we have garnered from them is Rs.200 crore

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all twelve calls the demand driver is direct consumer marketing, festive/wedding campaigns and store footfall, not a professional prescriber; franchisees are capital partners under Senco's own brand, not independent experts recommending the product to a paying third party.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The “Elements of Love” campaign is the initiative we have launched.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Affordability engineering is real and repeated — 9-carat/14-carat launches, lightweight designs, 'fit into the budget of the consumer' (Feb 2026, Jun 2026) — plus cheap funding (3-3.5% gold metal loan) and operating leverage in Q3, but there is no itemised cost-culture disclosure and inventory turns are slow (186 days), so scale-driven low-cost economics are not demonstrated.
LOWPRICE.quote: fit into the budget of the consumer, create products, whether it be in 22-carat, 18-carat, 14-carat or even 9-carat

PRICING.rationale: Management shows conditional pricing power — making charges are levied on value so they rise with gold, and lightweight designs command extra making charges (Feb 2026) — with only ~-1% gold volume impact at record prices (Feb 2025); but volume degrowth at high prices is admitted (Jun 2026) and headline EBITDA gains are explicitly attributed to price rise, not sustained pricing, with guidance reverting to 7.5-7.8%.
PRICING.quote: the customer does not get the same jewellery weight at other jewellers and then he is willing to pay extra prices to us, extra making charges to us

BRAND.rationale: Consistent across the arc: Bengal/East India heritage and goodwill leveraged into North and Central India, brand-led shift from unorganized to organized buying with ~50% first-time buyers, loyalty-driven repeat purchase in FY26, and adjacency stretch via the Sennes lifestyle entity (bags, perfume, lab-grown).
BRAND.quote: continue to leverage our brand and goodwill in Eastern India and to build the brand more and more in Northern part of the country

INNOVATION.rationale: Design innovation is regular and quantified — ~9,000 gold and 6,000 diamond designs in Q1FY24, 6,000+ and 3,000+ in Q3FY26, ~1.5 lakh designs for FY26 — plus first-mover on 9-carat hallmarking and AI-based inventory software; but there is no disclosed R&D spend, no share-of-industry-R&D claim, and gross margin stays a modest 14-15%.
INNOVATION.quote: we have launched more than 6,000 designs in gold and more than 3,000 designs in diamond for the quarter

FORWARD.rationale: Senco is a manufacturer (own factories under Senco Artisan, 75% handmade jewellery) that sells through its own retail network and franchisees — 140 stores in Aug 2023 rising to 196 by Feb 2026 and 200+ targeted, with franchisees at 33% of revenue and explicitly positioned as third-party-funded scalability into Tier 2/3/4 towns.
FORWARD.quote: the focus for our team is on how we can open more and more franchisees because that will enable our scalability

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent expansion and organized-sector share capture is evident — store count 140 to 196+, new geographies (Sikkim, MP, Rajasthan, Western UP), FY26 revenue Rs.8,430 crore at 33% growth and 24% five-year CAGR — but the company never gives its own market-share number against named competitors, and concedes new-market entry requires higher discounts.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Currently, we have 196 stores in the whole network.

CULTURE.rationale: Family-run with stable leadership (Sen family, CFO Banka throughout), conservative guidance repeatedly beaten (20-25% guided, 33-35% delivered), store-opening targets met, and unusually detailed self-explanation of the FY25 margin shortfall and hedge accounting; offset by an investor rebuking inconsistent 22% vs 27% growth disclosure (Feb 2025) and hedging discipline loosening from 80-90% to 55-60% and then 40-50% under price volatility.
CULTURE.quote: we've always taken a conservative approach... we have been guiding the investors on around 20% to 25% growth. And by the end of the year, we have achieved a growth of 35%

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuine but partly replicable barriers: multi-decade Bengal heritage, a karigar network behind 75% handmade jewellery, and an inventory-heavy 196-store footprint; against that, management itself describes well-funded rivals using IPO/QIP proceeds to open competing stores and buy share with discounts, which is precisely the copycat-with-money test the pattern requires you to survive.
MOATTEST.quote: a lot of branded jewellery players have done QIPs, and IPOs and they are using that money to open fresh stores

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 19 calls the business is a one-off durable sale (mattress, foam, cushioning) — no AMC, licence, renewal or subscription stream is ever discussed, and there is no mention of deferred revenue or customer advances funding the business; the only recurring-style model is subsidiary Furlenco's furniture rental, which is discussed as a capital-consuming turnaround, not an installed-base annuity.
RECURRING.quote: Furlenco reported a revenue of INR370 crores, a growth of over 60% year-on-year

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run heavily through a dealer/MBO/EBO channel that the company cultivates (dealer incentive and margin programmes, 'cushioning partners', 8,400 U2O dealers, MBO-to-EBO conversion), but the end consumer still chooses the brand — management runs mass consumer campaigns (World Cup) and says buyers 'look at a range… a price point', so the retailer influences rather than prescribes.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We have right now not yet tweet with the dealer margin. It's too early for us to dealer margin or the dealer incentive program.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Foam is a large, visible input for B2B furniture/auto customers and prices are openly renegotiated with raw-material swings (TDI/polyol up 25–35% passed through with lags, Australia 'renegotiating prices with key customers'); no certification, standards or 'don't switch once converted' language appears in any call.
TOLLROAD.quote: polyol and TDI on an average increased between 25% to 35%… we have been able to increase prices to offset those price increases

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost-and-scale thread — Tarang/U2O priced at ~INR2,000 against cotton mattresses and deliberately piggy-backed on existing FMCG distributors to avoid a dedicated cost structure, plus Kurlon synergies (10% better foam yield, lower freight, waste reduction in Australia) — but this is one segment, not a company-wide low-cost culture, and margins are built on brand premium elsewhere.
LOWPRICE.quote: we don't want to create a completely new distribution cost structure only for this because these are lower-cost products… it just is an add-on product, which they carry on their existing infrastructure

PRICING.rationale: Price increases are taken and passed through without volume loss (FY26: mattress volume +12%, value +10%; ASPs rising in offline, e-com and U2O with explicit premiumisation), and management says a 5% rise 'is not a determining factor' for a mattress buyer — but the increases are inflation/raw-material recovery of 4–5%, and in FY23–FY24 pricing was flat-to-negative with ASP pressure and margin compression, so this is cost pass-through more than pricing power above inflation.
PRICING.quote: I generally take the inflation, which is a low number, and some raw material changes that come. But it is of the order of between 4-5% here.

BRAND.rationale: Sleepwell plus Kurlon give the group the No.1 and No.2 branded positions nationally, backed by sustained A&P (4.5–8.6% of sales, World Cup campaign), consistent brand-led growth (Sleepwell mattress +26% in Q3FY24, broad-based Sleepwell+Kurlon growth in FY26), stretch into adjacent categories (pillows, home comfort) and export of the brands into GCC exclusive stores.
BRAND.quote: we were the largest brand in the country with Kurlon being the second largest brand in the country… one of the two brands is a leader in those places

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products arrive regularly with revenue impact — Nexa (INR24,000+), FitRest, Tarang, My Mattress, now pillows — and management credits them for growth, but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, gross margins are raw-material-whipsawed rather than innovation-fat, and marketing (not R&D) is the disclosed investment line.
INNOVATION.quote: This growth is aided by the two new models under the Sleepwell brand, namely Nexa and Fitrest, which has received tremendous market response
