FORWARD.rationale: A consistent, delivered multi-year march toward the customer: exclusive-brand-outlet expansion from ~5,000 outlets in FY23 to ~600 net new showrooms added in each of FY26's periods, first company-owned company-operated stores, D2C brand.com up 136% in FY26 and e-commerce up 53%, Furlenco shop-in-shops in 40+ integrated stores targeting 100, plus own exclusive retail stores across the Emirates.
FORWARD.quote: we added approximately 600 net new showrooms during FY '26… we plan to operationalize select company owned, company operated stores

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is real but largely bought rather than earned organically — volumes were below FY2019 levels and market share was being questioned in FY23, after which Kurlon was acquired to consolidate No.1 and No.2; organic penetration is now genuine (U2O volume +65%/value +111% in FY26, 8,400 dealers in 5,000 towns) but management gives almost no explicit share percentages versus named competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our ability to penetrate the Indian market and to increase our market share is now much more robust

CULTURE.rationale: Positives: stable family ownership (Gautam family across all 19 calls), candid flagging of one-off Kurlon costs, debt reduced INR156 crores, asset monetisation, and the promised Kurlon turnaround actually delivered (mid-single-digit to ~10% EBITDA) with the first-ever dividend in FY26. Against that, the 12.5% EBITDA normalisation promised in Feb 2024 took two more years, the 15% growth/15% margin target set post-Kurlon is still only 'underway' at 10.8%, and the leadership layer churned (CEO Mazumdar in and out, two chairmen and a CFO exited).
CULTURE.quote: we had talked to the investors, and we set ourselves a target of 15% growth with a 15% EBITDA margin… That journey is currently underway.

MOATTEST.rationale: The hard-to-replicate assets are the two heritage brands plus the physical network — thousands of exclusive showrooms, 8,400 U2O dealers across 5,000 towns in 24 states, and a national manufacturing footprint that cuts freight — which a new entrant could not assemble quickly; but foam manufacturing itself is commoditised, raw-material driven, and ~85% of the market is still unorganized, so the barrier is distribution density rather than anything structurally uncopyable.
MOATTEST.quote: now operates through 8,400 dealers and reaches over 5,000 towns across 24 states

RECURRING.rationale: Shaily earns platform/licensing fees from its UK and Abu Dhabi IP entities recognised over 12–21 months against milestones, and each qualified device platform creates a multi-year annuity of pen supply once the customer's drug launches; but there is no discussion of attach rates, AMC/service revenue share, renewals, or customer advances funding working capital.
RECURRING.quote: we basically license or give access to people to our platforms where the fees are recovered over 12 to 18 months or 21 months in terms of agreed milestones with the customer

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all 16 calls Shaily sells B2B to pharma companies, IKEA-type retailers and OEMs; there is no prescriber/installer channel, no trade training programme, and no third-party expert recommending the product to a paying end customer.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The pen injector is a small part of a GLP-1 drug's economics yet is written into the customer's regulatory filing after PQ batches and design verification, so switching is impractical — and management repeatedly stresses a limited-player market ("very limited number of players in the pen market") with FDA/EU approvals as anchoring; management never quantifies the device as <1-2% of customer cost.
TOLLROAD.quote: it's not a very short process, especially for a new supplier to enter

LOWPRICE.rationale: The calls are silent on any cost-obsession culture or itemised savings; discussion of costs is about raw material inflation, exhibition spend and utilisation, and fixed asset turnover of 1.7–2.0x is not the high-turns model this pattern describes.

PRICING.rationale: Roughly 80% of the business is on formula-based raw-material pass-through with quarterly resets, and Q1 FY23 margins collapsed to 12.6% on input inflation the company could not price ahead of; the later margin expansion to 29% EBITDA in FY26 is explicitly mix-driven (healthcare 21%→40% of revenue), not price increases.
PRICING.quote: I would say 80% of our business passes through on a quarterly basis or more.

BRAND.rationale: Shaily sells into other companies' brands (IKEA-type furnishings, customers' Semaglutide launches); apart from naming its own devices Shaily Neo and Harmony, there is no A&P spend, heritage story or distributor leverage discussed on any call.

INNOVATION.rationale: From the Aug 2022 call's IP build-out in Shaily UK through 25+ active device projects, the patent-free spring-driven Neo and Harmony platforms, and FY26 commercial launches plus first US tentative approval, R&D-led IP has driven both volume and a gross/EBITDA margin lift (12.6% EBITDA in Q1FY23 to 29% in FY26) — with capability adds like human factors engineering to serve big pharma.
INNOVATION.quote: every single pen on the market except Novo's FlexTouch and Shaily's Neo are mechanical pens

FORWARD.rationale: Shaily has moved up the value chain into its own IP but remains a pure B2B supplier — no own stores, franchising, D2C channel or consumer-facing distribution appears in any call; even margin disclosure is refused on B2B grounds.
FORWARD.quote: we would not be able to give individual margins, it's a B2B business

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Management claims 65–75% share of the first Semaglutide filers in Canada and first US tentative approval, with healthcare revenue up 139% in FY26 and industrial up 41%; but the largest segment, consumer, de-grew 9% in FY26 and 31% in Q4, and share numbers are given only once rather than tracked rising over time.
SHAREGAIN.quote: I believe Canada, potentially the first 6, 7, 8 filers, I would say we have upwards of 65%, 75% of that share.

CULTURE.rationale: The 2022 promise of ~20 million pens and margin normalisation was substantially delivered (23.3–23.5 million devices, 29% EBITDA, ROCE 35.8%, debt/equity 0.3x by FY26), and management discloses shortfalls plainly — missed pen guidance on capacity, the Q1 FY25 technical failure, unresolved powder-coating problems in the steel furniture plant; stable Sanghvi family leadership offsets repeated CFO turnover (four CFOs across FY21–FY25).
CULTURE.quote: they're a little lower than what we had said and primarily because our capacities are not able to produce what we had projected

MOATTEST.rationale: A new entrant would need a globally marketable device free of Novo/SHL patents, multi-year PQ and design-verification cycles embedded in customers' regulatory dossiers across geographies, and 80→150 million units of qualified assembly capacity — a barrier management articulates concretely and which the FY26 Canada/US/EU approvals validate.
MOATTEST.quote: None that can be marketed globally like ours. None that don't have IP challenges.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four calls revenue is one-time equipment/EPC sales into government tenders; there is no attach-rate, AMC, subscription or renewal disclosure, and instead of customer advances funding the business the company carries enormous receivables (INR1,276 crores at FY26-end, 120–150 day norms, INR477 crores of retention money) — the opposite of negative working capital.
RECURRING.quote: Our receivables have historically also been in the range of 120 to 150 days.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The buying decision runs through government rate contracts and L1 tenders where price is the binding criterion, not through an expert recommender insulating the company from price sensitivity; the only channel-building (rooftop distributors, export dealers) is recent and unaccompanied by any trade-training or professional lock-in narrative.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: there are some criteria for L1, that we will have to match the minimum price

TOLLROAD.rationale: The solar pump is the entire capital item for the farmer/DISCOM, not a sub-1% critical input, and realizations are set by competitive tender rather than paid without negotiation — Magel Tyala tenders alone cut realization 3–4%.
TOLLROAD.quote: the recent Magel Tyala tenders we have had an impact of 3% to 4% on realization

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine cost work — 3% raw-material reduction through vendor scheduling in FY25, operating leverage of 2–3%, and backward integration into VFDs, structures and 2.2 GW of solar cells expected to add ~3% EBITDA — but scale has not produced durable low-cost advantage, since margins fell from ~24% to ~9.6% once input costs and competition moved.
LOWPRICE.quote: we have succeeded in reducing the price by 3% in the raw materials

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory shows the opposite of pricing power: FY23 price hikes were insufficient to cover raw-material inflation, and by FY26–FY27 realization is falling under competitive L1 tenders while a ~6% raw-material hit cannot be passed on, taking EBITDA margin from 24% to ~10%.
PRICING.quote: approximately 6% from higher raw material costs and a 4% from lower realization

BRAND.rationale: Brand recall with farmers is repeatedly cited from 2022 through 2026 (46% KUSUM-2 share on brand recall, a 25,000-pump Maharashtra portal filling in 25 minutes, Shakti brand acceptance carrying the new rooftop inverter), but the brand delivers volume and demand rather than premium pricing — it does not stop tender-driven price erosion.
BRAND.quote: the portal for Shakti opened for 25,000 pumps and it was fully subscribed in 25 minutes

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent innovation record — 14 patents granted of 29 filed by Jul 2024, a patented grid-connected export-to-grid pump, in-house motors/controllers/VFDs, and rooftop inverters showing ~10% better generation — but R&D spend is never quantified or shown to fund pricing power, and gross margins have compressed rather than expanded.
INNOVATION.quote: we received another patent during the quarter, taking the total number of patents granted to 14, out of the 29 which we had filed

FORWARD.rationale: Movement toward the customer is real but early: a dealer/distributor network for exports and rooftop, and a cash/retail business at INR24 crores in Q1 FY27; there are no own stores, franchising or royalty streams, and the dominant integration push is backward (0.5 GW module and 2.2 GW cell plants).
FORWARD.quote: Our emerging cash and retail sales business is witnessing encouraging traction, supported by the continued expansion of our dealer network.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume leadership is persistent — 46% of KUSUM-2 installs in 2022, 86,086 pumps in FY26 (+20%) and +57.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 — but reported share fell to roughly 20% by Jul 2024, and recent share is being defended in an environment of new entrants and falling realizations, which is share held at the cost of profitability.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our competition has increased and because of that the price also gets affected a bit

CULTURE.rationale: Family-led with long-tenured Patidar leadership and evidence of promises kept — the FY26 pledge to fix working capital produced a INR420 crore receivable reduction and 77-day improvement, and management walked away from a Haryana order and INR200 crores of Maharashtra orders on margin/payment grounds; against that, the EV business promised since 2024 (INR250 crores planned) still shows no revenue and guidance has become vague.
CULTURE.quote: in the last quarter, to strengthen the Balance Sheet, we left orders of INR 200 crores in Maharashtra

MOATTEST.rationale: The four-year record answers the replication test negatively: new entrants arrived, tender prices fell and margins more than halved, showing 40 years of brand and 14 patents did not prevent a well-funded copycat from competing away the economics; the integration case (cells/modules by 2027-28) is a promise, not yet a demonstrated barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: we cannot stop the new players. The new players will come, some will exit.

MOATTEST.rationale: Across all five calls management grounds the business in ~3,000 owned registrations plus ~1,000 in the pipeline built over decades, funded by INR 400-505 crore of annual registration capex, with approvals taking 1-7 unpredictable years — a concrete, time-and-money barrier a funded newcomer cannot short-circuit.
MOATTEST.quote: a registration may be obtained in 1 year or 2 years, and the same registration can take 6 to 7 years because of the uncertainties

TOLLROAD.rationale: Regulatory anchoring is explicit and repeated (Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026): customers may only source from registered products and approved factories, so sources are few and tariffs/raw-material rises are absorbed without argument; but management never claims the product is a tiny (<1-2%) share of customer cost, and agrochemicals are a material input for the farmer.
TOLLROAD.quote: customers have no other choice to buy from anywhere... They have to source the products only from registered sources and registered sources are very limited for every product

PRICING.rationale: Conditional pass-through power is real and repeatedly demonstrated — tariffs and RM increases passed on 80-90% with 'graceful' acceptance, and gross margin rose from 25.9% (FY24) to 29.9% (FY25) to 35.9% (FY26) — but reported price/product-mix contribution was negative (-1.8% FY26, -3.0% in Q4 FY26) and FY26 revenue growth leaned on volume and a +10.3% forex tailwind, so this is pass-through rather than sustained real price increases.
PRICING.quote: Price and product mix impact was (-1.8%). And total growth was 21.9%

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-CMD Bubna has led throughout, the company stayed net-debt-free with INR 700-826 crore cash, kept spending on registrations through the downturn and met/raised its own FY26 guidance (15-18% EBITDA raised to 18-20%, delivered 19.7%); against that, the board churned (three chairmen and a CFO exiting FY2021-22), management deflects analyst questions ('go to the next question', 'we will take offline'), and it disowns rather than learns from the 2022 inventory write-off.
CULTURE.quote: We were only facing the situation, but we were not having any contribution to the cause of the situation

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Registrations grew 2,964 to 3,011 with volumes up 42-44% in FY25 and 13.4% in FY26 across Europe, NAFTA and LATAM — growth well ahead of a recovering industry, and geography-specific registration counts show local adaptation — but management never cites a market-share number or names a competitor it is taking share from.
SHAREGAIN.quote: registration wise European region 1,675, NAFTA, 321, LATAM, 760, RoW 248, total 3,004

INNOVATION.rationale: The INR 400-505 crore annual registration capex is a disclosed, growing, margin-funding pipeline investment and management says being second or third registration holder earns better margins, but there is no molecule R&D, no named new products, and it cannot even quantify revenue from recent launches.
INNOVATION.quote: we don't have that analysis and it's difficult to analyze it this way

RECURRING.rationale: No licence, AMC, subscription or renewal stream appears in any of the five calls; revenue is one-off product sales and working capital is firmly positive (118 days in Mar-25, 70-98 days since), so customers fund nothing — the opposite of advance-billed recurring revenue.
RECURRING.quote: Working capital days stood at 98 days as on 31st March 2026

BRAND.rationale: Management attributes customer stickiness entirely to registrations, on-time delivery and quality, never to brand; there is no A&P spend, heritage story, premium-pricing claim or adjacency launch anywhere in the five calls, and it describes itself simply as a marketing company.
BRAND.quote: My always statement that we are a marketing company. And for this marketing, registration is the most important

RECURRING.rationale: Some annuity-like streams have been built and disclosed across the later calls — MTF book (Rs 239cr FY25 → Rs 424cr FY26 → Rs 470cr Q1 FY27), PMS AUM (Rs 100cr → Rs 150cr), uTrade subscriptions (+20% QoQ, 5,231 clients) — but there is no attach rate, renewal rate or deferred-revenue/customer-advance discussion, and the bulk of profit still comes from prop/broking volumes.
RECURRING.quote: MTF is one thing where we are bullish and it gives us sustainable revenue

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Authorised persons/APs are added as a channel (29 new APs in Q3 FY25) and third-party product distribution is being built, but the stated strategy is the opposite — company-owned Tier-3 branches going direct to the end customer, with no trade-training or channel-lock-in language.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our goal is to approach the maximum direct customers as much as possible in Tier-3 cities

TOLLROAD.rationale: Revenue is directly geared to exchange volumes and regulation, not to a small-but-critical input customers pay without negotiating; SEBI's derivative measures and STT hikes cut ADTO ~21% in one quarter (Q3 FY25) and management admits transaction/compliance costs squeeze margins.
TOLLROAD.quote: ADTO has dropped from Rs. 10,400 crores from Quarter 2 to Rs. 8,200 crores per day in Quarter 3

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real cost-and-capital-efficiency thread — self-clearing instead of PCM, second membership working-capital gains, repeated 'cost optimization', and a claim of being most cost-effective on scale — but management explicitly refuses the discount-broking volume model, so scale-plus-low-price is not the strategy.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are the most cost effective because of our market share

PRICING.rationale: Across the 13 calls pricing is set by exchanges and regulators, not the company; standardised exchange charges, higher STT and F&O curbs drove a 24% QoQ consolidated revenue fall in Q3 FY25 and consolidated FY26 PAT slipped to Rs 324cr from Rs 328cr on flat revenue.
PRICING.quote: High transaction costs and compliance costs impacting overall margins

BRAND.rationale: No heritage, A&P or premium-pricing evidence; management concedes limited marketing reach and slow customer acquisition in Nov 2022 and, by Jul 2026, cannot explain why a 'low PE, high growth' stock is unloved — brand pull is absent from the record.
BRAND.quote: you might see that customer acquisition is a bit slow

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a genuine cadence of named launches — IBD platform (Sep 2022), uTrade Algos, MTF, institutional desk, PMS, AIF, Share India Cred, GIFT City — and a stated AI/automation investment, but no disclosed R&D spend, no share-of-industry-R&D framing, and no evidence the innovation produces pricing power or higher gross margins.
INNOVATION.quote: Share India is a leader in providing the algo trading platform for the retailers

FORWARD.rationale: A deliberate move toward the end customer: own trading apps, direct retail focus, and company-owned Tier-3 branches (7 open, 30 targeted in 24 months) with disclosed unit economics of an 8-month payback on a Rs 15cr MTF book per branch; but no franchising, royalties or own-store share-of-sales disclosure.
FORWARD.quote: these are Company owned branches where we offer not only broking services, but all the Wealth products

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share numbers are quoted (6%+ options, 5-7% commodity, 8-10% currency, 20% ISFC market-making in Nov 2022) and client/institutional counts rise (137→186→212 empanelments), but by Feb 2025 management describes share as merely 'stable' and volumes falling in line with the industry — growth by adding verticals, not by persistent share capture.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our market share has remained more or less stable in comparison to on a quarter-on-quarter basis

CULTURE.rationale: Several old promises were visibly delivered — the algo product promised for Feb/Mar 2023 became uTrade with 5,231 clients by FY26, PMS was board-approved in Jan 2025 and launched with Rs 150cr AUM by Q1 FY27, branches promised were opened — and the balance sheet is conservative (Rs 2,760cr net worth); against that, weak quarters are consistently attributed to regulation and geopolitics rather than owned, and the board has churned heavily (Rajesh Gupta, Saroj Gupta, Suresh Arora exits).
CULTURE.quote: this year Wealth Management team has joined and operations will start for the Wealth Management as promised earlier

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in the record a funded newcomer could not rebuild — the business depends on exchange memberships, licences and prop-desk funding that regulators can and did restrict, and management itself lists RBI funding curbs and frequent SEBI changes as structural constraints.
MOATTEST.quote: RBI restrictions and tighter norms impacting funding availability for proprietary business activities

RECURRING.rationale: CDMO/licensing structure gives multi-year annuity-like streams — the Unicycive deal is a 4+4 year exclusive supply agreement with $10m staged milestones and customer-funded capex, and later calls show recurring licensing income (~INR200 crores) plus quarterly partner profit-shares — but there is no installed base, attach rate, renewal rate or deferred-revenue funding discussion in the classic sense.
RECURRING.quote: it is four years plus automatically renewal for four years… they are also funding us creating the dedicated block for them

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The FY26 NorUDCA launch is explicitly prescriber-led — physicians choose, patients pay — and distribution runs through three large pharma partners' detailing forces rather than end-customer marketing; but no trade training programmes or channel-relationship investment is described across the 18 calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: has exceeded our expectations, and we have had great response from the physicians

TOLLROAD.rationale: The specialty CDMO franchise has toll-road economics: Shilpa is the exclusive API+formulation source embedded in a partner's NDA (so switching means refiling), the innovator funded the dedicated block ($6.5m), and margins are stated above 50% — regulatory anchoring via DMFs/CEP is the switching cost, though no explicit 'tiny share of customer cost' or certification-standard language is used.
TOLLROAD.quote: we are the exclusive supplier for them… we have the margins in this that much we can tell you above 50

LOWPRICE.rationale: Strategy across all 18 calls is the opposite of low-price-plus scale: limited-competition, first-in-class, complex 505(b)(2)/NCE/biologics products carried at 68-71% gross margins; cost work is framed as margin defence against API price erosion, not as a replicable cost culture passed to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: our focus is on limited -competition products, first -in-class therapies, complex delivery platforms

PRICING.rationale: Evidence points to price deflation, not pricing power — FY23 gross margin fell 68%→61% on API/formulation price erosion, Europe is admitted to be tender-driven, and management expects Nilotinib generic entry to hit FY28; margin recovery by FY26 comes from mix and operating leverage, never from disclosed price increases.
PRICING.quote: pricing pressure on some of our key products both in the API and formulation segment

BRAND.rationale: There is a reputational (B2B) brand — a stated global reputation for compliant, non-infringing chemistry that helps win CDMO mandates, and the FY26 own-label NorUDCA launch — but no heritage story, A&P spend, or distributor leverage is discussed, and consumer brand economics are absent.
BRAND.quote: globally , it is known that if Shilpa gives the product , then it is complian t with all global standards

INNOVATION.rationale: R&D-led differentiation is the whole model and it is now converting: named products each year (Nilotinib EU, Rotigotine transdermal MA, NorUDCA NCE launch, Ondansetron ER, ADC/albumin/Aflibercept pipeline) funded by 68-71% gross margins, with FY26 revenue +18%, EBITDA +30% and adjusted ROCE up from ~4% (FY23) to 17.4% (FY26).
INNOVATION.quote: invest in R&D, build differentiated assets, launch it with strong margins, scale it through partnership

FORWARD.rationale: The company moves away from the customer, not toward it — the repeated model is out-licensing and 'launching niche products globally through strategic partners' (Amneal in US, tender partners in EU, three pharma partners for NorUDCA, SteinCares for Nivolumab); no own stores, franchising or D2C exists beyond one domestic own-label.
FORWARD.quote: our strategy of developing and launching niche products globally through strategic partners is gaining very good traction

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is real but partly borrowed and uneven: the US partner's Pemetrexed share reached 35% and EU formulation revenue more than doubled to INR200+ crores in FY26, yet US revenue flatlined around INR28 crores a quarter, azacitidine was exited, RoW de-grew, and API was flat for 7-8 quarters.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our U.S. formulation revenue has grown only from INR54 crores in FY25 to INR80 crores in FY26, and it's kind of flatlined

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured promoter family (V.C. Bhutada, now son Keshav as CEO), candid disclosure of the USFDA import alert and margin erosion in 2022, capex funded by internal accruals, and self-measurement on ROCE (3.5%→17.4%); against that, multiple 2022 promises slipped badly — Aflibercept Phase III 'next month' in 2022 is still pre-submission in FY27, and film/transdermal revenue arrived ~4 years later than the '23-'24 guidance.
CULTURE.quote: whatever heavy lifting was required for the company on the investment side, we have largely completed in last many years

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — 212 DMFs, non-infringing process IP, a partner-funded dedicated NCE block embedded in an NDA, and a claimed first-of-its-kind integrated ADC suite (mAb + payload + linker + conjugation) in India — but much of the portfolio is generic oncology API and 505(b)(2) work that a well-funded Indian peer could rebuild in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: it will be o ne of its kind in India

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Calls disclose trade-sales share (78-80% in FY23 falling to 65% by Q3FY26) but never discuss masons, contractors, dealers or influencer training programmes, so there is no evidence either way on an expert-recommender model.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cement here behaves as a price-negotiated bulk commodity, not a critical micro-cost input: management repeatedly ties realisation to demand and to the price gap versus UltraTech, and had to sacrifice volume for two quarters just to narrow a INR30/bag discount, the opposite of customers paying without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: We had a large divergence between our sales price and sales price of competitors like UltraTech

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost leadership is the consistent thread across all four years: Akhoury's FY23 pledge to "remain the cost leader" is backed in FY26 by the lowest fuel cost per kcal in the industry (1.56 vs peer 1.80), 61% green power, multi-fuel burners chosen on landed cost, and the claim of the peer group's highest EBITDA per ton for FY26.
LOWPRICE.quote: per kilocalorie cost is lowest in the industry sitting at 1.56

PRICING.rationale: The record shows price deflation, not pricing power: realisation fell from INR4,854 (Dec'22) to INR4,469 (Q1FY25), the company sold at a INR30/bag discount to the leader, and Bhandari states plainly that price is set by demand and refuses to guide on it; the FY26 3.6% realisation gain was bought by giving up volume growth (2.2% for the year).
PRICING.quote: Pricing is a function of demand. If the demand does not revive, the pricing power will not be there with the industry.

BRAND.rationale: Real brand investment is visible — new brand identity, premium Bangur MAGNA, "Solid Ghar Sirf Bangur" campaigns reaching 100 million people, and Bhandari arguing volume gain proves brand acceptance — but the brand still commanded a discount to UltraTech that took two painful quarters to halve, so premium pricing is not established.
BRAND.quote: advertisement expenses also increased due to the launch of the new brand identity, along with Bangur MAGNA, our premium brand

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is real but process- and sustainability-led (1 GW captive power, 61% green electricity, alternative fuels, agro-waste, digital/SAP/CRM investment, one premium product launch) with no R&D spend, pipeline, or share-of-industry-R&D ever disclosed across the twelve calls.
INNOVATION.quote: significant investments are in process to make Shree, a very modern company in terms of technology

FORWARD.rationale: A genuine forward-integration push into ready-mix concrete built from scratch — 7 plants in Aug'24, 19 by Q3FY26, 36 entering FY27 and a 50-55 target — with 45% captive cement consumption, but revenue is still trivial (INR71 crores a quarter) and there are no own stores, franchises or royalties.
FORWARD.quote: The company plans to set up almost 100 Bangur concrete plants over the next 3 to 5 years

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Shree gained share convincingly through FY23-FY25 (8% volume growth in Q1FY25 while Ramco, Dalmia and UltraTech shrank), but from Oct'24 management deliberately handed share back to chase price, closing FY26 at just 2.2% volume growth and guiding only to industry-plus-1%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Ramco lost 21% in quantity, 16% was lost by Dalmia, UltraTech lost 9%. We gained 1%.

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on earlier calls are audited on later ones — the May'26 call opens by matching the 2-3% growth guidance (delivered 2.2%) and the pledge to narrow the price gap — alongside a conservative balance sheet (no borrowing in 15 years, capex from internal accruals, INR6,400 crores net cash, AAA rated), long-tenured Bangur family leadership, and candid admissions of weak quarters and cost overruns (INR52 crores of Guntur/Nawalgarh stabilisation spend).
CULTURE.quote: which explains our ethos of delivery and not proclamation

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-copy assets exist — limestone reserves secured to 80 mt, 1 GW of captive power with 61% renewables, and 40 years of lowest-cost fuel procurement — but the calls also show the advantage is contestable: capacity is added freely by rivals, utilisation sat at 56% in Dec'25, and Shree still had to discount to the market leader.
MOATTEST.quote: We have the necessary limestone reserves for taking us up to 80 million tons

RECURRING.rationale: The OEM-fitment-then-aftermarket-replacement structure gives a genuine annuity off an installed base (a 150-million vehicle park, 1,200 aftermarket touch points, packaged con-rods/valve seats/guides sold with pistons), but across all 12 calls management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates, service/AMC contracts, subscriptions, or deferred revenue/customer advances as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: we have over 1,200 touch points now and all the touch points have actually improved our visibility in the market

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Aftermarket demand is effectively specified by mechanics/garages at the point of engine overhaul, and SPR bundles complementary parts to capture that decision, but the calls show no trade training programmes or channel-relationship investment beyond distribution reach.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: every time the engine is open, the connecting rod has to be changed if the piston requires a change

TOLLROAD.rationale: Pistons/rings/valves are a tiny share of vehicle cost yet critical, sold into a small qualified oligopoly with long OEM homologation and full raw-material pass-through — but management also admits being priced out of lines by cheaper competitors, which is not toll-road behaviour.
TOLLROAD.quote: 100% of the commodity changes are backed up by the customers, and we go back to our customers and claim

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real cost culture (five-year 'leakers and bleeders' programme, productivity/automation, operating leverage), but the company deliberately abandons price-competitive business rather than winning on low price with scale — the opposite of Low Price Plus.
LOWPRICE.quote: for areas where we were getting priced out because of our competition being on a much lower price targets, we decided to actually exit those businesses

PRICING.rationale: Margin expansion from FY20's 12.4% EBITDA to ~23% came from mix pruning, productivity and operating leverage, not price increases; pricing is a formula-based commodity pass-through with a quarter's lag, and management conceded exiting products where competitors underpriced them.
PRICING.quote: One is, of course, going back to the customers to see if we can get some improved prices

BRAND.rationale: Six decades of heritage under the SPR and Usha names with aftermarket recognition domestically and in 45 export countries, and the name is being stretched to a multiproduct identity (SPR Auto Technologies) — but there is no A&P spend, premium pricing or share-plus-price evidence in any call.
BRAND.quote: Our products are marketed and distributed under our well-known renowned brands SPR and Usha

INNOVATION.rationale: A DSIR-recognised technology centre, four decades-old technology collaborations, hydrogen pistons in advanced field trials with three customers, Euro-6 ring coatings, ICAT/PM E-Drive-approved localised motors and hybrid engine programmes slated for 2029-30 show a regular pipeline; however R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and much core technology is licensed from Kolbenschmidt, Riken, Fuji and Takahata rather than owned.
INNOVATION.quote: There are at least 3 customers with whom our product is under advanced field trials

FORWARD.rationale: The company remains a component manufacturer selling to OEMs and through third-party aftermarket distribution and Tier-1 customers; across the 12 calls there are no own stores, franchising, licensing royalties or D2C revenue — investment goes into JIT assembly centres for OEMs, not toward the end customer.
FORWARD.quote: we have set up five assembly units in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat where most of the OEMs have their manufacturing setups

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Repeated, quarter-after-quarter outgrowth of every end segment — 11.5% vs low-single-digit industry in Q3FY25, standalone 9.4% vs ~6% market, subsidiaries 'outgrowing 100%', 25% consolidated growth in FY26 — achieved alongside rising margins rather than bought with price, plus aftermarket geographic expansion from Assam to Kerala and exports to 45 countries.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We have continued to outperform the industry, which grew by low single-digit figure this quarter on an overall basis

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter-family and long-tenured professional leadership (KKS and Prem Rathi through the whole period, staff with 30+ years), a conservative balance sheet (D/E 0.24, debt-free-cash-free INR16.7bn Antolin buy funded without stress), uninterrupted dividends and bonuses since 1991, prompt disclosure of the INR252mn Labour Code exceptional hit, and promises delivered — the Coimbatore motor plant flagged in earlier calls was inaugurated in Nov 2025 and the five-year margin programme visibly delivered.
CULTURE.quote: in November 2025, as committed earlier, we have inaugurated the state-of-the-art world-class facility at Coimbatore

MOATTEST.rationale: Barriers are real but not un-replicable: 50+ year exclusive technology tie-ups (Kolbenschmidt 1972, Riken 1978, Honda Foundry 1989, Fuji 1993), decades of OEM qualification and JIT co-location, and rare full-localisation ICAT/PM E-Drive approval — yet the piston capacity itself was purchasable off Craftsman's Sunbeam for just INR280mn, and the newer plastics/interiors businesses were bought rather than built.
MOATTEST.quote: Our longest-standing partnership dates back to 1972 with the Kolbenschmidt Group, focusing on piston manufacturing

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Origination is branch-led and direct to the retail borrower rather than through recommending professionals; management explicitly resists building the business on third-party sourcing (the only intermediary reference is a two-wheeler DSA payout accounting change in Q4 FY26).
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we do not wish to make the outsourcing as a big way to move forward in a personal loan

LOWPRICE.rationale: This is a high-yield, high-credit-cost niche lender, not a low-price scale player: NIM ran 6.91% (Q1 FY23) to 9.04% (Q1 FY27) with credit cost guided around 2% and cost of funds still 8.56%; the cost-to-income improvement in Q4 FY26 came from a flat headcount and lower branding spend, not an articulated cost culture.
LOWPRICE.quote: the credit cost is factored in our lending rates

PRICING.rationale: Management claimed pricing power explicitly in Aug 2022 and delivered it through the cycle — NIM expanded from 6.91% to 9.04% across the 18 calls while rate cycles moved both ways, and they state credit cost is priced into lending rates; the only dilution is deliberately passing lower funding costs into new-vehicle loans from FY27.
PRICING.quote: We have the pricing power. Since we are in the niche segment of lending to used vehicle and in the rural market, we have that pricing power to pass on any increase in borrowing cost

BRAND.rationale: A ~50-year heritage in used-vehicle finance lets them win back lapsed customers and supports a large retail deposit franchise (24% of borrowings), and they spend on branding; but the calls never evidence brand-driven premium pricing or share gain directly.
BRAND.quote: Shriram has been in this business for nearly 50 years

FORWARD.rationale: They own their distribution — ~76,000 employees and a national branch network, with 2,200 branches retrofitted (strong rooms, security) to originate gold loans and cross-sell personal loans to existing gold/MSME customers — and prefer in-house sourcing to outsourced channels.
FORWARD.quote: around 2,200 branches are made ready for gold loan activity

SHAREGAIN.rationale: AUM compounded from INR1.31 lakh crore (Q1 FY23) to INR3.14 lakh crore (Q1 FY27) with disbursement growth of 15–24% and stated penetration gains — new vehicle from 10% to 16–17% of disbursement, gold and MSME targeted to double their book share — but explicit market-share numbers versus named competitors are never given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the customers who were otherwise going out to the competition, we are able to retain and finance them

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is unusually stable (Revankar, Parag Sharma and Sunder present on calls from FY23 to FY27), guidance is conservative and repeatedly met or beaten (15% AUM guidance held then exceeded; 18% reaffirmed in FY27), the balance sheet is run conservatively (excess provisions of INR6,730 crore over RBI norms in FY23, leverage 3.8x falling to 2.1x post MUFG), and they disclose unflattering items plainly, including the INR196.95 crore labour-code gratuity hit and the two-wheeler DSA accounting change.
CULTURE.quote: we always have been conservative in our guidance

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barrier is the ~50-year-old used-vehicle appraisal and rural collection franchise — thousands of branches, ~76,000 staff and near-100% collection efficiency in a segment banks avoid — which underwrites the pricing power; the calls assert this niche position but never quantify why a funded newcomer could not rebuild it.
MOATTEST.quote: we are in the niche segment of lending to used vehicle and in the rural market

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 15 calls revenue is one-off tonnage sales of steel, pellets, alloys, aluminium foil — no licence, AMC, service or subscription stream is ever mentioned, no attach or renewal rates, no installed base. The only 'advance' language is trade terms, not deferred revenue funding a recurring annuity.
RECURRING.quote: the group focuses mainly on selling, either on advances or letter of Credit basis leading to lower debtors

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through a B2B/B2C dealer-distribution network with mass-media pull marketing (Salman Khan endorsing the Tiger TMT brand), not through prescribing professionals; no trade-training programmes or channel-expert lock-in are discussed in any call.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our branding and marketing initiative of Tiger brand promoted by Salman Khan

TOLLROAD.rationale: Steel, pellets and ferro alloys are a large, closely negotiated input for customers, and management repeatedly describes prices being set by China exports, imports and global volatility rather than by any certification or standards anchoring.
TOLLROAD.quote: The Indian steel prices remain under pressure on a higher import and comparatively weak export

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost leadership is the recurring theme across all four years and is itemised: 82% captive power at Rs.2.47/kWh vs Rs.3.04 blended, coke-oven and blast-furnace backward integration, TGPRT energy recovery, brownfield capex at roughly a third of greenfield cost, and working capital cut from 22 to 9 days — low unit margins (PAT margin 6%) offset by scale and high asset turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: One of the biggest competitive strengths continues to be our integrated operation and industry-leading cost position

PRICING.rationale: The company is an explicit price taker: margins swing with coal, iron ore, China exports and LME, and management concedes aluminium pricing is a pass-through. Realisation gains in FY26 are attributed to product-mix shift into value-added lines, not to price increases holding above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: related to your aluminium price, we should not be very much worried... it is going to be almost passed through

BRAND.rationale: There is a real consumer-facing brand effort — Tiger TMT/stirrups/wire/roofing/stainless/aluminium foil all carried under one name, celebrity A&P, and a stated B2C push that management credits for holding volumes when peers fell 20-25% in Q1 FY23 — but no evidence of premium pricing or heritage-driven durability; realisations track the commodity cycle.
BRAND.quote: with the enhancing of our brand values... having Salman Khan and getting into the penetration of the rural it really helped us to overcome this crisis

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or named product innovation is disclosed in any of the 15 calls; 'value-added product' growth comes from buying and building capacity (CRM, colour-coated, blast furnace, foil stock) rather than from proprietary technology.
INNOVATION.quote: the focus has been on the value added product, where the revenue has grown at a CAGR of 43.2% in last five years

FORWARD.rationale: There is a consistent downstream/forward-integration programme — foil converting, heat treatment, CRM/colour-coated, stainless downstream, plus a stated shift toward B2C and a large Eastern India distribution set-up — but no owned stores, franchising, royalties or D2C e-commerce economics are ever quantified.
FORWARD.quote: focusing more on B2C and value-added product... We already have a vast distribution set up, specifically in the Eastern India

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume growth has persistently run far above the 7-8% Indian steel demand growth management cites (FY26 volumes +26% to 4.94mt, revenue Rs.6,000cr to Rs.18,552cr since the 2021 IPO), and share gain is an explicit aim, but the company never gives market-share percentages or comparisons against named competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we are adding our existing capacity, which will help us to reduce our cost and help us to take more market share

CULTURE.rationale: Family-controlled with Brij Bhushan Agarwal and Deepak Agarwal present on every call from Aug 2022 to Jul 2026; capex is self-funded from internal accruals, the balance sheet stayed net cash (Rs.1,099cr in Q2 FY25) through the peak capex cycle, dividends have run every quarter since listing, CRISIL upgraded AA-/positive to AA/positive, and ROCE/ROE are disclosed and targeted — a record of promising and then delivering, though the tone is notably promotional.
CULTURE.quote: whatever numbers we have given, we have over delivered it in the last four years... We rather believe to speak less and deliver more

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but capital-replicable barriers: full backward integration, captive power rising to 706MW, railway sidings, and brownfield sites that let them build a 2mt HR plant at about a third of the Rs.16,000-18,000cr greenfield cost, plus proximity (80% of sales within 500km) to Eastern India. A well-funded entrant with time and capital could nonetheless build equivalent commodity capacity.
MOATTEST.quote: to set up a 2 million tonne of HR plant, it generally costs close to INR16,000 crores to INR18,000 crores. But in our case... almost 1/3 capex

RECURRING.rationale: Product-and-service revenue is a stable ~69-70% of sales and the locomotive contract carries a 35-year maintenance tail after an 11-year delivery period, but across all four calls management never quantifies attach rates, renewal rates, AMC revenue share or deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: we will be delivering 1,200 locomotives over a period of 11 years... with a maintenance period of 35 years thereafter

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Dec 2025 describes routes to market running through OEMs and territory sales, and both 2022 and 2024 calls stress an ecosystem of system integrators, service providers and partners who design solutions on Xcelerator — but there is no trade-training programme or prescriber economics discussed, and the end customer is the paying industrial buyer.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The route to the markets happen via OEMs, it happens via our territory sales

TOLLROAD.rationale: The installed-base statistics imply toll-road economics — one in three PLCs, 75% of discom switchgear, 50% of metros electrified — and control/automation content is a small fraction of a plant's capex yet critical to operation, but management never uses the '<1-2% of cost' or 'customers don't switch' framing, and Jun 2026 shows it could not fully pass on input costs.
TOLLROAD.quote: one in three automation controllers, PLCs, in the country that have been installed, are from Siemens. Over 75% of utilities distribution discoms are powered by Siemens switchgear

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management explicitly positions away from low-price competition, arguing the tender-lowest-bidder model is being replaced by solution selling on flexibility, quality and speed; cost discipline is mentioned (non-material costs up only 0.8% in Q6 FY26) but never as a price-leadership strategy.
LOWPRICE.quote: it is not about a product at a cheapest price, it is about delivering a solution that answers a specific problem of a customer

PRICING.rationale: FY24 margin expansion was explicitly attributed to 'better pricing' and 'price enforcement' with 100-270bps EBITDA gains, but the Jun 2026 call is a direct counter-example: commodity and FX-driven cost increases could not be passed through and EBITDA margin fell 290bps to 9.7%.
PRICING.quote: we have seen price increases for material and purchase products from suppliers, which we couldn't completely pass on to the market

BRAND.rationale: Siemens carries genuine engineering heritage and third-party validation (ranked India's No.1 sustainable company in its sector, ESG upgrades from all three agencies, governance leadership), and the name stretches across DI/SI/Mobility — but no A&P spend, consumer brand premium or distributor leverage is ever discussed.
BRAND.quote: We've been ranked as India's number one sustainable company in the engineering, electrical and electronic sector

INNOVATION.rationale: Xcelerator has been developed and reported on consistently since the 2022 Innovation Day, scaling from 125 use cases to 200+ references by Dec 2024, plus industrial AI, digital twins and Industrial Edge; but R&D spend is never disclosed or shown growing, gross margins are project-grade, and much of the core technology and software layer sits with the German parent rather than the Indian entity.
INNOVATION.quote: two years ago, when we launched this, we had 125 individual cases... we've just taken a couple of these use cases and have been able to already win 200 references

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Management claims market outperformance through a weak private-capex cycle and cites dominant installed-base positions, with orders up 26.8% and revenue up 14.3% in H1 FY26 on a record INR 450bn backlog — but no explicit share series versus named competitors is given, and Digital Industries has been losing ground through destocking.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have outperformed the markets in spite of the fact that there have been global headwinds, in spite of the fact that private sector CapEx has not yet kicked in

CULTURE.rationale: The trajectory shows promises made and kept: the Dec 2022 statement that Mobility was a strategic focus and that the 9,000HP loco would be localised became first contractual delivery of 40 locomotives with 90% localisation by Mar 2026; the demerger promised for CY2025 was completed; and Wolfgang Wrumnig discloses bad news plainly (290bps margin decline, inability to pass on costs) rather than burying it, under a stable long-tenured MD.
CULTURE.quote: we delivered the first contractual … we met the first contractual delivery dates of dispatching 40 locomotives from Dahod to the Indian Railways and have been fully paid

MOATTEST.rationale: Real replication barriers exist — 25 localised factories, an 11-year/35-year railway contract, an approved bogie plant now inside Siemens' global factory network winning an INR 18bn export order out to 2039, and an installed base a newcomer cannot buy — but much of the advantage rests on the parent's technology and transfer pricing rather than something the Indian entity independently owns.
MOATTEST.quote: Our bogie factory in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is now part of the global network of factories of our Mobility activities

RECURRING.rationale: Pure build-to-sell residential development: revenue is booked on project completion with no licence, AMC, subscription or installed-base stream discussed in any of the ten calls; customer advances arise only from construction-linked payment plans that fund the same project being built.
RECURRING.quote: by and large, we are sticking to a strategy of mid-income housing, working on a build-to-sell model

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The calls are silent on professional prescribers or trade training; brokerage appears only as a cost line ("SG&A brokerage and taxes") and the 2023 call's "strong distribution network" is never developed into channel lock-in or training programmes.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is a home at an average ticket of INR3.5 crore per unit — the buyer's single largest outlay, the opposite of a sub-1% critical input; management repeatedly re-engineers unit sizes down to keep ticket sizes affordable, showing high, not negligible, price sensitivity.
TOLLROAD.quote: we've tried to ensure that the ticket size remains attractive, and it's affordable for the end user

LOWPRICE.rationale: The affordable/mid-income positioning ("MAKING INDIA AFFORDABLE"), deliberate competitive pricing to drive volume, fast land-to-launch churn (high asset turns) and cost/efficiency work with Bain and named contractors fit the pattern; but 35% embedded EBITDA margins and steadily rising realisations are the opposite of low unit margins, and no itemised cost-culture savings are ever disclosed.
LOWPRICE.quote: Since we want to drive good volumes on the product front, we try to stay as competitive on the product pricing as possible

PRICING.rationale: Realisation rose from ~INR4,000/sq ft in FY21 to INR7,425 (FY23), INR9,800 (H1FY24), INR11,700 (FY24), INR12,700 (9MFY25) and INR15,200 (9MFY26) while volumes grew — presales CAGR of ~60% over three years — and management explicitly says project-level increases were passed on and guides to further high-single-digit rises; part of the lift is mix and market, and Feb 2026 flags demand as "steady but not euphoric".
PRICING.quote: even on a like-to-like market, individual markets also, we have seen an escalation closer to about 15-odd percent in each of our key micro markets

BRAND.rationale: Management consistently invokes brand, track record and customer trust as the reason for absorption (Nov 2023: "coming from a very strong brand"; Feb 2026: preferred-brand positioning), backed by ISO/IGBC/EDGE certification and an IFC debt tie-up; but there is no heritage story, no A&P spend disclosure, and no evidence of the brand being stretched into adjacencies.
BRAND.quote: we do want to position ourselves as the preferred brand -- preferred choice of customers in this middle-income housing market

INNOVATION.rationale: Product-level innovation is real and recurring — green-certified homes (IGBC Gold, IFC EDGE) claimed to save ~30% energy/50% water, resized 1,800 sq ft formats to protect ticket size, and a Feb 2026 earthquake-safety technology agreement — but no R&D spend is disclosed, there is no pipeline or share-of-industry-R&D language, and none of it is tied to margin or pricing outcomes.
INNOVATION.quote: we have recently entered in an agreement to use advanced earthquake safety technology across our high-rise projects

FORWARD.rationale: The calls never discuss owned stores, franchising, licensing or D2C channel economics; the only channel reference is brokerage as an expense line.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has clearly outpaced the market — presales from INR1,861 crore in H1FY24 to INR128.8 billion in CY2024 and ~60% three-year CAGR, with a self-described unparalleled 8 msf launch pipeline and dominant supply in Sector 71 — but no explicit market-share percentages or share-versus-named-competitor data are ever given, and management itself reframes the story as category creation rather than share.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we are amongst few large supply creators in the Sector 71 market

CULTURE.rationale: Family promoter ownership with stable Aggarwal leadership, a conservative balance sheet (net debt held ~INR10 billion through years of growth, guided to zero), candid disclosure of misses (rain-hit completions, pollution-ban sales drag, launches drifting to H2, an openly acknowledged gap to FY26 guidance), and FY25 guidance broadly met; against that, three CFOs turned over across FY24–FY25 and 9MFY26 sales of INR67 billion against INR125 billion guidance leaves a large unclosed promise.
CULTURE.quote: there is still a bit of gap between the current achievement and the overall guidance for the year

MOATTEST.rationale: The concrete barrier is finite prime land assembled in three Gurugram micro-markets — ~92 contiguous owned acres in Sector 71 plus 21 msf of approved-stage land bank — which a new entrant cannot simply buy back at the same cost; but land, approvals and contractors are all purchasable by well-funded rivals (DLF, Godrej, M3M operate the same corridors), so this is a head-start rather than an un-replicable moat.
MOATTEST.quote: we have access to about 92 acres plus land, which is mostly owned by the company

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is regulated tariff/PPA offtake from state DISCOMs, not a front-end product sale with an attached service annuity; instead of customers funding the business, SJVN funds them — receivables ballooned to INR1,299 crore (incl. INR906 crore unbilled) in FY26, and earlier calls dwell on J&K dues and late-payment surcharge as an income line.
RECURRING.quote: The trade receivables ... as on 31st March '26 stands at INR 1,299 crores as against INR 262 crores on 31st March '25.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Power is the DISCOMs' largest cost item, tariffs are set by CERC or by competitive bidding, and buyers simply refuse to contract — of 16 GW awarded as implementing agency only ~6 GW of PSAs were signed by May 2026, the opposite of customers who pay without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: the demand is not that much, frankly speaking, because ultimately, this power has to be purchased by the DISCOMs

LOWPRICE.rationale: Low realised prices (INR2.45–2.88/unit solar, Sadla at INR2.43) come without the cost culture or returns the pattern requires — the FY24 call books INR138.7 crore of impairments on wind/solar assets and FY26 shows INR174 crore more plus a INR258 crore loss at SGEL.
LOWPRICE.quote: we were compelled to sign PPA with the juvenile at the lower tariff and that's why we have to go for the impairment loss

PRICING.rationale: Tariffs are administered (CERC true-ups, CPSU cap of INR2.45) and the trajectory is deflationary — management explicitly cites falling tariffs in successive bids, and FY26 incentives went the wrong way (PAF-based incentive minus 40% in Q4) after CERC curbed the 110% availability incentive in 2023.
PRICING.quote: there is a decrease in the ... tariff with the subsequent bids which have come in the market

BRAND.rationale: Electricity sold wholesale at regulated or bid-discovered tariffs to UPPCL, GUVNL, Bihar and Assam DISCOMs; across all 15 calls there is no premium pricing, no A&P, and no brand-led share — only institutional awards (SCOPE, Suryacon) that carry no pricing consequence.
BRAND.quote: The power from this solar project is being sold to Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited.

FORWARD.rationale: SJVN remains a pure wholesale generator selling under PPAs/PSAs to state distribution companies; the only customer-facing activity (PM-Surya Ghar rooftop, 21.1 MW awarded) is a government-allotted implementation mandate, not owned distribution or pricing control.
FORWARD.quote: SJVN has been entrusted with the responsibility of implementing this scheme across three states

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Installed capacity did compound — 2,377 MW (Q4FY24) to 3,146 MW (Q2FY26) to 4,196 MW (FY26), with 16 GW awarded as a Renewable Energy Implementing Agency — but the growth is bid- and government-allocation-driven with no share metrics versus peers, and it was bought with rising debt (~INR30,000 crore), impairments and subsidiary losses, which the pattern explicitly discounts.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the total installed capacity of SJVNL stands at 4196 megawatts

CULTURE.rationale: Management is candid about bad news (impairments, 'you are very right' on revenue not tracking depreciation, admitting projects 'did not come in time'), but the promise-vs-delivery record across 2022–2026 is poor: Buxar Unit 1 promised June 2023 was COD'd November 2025, Arun-3 slipped from Dec 2023 to Dec 2028, the '12,000 MW by March 2026' pledge landed at 4,196 MW, and leadership churned through four chairmen in five years including three-month CMD stopgaps.
CULTURE.quote: We will be covering almost 12,000 megawatt by the March '26.

MOATTEST.rationale: The hydro assets pass a genuine replication test — Nathpa Jhakri/Rampur and pipeline sites like the 3,097 MW Etalin need finite river locations, forest/environment clearances and land acquisition taking a decade (Arun-III began before 2022 and commissions in FY29) — but the solar and thermal build, which is where all recent capacity comes from, is open-tender commodity capacity any funded developer can replicate, and regulated equity returns cap any excess earnings.
MOATTEST.quote: we are in the final stages of acquiring the land, which is a prerequisite to start the construction activity

RECURRING.rationale: Bearings generate a large installed-base replacement stream — vehicle aftermarket plus industrial distribution consistently ~34-36% of sales (Aug 2022) and ~36% in Feb 2025 with 18-20% aftermarket growth — but across all 16 calls there is no discussion of contracts, renewal rates, attach rates or customer advances/deferred revenue funding the business; working capital is a use of cash, not a source (May 2026: net working capital up 4.6%).
RECURRING.quote: The OEM share is around 55% for this quarter and after market is 36%

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales into the replacement market run through distributors, industrial part sellers and authorised dealers rather than end-user marketing (Feb 2025), but no call describes trade training programmes, prescriber loyalty or low end-customer price sensitivity — indeed the May 2026 call shows the channel forcing discounts.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we are kind of continue to onboard new industrial part sellers as well as engage new AID's across the market

TOLLROAD.rationale: Bearings are a small-cost, mission-critical component with formal qualification barriers — Indian Railways class E and class K approvals plus pilot orders before wagon makers switch (Aug 2022) — and EV insulation/high-speed bearings priced at a large multiple (May 2026); but management never claims customers don't negotiate, and the May 2026 discounting and 11-12% PBT guidance argue against true toll-road economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: We have approval Sandeep now for class E and also class K... We have also supplied a sample order to the wagon manufacturer.

LOWPRICE.rationale: SKF India positions on technology and premium bearings, not low price plus cost culture; no itemised cost savings or no-frills economics appear in any call, and the cost line has instead been a problem (high traded-product cost, gross margin down ~600bps in Q3 FY25, PBT margin guided down to 11-12% by May 2026).
LOWPRICE.quote: one of the reasons why it was lower was the high cost of the traded products

PRICING.rationale: Pricing power was visible only in the FY23-FY24 inflation pass-through window; from FY25 growth is explicitly volume-led with no price increases, and by FY26 the aftermarket is being defended with discounts — net aftermarket sales down on flat volume — the price-deflation outcome the pattern says must be avoided.
PRICING.quote: on a net sales point of view, it is a little bit down because of the discounts we offered to remain in the market and to beat the competition

BRAND.rationale: The SKF name carries enough equity to stretch into adjacent aftermarket categories (greases, sprockets, belts, steering/suspension) using existing retail access (Aug 2022), and customer awards from TVS, Honda and Suzuki are cited (May 2026); but no call discloses A&P spend, heritage positioning or brand-driven premium pricing, and brand did not prevent aftermarket discounting.
BRAND.quote: we already have access to the retail market where these will also get sold in addition to bearings

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a genuine product cadence — HUB 3 for EV LCVs, EV motor bearings, electric insulation and high-speed bearings with an order book stretching to 2030 (Aug 2022, May 2026) — and an in-house India engineering centre, but R&D spend is never disclosed or discussed as growing, and high margins are not shown funding it; margins are in fact falling.
INNOVATION.quote: certainly the performance of the electric vehicle products is much, much higher than the ICE vehicles

FORWARD.rationale: Growth toward the customer is pursued by adding third-party distributors and part sellers, not by owning it — across all calls there is no own-store count, franchise royalty, or D2C revenue discussion; the company remains a manufacturer selling through OEMs (66% of Q4 FY26 sales) and independent distribution (20%).
FORWARD.quote: original equipment manufacturers accounted for about two-third of our sales, that is about 66%, while distribution sales were about 20%

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Named, repeated share gains — 2-wheelers with Bajaj and Honda, general machinery OEM onboarding, railway freight entry via class E/K approval, and ~50% share of EV 2-wheeler business (Aug 2022, Feb 2025, May 2026) — but the gains are partly cyclical/order-driven, competitors are localising SRB/CRB capacity, and FY26 aftermarket share was defended with discounts and falling profitability, which the pattern discounts as worthless share.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we continue to gain market share with customers like Bajaj and Honda

CULTURE.rationale: Management is candid about shortfalls (localisation lag, transfer-pricing margin mechanics, unprofitable wind customers) and the demerger was executed transparently through the NCLT process; but leadership has churned heavily across the period — three MDs (Bhatnagar, Vasudevan, Sharma) and three CFO arrangements (Saraf, interim Arora, Holani) in four years — and the 2022 promise to 'play catch up' on industrial localisation was still stuck at ~40% in 2025.
CULTURE.quote: has localization moved at the pace we would have liked to over the past few years, no

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — multi-year OEM qualification, railway class approvals, an India technology centre and global manufacturing transfers — yet management concedes competitors are adding localised SRB/CRB capacity and that it must localise 'as much as possible' just to stay competitive, and roughly 60% of industrial product is still bought from the parent, so the advantage is not obviously un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: we're seeing new capacity is coming up from the competition on localizing SRB, CRBs... do you think immediately you might see some pressure on either market share or pricing

RECURRING.rationale: Management frames lower-margin OEM wins as a route to a higher-margin annuity aftermarket stream (bearings get replaced over the equipment's life), but there is no license/AMC/subscription revenue, no attach or renewal rates, and working capital is positive (18.7% of sales), not customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: The OEM business which we are winning, though it comes at a lower margin ... helps us in long-term aftermarket business

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The call discusses a distributor channel and key-account management with OEMs, but says nothing about professionals/prescribers specifying the product for an end payer, nor about trade training programmes.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Bearings are a small-cost, mission-critical component designed into customer platforms (tractor platform design, unitized rail bearing extending maintenance intervals from 1.0m to 1.2m km), which is classic toll-road engineering-in; but management explicitly describes intense competition and hard price negotiations with OEMs, which contradicts the 'customers pay without negotiating' element.
TOLLROAD.quote: it is a competitive environment and we do face lots of competition ... especially at the OEMs, I think the competition is intense

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost programme with itemised results — localization of components, capacity raised from 600k to 886k pieces with less manning, cost down 18%, setup time down 20% — but this is margin recovery toward 15%, not a low-price-plus-scale proposition passed to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: we increased capacity from 600,000 pieces to 886,000 pieces. Cost was reduced by almost 18%

PRICING.rationale: Price increases are being taken to recover FX and 3-4% input-cost escalation, and more readily in distribution than with OEMs — this is cost pass-through, not pricing above inflation; margin in fact fell from an adjusted 13.1% to 11.5% on mix.
PRICING.quote: With distributors, we will probably pass on a larger chunk ... with OEMs, it might be it's a little tougher, those are tougher negotiations

BRAND.rationale: The SKF name carries global engineering heritage and is valuable enough that the entity pays royalty and trademark fees on sales, but the call shows no A&P spend, no premium-pricing-plus-share evidence, and no brand-led adjacency.
BRAND.quote: the big components of other expense cost was one was around royalty and trademark

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular incremental product addition is evident — customer-specific tapered/cylindrical roller bearings designed at platform stage, a unitized bearing-housing-seal for commuter rail now being tested to 180 kmph, hybrid ceramic bearings for data-centre chillers, and 'two or three more product lines' added per quarter — but no R&D spend is disclosed or quantified.
INNOVATION.quote: almost every quarter two or three more product lines are added

FORWARD.rationale: The business moves the other way: 50-51% of sales are to OEMs and ~32-35% through third-party distributors, with no own stores, franchising or D2C; the quarter's distribution weakness was itself a distributor-credit problem, showing dependence on the channel.
FORWARD.quote: we made some corrections to distributors whose payments were outstanding

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Management claims share re-entry in wind, rail freight and tractors on the back of localization, with 91% q-o-q wind growth from ZF and Suzlon orders — but admits the share is being won at lower margin, which is exactly the 'share bought with profitability' caveat.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we are winning more share, but if you compare it to it comes at the cost of some amount of margin

CULTURE.rationale: The call is candid about one-off demerger costs, the mix-driven margin fall and the distributor receivables clean-up, and articulates an execution ethos plus a large organic capex commitment (INR 800 crore, new Pune plant by end-CY28); however, this is the first call of a newly demerged entity, so there is no record of promises delivered over years.
CULTURE.quote: people who have a high ratio of do versus say ... and are accountable to delivering the results

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real replication barriers — decades of SKF bearing technology, designed-in status from the platform design stage, and INR 800 crore of channel/plant capex over four to five years — but management's own description of intense OEM competition and margin pressure suggests the advantage is not one a funded rival could never rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: SKF Industrial worked right from the platform design stage ... and created a customer-specific offering

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 15 calls revenue is one-off project/tender supply with no licence, AMC, subscription or attach-rate discussion; management explicitly describes the business as project-based, and working capital is negative for the company (receivables of INR1,485 crores in FY26, funded by debt), the opposite of customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: Our orders are project based... It is when they win projects that's when they enter into contract with us.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Engineering sales are routed through ~200-250 global EPC contractors who buy on behalf of the paying utility, and the polymer business was built through a 25,000+ retailer/dealer network rather than end-consumer marketing; but there is no trade-training programme and pricing is set by competitive tender, so the low-price-sensitivity element is absent.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we work globally with about 200 to 250 global EPC contractors

TOLLROAD.rationale: Towers and EPC are a large share of a transmission project's cost and are awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding with 8-10 qualified manufacturers, so customers negotiate hard; the certification-style language (765/800 kV qualification, plant audits, test beds) is about entry qualification, not toll-like pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: Most of the major projects are conducted on TBCB, tariff-based competitive bidding

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost advantage is real and structural — the only end-to-end backward-integrated T&D player (rolling mills to EPC), largest India capacity scaling 300k to 450k tonnes with operating leverage lifting EBITDA margin from ~9.6% to 10.3% and ROCE ~21% on thin 3.7% PAT margins — but there is no itemised cost-savings culture or no-frills positioning discussed on the calls.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are the only company having backward integration of rolling mills, tower production, poles production, fasteners production and EPC construction in the same company

PRICING.rationale: Realisations are commodity- and tender-linked, not price-led: PVC suffered inventory losses when commodity prices fell (Nov 2022), and management repeatedly defends margins through firm/variable price contract mix and buffers rather than price increases, with raw materials ~60% of selling price.
PRICING.quote: we have a healthy mix of variable price and firm price contracts

BRAND.rationale: Management cites brand equity from the R&D centre and tower testing station and a sustained PVC brand-building push, but there is no heritage story, no disclosed A&P spend, and no evidence of premium pricing from the brand across the FY23-FY26 calls.
BRAND.quote: strengthening its brand equity in the global market

INNOVATION.rationale: There is genuine engineering capability investment — in-house design team offering cost-saving designs, an R&D centre, and Test Bed 2 commissioned in FY26 making it the only company globally with dual test beds at one location — but R&D spend is never disclosed, and there are no named new products with revenue impact in any year.
INNOVATION.quote: We successfully commissioned Test Bed 2, making us the only company global with dual test bed facilities at the same location

FORWARD.rationale: Skipper is integrated backwards (rolling mills, fasteners) not forwards; polymer goes through dealers and retailers with no own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C discussed in any of the 15 calls.
FORWARD.quote: backward integration of rolling mills, tower production, poles production

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Scale gains are evident — largest tower capacity in India expanding 300k to 450k tonnes (600k by FY28), record FY26 revenue of INR5,553 crores and order book of INR8,502 crores, plus a first North American utility order — but management gives no explicit market-share numbers, and the promised export share (50% of engineering revenue by FY23, 75% by FY24) collapsed to 10% of the order book by FY26.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have the largest capacity located in India

CULTURE.rationale: Family-run with stable leadership (Bansal brothers throughout), Great Place to Work for five consecutive years, conservative leverage (debt/equity 0.62x), and candid disclosure of misses — the 25% growth aspiration trimmed to 21%, capex slipping to Q1, and the INR260 crores receivables timing explained openly — but the FY23 promise of exports at 50-75% of engineering revenue and PVC at INR1,000 crores in two years (polymer only crossed INR500 crores in FY26) were both badly missed.
CULTURE.quote: in the beginning of the year, 25% is an aspiration. I believe we are not very far off from that

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are genuinely hard to rebuild — 15+ years of utility registrations and approvals across 70-80 markets, completed plant audits in North America, Europe, Australia, 765/800 kV qualification and the only dual test-bed site globally — but management itself names 8-10 domestic competitors plus KEC, Chinese and Turkish players, so a well-funded entrant is not structurally excluded.
MOATTEST.quote: it's a long process of registration and approvals which we have to take with the end customer, and we have been working on the international market for more than 15 years

RECURRING.rationale: Sky Gold is a B2B jewellery manufacturer with one-off order-based sales (7-20 day delivery windows) and no licence, AMC, subscription or renewal stream; far from customers funding it, the business is working-capital intensive — 75 days in Nov 2024, 59 days by Mar 2026, with cash from operations of negative INR272 crores before improving to INR45 crores negative.
RECURRING.quote: Our cash from operations improved from negative INR272 crores to near neutral operating cash flows of INR45 crores negative

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The retail chains (Malabar, Kalyan, CaratLane, Reliance, Damas) are the decision-makers while the end consumer pays, and Sky Gold invests heavily in that channel through co-creation, a 150-person merchandising/design team, a custom cell and design-selection 'strike rates' — but the retailer sells under its own brand, negotiates making charges hard, and there is no professional-training lock-in of the classic kind.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Our teams are constantly co -creating with the retailers like Malabar, GRT, PNG, Carat lane, Joyalukkas, Reliance, Adit ya Birla, Kalyan and many more.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Sky Gold supplies the retailer's core saleable product, not a tiny-but-critical input; gold is passed through back-to-back hedged and the company competes on design, delivery speed and making charges rather than any certification, standard or industry-body anchoring.
TOLLROAD.quote: We are fully back -to-back hedged, so price movements do not directly benefit us.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The model is genuinely low-margin/high-turn (gross margin 6% in FY24 to 8.45% in FY26, PAT margin 4.5%) with an itemised cost culture — gold loss cut from 1.5% to 0.5% worth 100bps of gross margin, jewellery made 20-30% lighter, delivery 30-40% faster, working capital 71 to 59 days — but management is using those savings to lift its own margins rather than to underprice, so the 'plus' side of the pattern is only emerging.
LOWPRICE.quote: he has reduced gold losses from 1.5% t o 0.5% and continues to drive further improvements

PRICING.rationale: There is evidence of repricing on differentiated 'monopoly' designs (making charges of Rs.300/gram to Rs.500-600/gram in Feb 2023) and a steady rise in gross margin, but management attributes the FY26 expansion mainly to gold-loss reduction, advanced-gold job work and value-added mix rather than price, and it plans 'strategic pricing' to win global share — so pricing power is real but narrow, not brand-based.
PRICING.quote: our making charges will grow from Rs.300 a gram to Rs.500 per gram and Rs.600 per gram

BRAND.rationale: Sky Gold sells white-label into retailers' brands; its own collection names (Tazim, Zenna, Aasma, Morni) are explicitly acknowledged as unknown to consumers, and the one consumer-brand attempt (Vesteria in the US with Varanium, Feb 2023) never reappears in later calls, with management confirming it has no retail ambition.
BRAND.quote: May be this brand is not popular among common customers but it is well known among our clients.

INNOVATION.rationale: Design-led incremental innovation is regular and monetised — 9 lakh design library, 25 jewellery projects, doubling the design/merchandising team to ~150, 3D printing/laser/direct casting, De Beers exclusive campaign partner, and value-added products rising from 4-5% to over 50% of revenue in three years — but no R&D spend is disclosed and gross margins are too thin to fund outsized R&D in the pattern's sense.
INNOVATION.quote: Value -added products now contributes more than 50% of the revenue compared to just 4% to 5%, 3 years ago.

FORWARD.rationale: Management repeatedly and explicitly rejects forward integration into retail, staying pure B2B manufacturing; the 2023 US D2C venture (Vesteria) disappeared from the narrative, and later 'downstream' moves are a dealer/distributor network and a Dubai Souk sales office, i.e. wholesale reach, not owned stores or franchising.
FORWARD.quote: right now, we are focusing totally on B2B manufacturing... Right now we are not in a mindset of retail.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, profitable share gain across the whole period: revenue from Rs.884 crores in 9M FY23 to a Q4 FY26 annualised run rate of INR7,650 crores, volumes 250 to 345+ kg/month, exports 1-2% to 11%, and a steadily lengthening named client roster (CaratLane, PN Gadgil, Reliance, Aditya Birla, Damas, Titan Gold) — accompanied by rising, not sacrificed, margins and falling working capital.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our Q4 FY26 performance significantly outpaced most industry peers
