CULTURE.rationale: Some promises were kept and bad news is disclosed — the Aug 2022 CFO openly accepted a poor quarter, the promised 600–700 wagons/month became 850 in FY24, and EPC losses and old bad debts were itemised — but there is heavy churn (Chairman Poddar and MD Gupta both exited; MD Mookerjee's role shifted), a chronically loss-making EPC arm whose demerger was announced then shelved, and the FY26 INR700 crore contingency provision routed against free reserves rather than P&L drew a statutory audit qualification.
CULTURE.quote: the statutory auditors have thus qualified their report... on account of provision being adjusted against the free reserves instead of taking it from the profit and loss account

MOATTEST.rationale: There are articulable barriers — RDSO prototype approval cycles, AAR certification of the foundry, an installed design base and scale to deliver 20,000-wagon orders — but the calls also show the advantage is fragile: named competitors out-earn them, output is hostage to third-party wheel-set supply, and the industry was being asked to double capacity to 30,000 wagons a year, which invites entrants.
MOATTEST.quote: lower wagon production levels... arising from continued wheel set availability constraints

RECURRING.rationale: Recurring streams exist — capital-light HMA management fees (INR 95 crores in FY26, guided to double-digit growth) and the new invite-only ARQ membership club targeting 2,000+ paying members across five cities — but management never discusses renewal rates, attach rates, deferred revenue or customer advances as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: the management fees for the full year we have done approx management fees of INR 95 crores

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The model is deliberately the opposite of intermediary-led: roughly two-thirds of revenue comes through direct channels and brand.com grew 153% YoY, with management citing the 'pull factor' of the brand rather than agent or trade recommendation.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our direct, which is a brand.com, which is the most efficient, and that shows the pull factor of the Leela brand has grown by 153%

TOLLROAD.rationale: A luxury hotel stay is a large discretionary purchase for the guest, not a sub-1% critical input to a customer's cost base; there is no certification, standards or regulatory anchoring anywhere in the four calls.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The entire strategy is premium price capture — RevPAR premium of ~INR 6,000 over the India luxury segment and a RevPAR index of 150 — the inverse of low-price-plus. Cost discipline exists (60% incremental-revenue flow-through, power cost cut to 3% of revenue) but funds margin, not lower prices.
LOWPRICE.quote: This translates into a RevPAR premium of approximately INR 6,000 over the India Luxury segment

PRICING.rationale: Every quarter shows ADR-led growth well above inflation without volume loss — 13% ADR in Q1FY26, 17% in Q3, 15% in Q4 — and in Q4FY26 they held 15% ADR growth even as war-driven occupancy fell, explicitly attributing it to pricing power; management repeatedly calls luxury demand inelastic.
PRICING.quote: our resilience on a pricing power and all that allowed us to mitigate that impact of occupancy through our ADR

BRAND.rationale: Four decades of heritage, NPS of 86 (12 points above the APAC luxury average), India's Best Hotel Group for the sixth consecutive year, Michelin Keys at three palaces — and the brand is being stretched into adjacencies (ARQ club, Leela Luxury Residences, Dubai, Coorg) while commanding an industry-leading RevPAR premium.
BRAND.quote: The Leela has now completed four decades of customer love and trust, four decades of true Indian luxury

INNOVATION.rationale: There is no R&D, but there is a regular, disclosed, profitable product-innovation cadence — seven new/refurbished F&B outlets, kids' clubs, spas, premium villas, ARQ — with named revenue impact (Jamavar +40%, Le Cirque +40%, Qube +27%) and a stated ~25% yield on cost.
INNOVATION.quote: targeted to deliver a projected yield on cost of approximately 25%

FORWARD.rationale: The company controls its own distribution — 300+ sales associates, nine regional sales offices, two-thirds direct revenue, website revenue up 72% then 153% — and uses third-party-funded HMAs (Jaisalmer, Hyderabad, Sikkim) as an asset-light, franchise-like growth channel; but it is an operator, not a manufacturer integrating forward.
FORWARD.quote: we have over 300 person sales associates, nine regional sales offices... which control nearly two-thirds of our revenue

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gains are quantified and repeated across calls — RevPAR index rising from 141 to 162 in Q3 and 150 for FY26, market share up 15 points (Apr–Nov 2025) and 11 points for FY26 — and are won on price and margin (EBITDA margin expanding 167bps to 49%), not bought with discounting.
SHAREGAIN.quote: In FY26, The Leela achieved 11 points increase in market share, with our RevPAR index strengthening to 150

CULTURE.rationale: Short public record (IPO June 2025) but within it promises were kept and beaten: mid-to-high-teens FY26 EBITDA guidance was raised then delivered at 19%, the Jaipur repositioning explicitly closed an IPO-time commitment, net debt halved to 1.6x, and one-off expenses and the March occupancy hit were disclosed with numbers rather than glossed over. No long-cycle track record or owned mistakes yet to confirm it.
CULTURE.quote: marks the completion of the commitment we had articulated at the time of our IPO

MOATTEST.rationale: The barrier is concrete and location-based: irreplaceable palace sites in micro-markets with essentially no new luxury supply — BKC has had no new hotel supply since 2011 and only 39 keys per million sq ft of office — combined with 40 years of brand equity a funded entrant cannot buy, and luxury supply growing at 6% against 11% demand.
MOATTEST.quote: The last supply that came in this micro market was in 2011. It's been nearly 15 years since there was a supply in this market

RECURRING.rationale: Management has consistently pushed services/AMC/spares off an installed base — services grew 30% in FY22 and ~20%+ thereafter, and the H/H-live digital platform was built specifically to reconnect with an installed base of which two-thirds had been lost; the projects business is also described as running on negative working capital. But service revenue is never quantified as a share, no attach or renewal rates are given, and by Q4 FY26 working capital had built up on collection delays rather than being customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: focus really deeply on the services part of our portfolio - bring digital in... have AMC capability, rapid spare parts... services have been growing for us at above 20%. Last year it grew 30%

TOLLROAD.rationale: Thermax sells boilers, FGD, chillers and EPC packages that are large capex line items bid competitively — not a sub-1% critical consumable; management itself says customers have choices everywhere and government work is pure L1 bidding.
TOLLROAD.quote: it is very competitive across the board. The kinds of products that we provide, our customers have choices

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is no cost-culture or itemised-savings narrative in any call; the stated strategy is the opposite — walk away from low-priced work (including the largest project in company history and sub-15% IRR solar deals) rather than win on price with high turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: we perhaps walked away from the biggest project in our history because the margins did not make sense

PRICING.rationale: Across four years margins are set by commodity cycles, not by the company: Q1 FY23 took a 6% hit to the bottom line from steel/styrene/nickel on fixed-price contracts, and in Q4 FY26 the same story repeats with styrene and construction-chemical raw materials squeezing the chemicals business. The only pricing edge claimed is a 2-3% 'last look' in niches, not price rises above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: the impact of commodity prices was quite substantial to the tune of 6% to our bottom line

BRAND.rationale: Thermax is repeatedly described as the trusted engineering partner customers give the last look to, supporting ~40% share in biomass/multifuel and 90%+ in on-site energy, and the name has stretched into solar, bio-CNG and data-centre cooling. But there is no heritage/A&P/consumer-brand machinery and the premium is worth only 'may be 2% to 3%'.
BRAND.quote: customers prefer to have some peace of mind, and they will come back and at least give us the last look. The last look may not be worth more than 2% to 3%

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a genuine, sustained innovation culture — a new-energy division from 2021, home-grown coal gasification worked on 6-7 years, bio-CNG, biomass-to-hydrogen, the H-live IoT platform, solar-plus-wind-plus-storage — but it is not the profitable, self-funding kind: gross margins are thin, R&D spend is never disclosed, and coal gasification still had zero orders in May 2026, three years after being showcased.
INNOVATION.quote: the technology solution hasn't become viable for the market players to progress on this front... there's nothing that on the order front that I have

FORWARD.rationale: Thermax has moved downstream from selling equipment to owning and operating it — TOESL biomass steam on pay-per-use and First Energy solar/wind on BOO, ~Rs.400 crores invested by FY23 and ~250 MW on ground by FY26. It is forward integration toward the customer, but capital-hungry and loss-making rather than the franchising/third-party-funded model, with a FY26 cost overrun after a contractor failure.
FORWARD.quote: we offer our steam and water treatment solutions on pay per use model... Solar, as an example, will be a loss making business for us this year

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Concrete share claims exist — ~40% in biomass/multifuel/waste-to-energy and 90%+ in the TOESL onsite-energy niche — plus new international wins (Dangote, a Rs.450 crores Middle East order, data-centre cooling and boilers). But the numbers are stated once rather than tracked rising over time, and consolidated FY26 revenue grew only 3-4%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: here in India we have maybe a 90% plus market share in a TOESL kind of a business

CULTURE.rationale: Bad news is disclosed promptly and owned (FGD losses reserved, chemicals 'went through hell', First Energy cost overrun, the FY26 working-capital build acknowledged when an analyst spotted it), and capital discipline is real — walking away from thin-margin projects and investing for 'the next 20 to 30 years'. Against that, several multi-year promises are undelivered: 10% product margins, coal gasification commercialisation, and the profitability ramp in green solutions.
CULTURE.quote: I very strongly believe that this is a great time to build a Thermax for the next 20 to 30 years, not just the next two to three years

MOATTEST.rationale: Management explicitly disclaims any proprietary technology a competitor cannot access; the advantage cited is execution trust and engineering reputation worth a 2-3% last look, which a well-funded engineering competitor could rebuild — and the repeated inability to hold pricing through commodity cycles confirms the weak barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: we are not at all in anything relating to a tech base or anything that would come back and say that we have access to any unique technology which is not available to anybody at all

RECURRING.rationale: Not a licence/AMC model, but the forex prepaid-card float is explicitly a customer-funded, negative-working-capital stream that management treats as operating income (Aug 2024: INR210 crore incremental float; Feb 2026: ~60% of other income from FDs on forex float; May 2026: INR16bn float). Sterling's genuinely recurring membership annuity was deliberately sunset in July 2023, weakening the pattern.
RECURRING.quote: Our float as we speak, stands at about INR 16 billion on a total prepaid card load volumes of USD 764 million.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The education-forex franchise runs through counsellors and NBFC lenders who steer students, and 73-80% of travel revenue is B2B through agents/corporates rather than end-consumer marketing — but there is no professional-training or switching-cost programme described across the 16 calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Our relationships with over 800 marquee education counsellors across the country gave us a genuine on-the-ground advantage.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Travel and forex are a large, visible share of the customer's spend, gross margins run ~1.5% in forex and ~3.3% EBIT in travel, and management repeatedly concedes price to competition (Feb 2026 Desert Adventures) and re-engineers Europe products to be 'more affordable' — the opposite of un-negotiated toll pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: Desert Adventures, faced stiff competitive intensity and muted demand owing to external factors, which led to lower business volumes. And consequently, we had to make a tactical progress in terms of our margin

LOWPRICE.rationale: A real, itemised cost culture runs through the whole record — 33-45% payroll/cost reduction held post-COVID (Aug 2022), DEI's ZBB-ZBO, Sterling's 18% fixed-cost cut, 'prudent cost and margin management' in FY26 — but it is margin defence, not a low-price scale proposition passed to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are talking about cost savings very well in terms of payroll, between 37% and 45%

PRICING.rationale: Sterling shows real pricing power (ARR up 5% then 12% y/y with occupancy also rising, RevPAR +16-17%) and forex EBIT margins expanded to 41-48%; but the core outbound travel business is price-taking — long-haul volumes fell as airfares rose 30-50% and management is repricing Europe downward to hold volume.
PRICING.quote: ARR increased 5% year-on-year to INR6,976 on a consolidated basis in Q3, that demonstrates our strength in holding and increasing our pricing propositions

BRAND.rationale: Genuine heritage assets — Thomas Cook's century-plus name and SOTC's 75th year (Aug 2024) — are cited by management as a core strategic pillar from the first call onward, and Sterling's TripAdvisor rankings evidence trust; but there is little disclosure of sustained A&P spend or brand-led premium pricing in the travel business.
BRAND.quote: we will always focus on interacting with our customers and leveraging the strong brand recall that we have across SOTC and Thomas Cook, both of which have a long history.

INNOVATION.rationale: Named product launches recur every year — VKYC and TCPay (FY25), TACY AI avatar and Rahi (Q3 FY26), TravSure and an industry-first visa-rejection cover, Blinkit forex-card delivery across 12 cities, Sterling ONE contributing INR1,000mn — but no R&D spend is disclosed and gross margins are too thin to fund innovation-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: We launched our summer Europe packages driven by our AI-powered digital avatar of Thomas Cook - TACY. We also launched Rahi - our own AI-enabled travel automation system

FORWARD.rationale: Consistent build-out of owned distribution — franchises, owned outlets, airport counters, Tier-2/3 store additions, and digital penetration rising from 21% to 23% with app bookings up 4.9x — plus Sterling's own proprietary platform; but it is a services group extending distribution rather than a manufacturer capturing downstream margin, and D2C is still a minority of sales.
FORWARD.quote: We have expanded our reach by opening 5 new franchises, 1 owned outlet and 1 airport counter during the quarter and also improved our digital penetration, which currently stands at 23%

SHAREGAIN.rationale: The FY26 calls benchmark performance explicitly against RBI LRS industry data and show repeated gains: retail forex +25% while industry travel fell 6%, education +39% against a 22% industry contraction (Feb 2026), and full-year holiday +13%/education +17%/remittance +19% against industry declines of 3%/22%/5% (May 2026), plus 8 new corporate accounts each quarter toward 8,000 clients.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Despite the contraction in the overall student education segment, we gained market share.

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable and long-tenured (Menon, Iyer, Nandy, Modi across the full period), guidance is given quarter-by-quarter and then measured against outcome, and bad news is disclosed promptly and specifically — the FTI bankruptcy provision, the Bangalore Airport exit, Sterling's ramp-cost margin dip, the Labour Code and GST ITC one-offs — with Sterling run debt-free with INR3.4bn cash through the cycle.
CULTURE.quote: we had guided to about 63% recovery when we spoke to you all the last time around, but our recovery on this front has been much higher

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-rebuild assets exist — an RBI-authorised forex network with a INR16bn float, a 28-currency prepaid card, 800 counsellor relationships and DMS entities in ~19 countries — but management articulates the defence as portfolio diversity rather than a barrier, and FY26's 14% EBT decline on geopolitical shocks shows the core travel business is exposed, not insulated.
MOATTEST.quote: the ability to manage movements in the performance of companies across the group through this diversity is a strength that Thomas Cook has carried for a long time

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is routed through franchisees and prescribing doctors rather than end-consumer marketing, with sustained investment in the channel — doctor advisory boards, 9 doctor meets and 256 doctor lab visits in FY26, 13 franchisee meets, and a specialty 'technical sales team to drive deeper doctor-led engagement'. But the classic low-price-sensitivity condition is absent: affordability and slab discounts to franchisees are the explicit value proposition.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The findings revealed that 9 out of 10 doctors trust Thyrocare reports and confidently recommend our services to their patients.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Certification language exists (CAP, NABL, 'only 2% of labs in India are NABL' accredited), but the commercial reality contradicts toll-road economics: Thyrocare competes as the cheapest B2B lab and runs an explicit slab-based discount structure for franchisees, i.e. price is negotiated, not simply paid.
TOLLROAD.quote: we continue to actually have one of the lowest prices as a B2B player in the country

LOWPRICE.rationale: Low price plus quality accreditation is the stated core across all 17 calls (2022 through Jul 2026), and it converts into returns via scale and turns — 210mn tests in FY26 'higher than some of our biggest competitors combined', hub-and-spoke operating leverage, gross margin 70%→74.7%, EBITDA 23% (FY23)→32%, ROCE 15%→34%, zero debt.
LOWPRICE.quote: All our efforts on our value proposition is towards ensuring low cost to the patient, assurance on quality of testing through our certifications

PRICING.rationale: The model is built on price reduction, not price escalation: 'affordable option to all patients' is repeated verbatim every call, the FY24 change was a pay-for-performance discount slab structure, and in FY26 they 'normalized our pricing into the insurance segment', which slowed that segment's growth. Margin gains came from supplier negotiation, volume leverage and mix (Jaanch, specialty), not from realised price increases.
PRICING.quote: This year, we have normalized our pricing into the insurance segment, and therefore, the growth has been slower in this segment.

BRAND.rationale: Deliberate multi-year brand build — 2022 rebrand off the thyroid imagery, Aarogyam as flagship with Jaanch and Her Check as adjacencies, Madhuri Dixit signed as ambassador in FY26, and awards for 'Best Diagnostic Lab Chain' and 'India's most trusted customer-focused diagnostic brand 2026'. But the pattern's second leg is missing: share gain comes with low pricing, not a price premium, and A&P spend is never quantified.
BRAND.quote: we onboarded Madhuri Dixit as the brand ambassador for Thyrocare, which is an important step in strengthening brand recall and consumer trust

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular, named menu expansion delivered over the period — test menu roughly 700 (Aug 2022) to 1,375+ (Jul 2026), in-house histopathology, Phadia allergy platform with 250+ SKUs, NGS/BioFire/HPLC, and a phased genomics entry starting with NIPT, plus published data studies (Bharat Aarogyam Score, fever study). No R&D spend is ever disclosed and innovation is adoption of vendor platforms rather than proprietary development.
INNOVATION.quote: Our test menu has increased nearly fivefold to more than 1,375 tests.

FORWARD.rationale: Growth is funded by third-party franchisees who own the collection points — the base grew from 2,700 at takeover to 11,700 by Q1 FY27, with a shift toward franchise store fronts and larger franchisees — but Thyrocare stays deliberately B2B, with no owned-store economics, no royalty disclosure and no D2C revenue share discussed.
FORWARD.quote: our active franchise network has grown to over 11,700, a fourfold increase versus when we took over

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gain from a low base: franchisees 2,700→11,700, labs 17→44, volumes compounding at 13–28% y/y, growth 'higher than industry average', plus Tanzania and Malaysia expansion — and importantly it was not bought with profitability, since EBITDA margin rose from 23% to 32% and ROCE from 15% to 34% over the same window.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we processed 210 million tests in FY '26, which grew by 23% year-on-year. It's important to contextualize that this volume is higher than some of our biggest competitors combined.

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in the early calls were delivered later — 15 NABL labs targeted in Aug 2022 became 25 of 30 by Jul 2024 and all owned labs by Jul 2026; TAT targets fell from 4 hours average to 3.37 hours; bad news is disclosed plainly (three-year non-COVID CAGR of only 5%, weakness in North India, radiology revenue -6%, the Q4 FY26 partnership dip quantified at ~INR4 crores). Rahul Guha has led throughout the five years with a conservative balance sheet (net cash INR230cr+, zero debt) and explicit ROCE measurement, though CFO turnover (Salvi→Jagnani→Gupta) and board churn are a caveat.
CULTURE.quote: Return on capital employed has also improved from 15% in FY 23 to 34% in FY 26.

MOATTEST.rationale: There is a real articulable barrier — a national network of 44 labs putting a lab within 150km of any pin in India, 11,700 collection points, 2,000+ phlebotomists and 100% NABL accreditation when only 2% of Indian labs hold it, all built over five years and giving volume 'higher than some of our biggest competitors combined'. But this is density and cost scale that a well-funded entrant could rebuild over time; there is no time-locked, data-locked or location-locked asset of the kind the test demands.
MOATTEST.quote: If you drop a pin anywhere in India, you will find a Thyrocare pathology lab within 150 kilometers

RECURRING.rationale: No discussion of licence fees, AMC/service revenue, renewals, attach rates, installed base or customer advances funding the business; the only adjacent items are a Tamil Nadu royalty arrangement and a Spaceman 'usership agreement', neither framed as recurring revenue economics.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is created by consumer-facing brand building and A&SP, not by an expert intermediary prescribing the product; across all calls the levers cited are 360-degree communication, packaging and state excise route-to-market, with no trade-training or professional-channel lock-in.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we also have an aggressive digital campaign which we have launched with a 360 degree of communication strategy

TOLLROAD.rationale: TI sells a discretionary branded consumer spirit, not a small-but-critical input into a customer's cost base; the calls show the opposite dynamic — competitor-driven price corrections and state excise changes that move consumer prices by Rs 20 per nip.
TOLLROAD.quote: we had to take a price correction in Andhra Pradesh in order to maintain our competitive position in the state

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, itemised cost culture — packaging optimisation, Rs 10 crore/annum bottling savings from Prag, 250-350bps of identified cost savings on the acquired IB business — but the strategy is premiumisation and P&A mix, not low price with high asset turns, so only the cost-discipline half of the pattern is present.
LOWPRICE.quote: TI expects savings in bottling costs to the tune of INR 10 crore per annum

PRICING.rationale: NSR has risen through mix and premiumisation (Rs 1,157 to Rs 1,250 in FY24; ex-IB Rs 1,161 to Rs 1,209 by Q3 FY26), but pricing is state-administered rather than company-controlled, and TI was forced into a ~Rs 200/case cut in Andhra in Q3 FY25 that de-grew revenue — the price-deflation outcome the pattern warns against.
PRICING.quote: The price correction in Andhra blended level on a state basis would be around Rs. 200, reduction

BRAND.rationale: Repeated across all four calls: a 1933 family heritage, Mansion House as India's largest brandy crossing 10 million cases in FY26, brand equity proven when Andhra secondaries grew 8% during a primary-volume collapse, and consistent stretch into adjacencies (Flandy, Monarch luxury brandy, Mansion House Whisky, Seven Islands) plus the acquired 30-year Imperial Blue legacy.
BRAND.quote: secondary volumes in Andhra Pradesh grew at 8%, indicating strong brand equity for our products

INNOVATION.rationale: A named new launch essentially every year with revenue impact — Flandy flavoured brandy (FY23), Blue Lagoon gin relaunch, Monarch Legacy Edition (FY25), Seven Islands pure malt (FY26) — and an explicit NPD pipeline, but no disclosed R&D spend, no share-of-industry-R&D claim, and management concedes packaging and distribution matter as much as the blend.
INNOVATION.quote: we do have an NPD pipeline in place

FORWARD.rationale: Alcohol route-to-market is state-controlled and TI sells through corporations and distributors; there are no owned stores, franchising or D2C, and the integration investment (Prag bottling, Shrirampur ENA distillery) runs backwards toward supply rather than forwards toward the consumer.
FORWARD.quote: This investment will enable us to expand our capacity from around 6 lakh cases per annum to 36 lakh cases per annum

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit, rising share numbers across the whole period and cited profitably: brandy share 14-15% to 20% over five years and IMFL share 2% (FY17) to 4.3% (FY23), Telangana 6.8% to 7.4%, southern IMFL 5.8% to 6.2%, then ~32% and ~40% P&A share in the South post-Imperial Blue — achieved alongside EBITDA growth and debt reduction, not bought with margin.
SHAREGAIN.quote: TI continues to be largest P&A IMFL player in Southern India with a market share of close to 40%

CULTURE.rationale: Fourth-generation family business with a documented promise-to-delivery record: gross debt cut from ~Rs 1,200 crore (2019) to Rs 45 crore with net cash by Q3 FY25, the Q3 FY26 TSMA-exit commitment met in Q4, Prag capex delivered as guided; bad news is disclosed promptly (AP price cut, April integration disruption, Telangana receivables), though four CFOs in five years and a Rs 2,100 crore acquisition loan temper the conservatism claim.
CULTURE.quote: we had mentioned that TI will exit the TSMA for significant operations by the end of Q4 FY26, and we have delivered on that

MOATTEST.rationale: Real, hard-to-rebuild assets exist — state licences, a South-India distribution network, aged-spirit brands and Imperial Blue's 30-year legacy that cost Rs 3,442 crore to buy rather than build — but management offers no articulable barrier of its own ("is there any secret sauce? Well, I can't tell you"), and Maharashtra's MML rule change de-grew IB's relevant segment 25%, showing regulation can erode the advantage.
MOATTEST.quote: the IB brand has a 30-year legacy and is the 3rd largest selling whisky in India

RECURRING.rationale: Across all five calls the business is described purely as component/vehicle sales — no attach rates, AMC/service revenue share, renewal rates or customer advances are ever discussed; the only services reference (Feb 2026) confirms service revenue is negligible and merely an ambition at subsidiary CG Power, where they are still recruiting a team to start it in FY27.
RECURRING.quote: services of CG Power should be like a 1%-2% business

TOLLROAD.rationale: Management repeatedly stresses that OEM qualification cycles make business sticky once approved (May 2025 and Nov 2025 on the new Nasik/large-diameter lines needing 3-4 months of customer approvals; US exports holding up on OEM business while distributor sales fell), and industrial chains hold ~50% of a Rs.900 Cr niche — but there is no 'tiny share of customer cost', certification-standard or pricing-immunity language, and the May 2026 call shows they must negotiate cost inflation with customers.
TOLLROAD.quote: that is how it gives you advantage in this kind of a time, where the business is sticky for some time

PRICING.rationale: Across the five calls pricing is pure cost pass-through with a lag, not price increases above inflation: Q4 FY26 revenue growth is stated as equal to volume growth ('no major price movements'), and fuel-cost inflation has to be 'taken up with customers' with an admitted recovery lag; in EVs, GST cuts on ICE forced them to defend on TCO and cut cost structures rather than price.
PRICING.quote: commodity price increase, we get it from our customers because we have contracts in place, which comes with sometimes a one or two quarter lag

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur each year — 4x2 truck variant and battery-swap tech (Nov 2025), tipper, upgraded Super Auto, e-bikes/fitness cycles driving mobility margin gains, new medical product development — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and the flagship innovation bet (TI Clean Mobility) has lost Rs.412 Cr in FY25 with breakeven repeatedly pushed out.
INNOVATION.quote: in the month of September we introduced a 4 by 2 variant. We also introduced a swap technology

FORWARD.rationale: Only in the EV arm does the company move toward the customer — direct selling for heavy trucks and a self-built dealer network scaling from 85 toward 120 three-wheeler dealers (May 2025) — while the core engineering/metal-formed business remains a Tier-1 OEM supplier; the FY26 move to take over the body-in-white supplier's plant is backward, not forward, integration.
FORWARD.quote: for the truck business, it is a direct selling model that we are deploying at this point of time

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Genuine share strength is claimed in the core (auto chains 'market share is intact, rather, it is a marginal improvement', ~50% of the Rs.900 Cr industrial-chain market, improved domestic tube share, double-digit engineering volume growth in FY26), but the newer bets contradict it — three-wheeler share was ceded to Mahindra on admitted product and supply failures, EV truck share slipped from ~83% of industry deployments in FY25 to 'over 40%' by Feb 2026, and Shanthi Gears and TI Medical shrank or stagnated.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Industrial market size is about 900 Crores and we do almost maybe let us say close to 50% share in that.

CULTURE.rationale: Strong candour and conservatism — Vellayan Subbiah owns the TI2/EV misjudgement unprompted in Feb 2026, refuses to give breakeven numbers because 'I have given an estimate in the past and I have been wrong', ROIC is held at 44-49% with FCF at 100% of PAT in FY26 and steady dividends under a long-tenured Murugappa promoter family — but the delivery record against old promises is weak: the Rs.1,000 Cr railway contract slipped from Q4 FY26 to FY27 to 'two or three quarters from now', medical CE certification and EV operational breakeven both slipped by years.
CULTURE.quote: I made some mistakes, kind of I have not perhaps performed as well as we could have in certain segments.

MOATTEST.rationale: The core tube business shows a real, articulable barrier — multi-year OEM product-approval cycles (even existing customers must re-approve the new Nasik and large-diameter lines over 3-4 months) plus capacity built 'two to three years ahead' — yet the company's own EV experience shows how fast well-funded entrants arrive (seven to eight players in electric trucks within two years), and nothing in the calls points to time-, data- or location-based barriers a copycat could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: plant capacity utilization almost two to three years ahead

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls the model is one-off product sales (drums, IBCs, cylinders, pipes) with no licence, AMC, subscription or attach-rate revenue ever mentioned; working capital is positive and long — 120 days four years ago, ~98-99 days in Feb 2026 with 70-75 days receivables — so customers do not fund the business.
RECURRING.quote: the working capital cycle time was 120 days, which is now reduced to almost 98 to 99 days

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct B2B to industrial buyers (chemicals, pharma, FMCG, OMCs) on negotiated pricing formulas, not routed through prescribing professionals; the only channel language is ordinary distributors for the new fire extinguisher, with no trade-training or professional-reputation lock-in anywhere in the record.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We operate on a B2B model serving industries like specialty chemicals, FMCG and pharmaceutical with long-term industry relationships on a mutually agreed pricing formula

TOLLROAD.rationale: Packaging is a small but operationally critical input for chemical/pharma customers, and the composite business is anchored in certification (PESO approvals, CPRI certification, OMC acceptance, Indian Institute of Packaging quality norms, PCR recycling compliance) — but the repeated admission that prices are reset monthly/quarterly with polymer shows customers do negotiate, which is not toll-road behaviour.
TOLLROAD.quote: newer sizes being developed for which the respective PESO approvals are being pursued

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, itemised and delivered cost culture — solar PPAs across five states now yielding ~INR11 crores annualised with ~1-year payback, unit consolidation, robotic automation, plant siting next to customers to cut logistics, finance cost heading from INR90-100 crores to INR25-30 crores — but management frames these as margin/ROCE levers, not as savings passed to price to win volume, and asset turns are modest with a ~98-day cycle.
LOWPRICE.quote: Power purchase agreements across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and West Bengal have already started generating annualized benefits of about INR11 crores

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is explicit cost pass-through, not pricing power: revenue repeatedly grows slower than volume when polymer falls (9M FY26 volume +15% vs revenue +11%), and management's commitment is to absolute EBITDA per tonne rather than to raising realisations above inflation.
PRICING.quote: The gap is primarily due to lower of the raw material cost... price revisions are implemented through mutually agreed monthly or quarterly mechanisms

BRAND.rationale: Sixteen calls contain no A&P spend, no heritage or consistency promise, no premium pricing and no consumer-facing brand; competitive position is described in plant, approval and cost terms, and 92% of sales are B2B on formula pricing.
BRAND.quote: almost 93% business came by B2B there is slight increase or decrease we have a system of passing to the customer

INNOVATION.rationale: Product development is regular, named and increasingly commercialised — Type IV CNG/LPG cylinders, 250-litre CNG, oxygen cylinders (approved 2/4/9 kg), hydrogen drone cylinders, 6/9 kg composite fire extinguishers, automated IBC lines, OPz/VRLA batteries — and it shows up in mix (value-added share 20% in FY23 to 29-30% in FY26 at ~18-20% contribution); but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, several items (fire extinguisher, 14.2 kg LPG) have slipped for years, and the innovation buys mix, not pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: value added products recorded a strong growth of 18%... the contribution of value-added products to total sales increased to 29%, up from 27%

FORWARD.rationale: Mostly a pure manufacturer selling B2B, but two genuine forward moves exist: backward-then-forward control via the wholly owned Time Ecotech recycling plants, and a Board-committed JV with private gas distributors to build an independent LPG distribution network; no own stores, franchising or D2C revenue is disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: Board has committed pursuing joint venture tie-ups with private gas distributors to establish an independent LPG distribution network

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Consistent double-digit volume growth (13-16% every year, ahead of the packaging industry) plus local-manufacturing international expansion — 10-11 countries, fifth US plant in Georgia, Saudi Dammam next — and claimed #1 in India industrial packaging and composite cylinders; but management never gives explicit market-share percentages or share versus named competitors, so the gain is asserted rather than evidenced.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we are, of course, the leading player in this country and with our presence in about 11 countries globally. We are there in the top 3 even on a global front

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured founder-led team (Vageria/Thyagarajan across all 16 calls), 30 years of unbroken dividends, a deleveraging promise largely delivered (debt INR647 crores to INR266 crores) and openly disclosed misses (FY26 ROCE 18.9% versus the 20% target); against that, the ROCE ladder promised in Aug 2024 for March '25 and March '26 arrived late, the Middle East disinvestment slipped from FY23 into FY25, and 'debt-free in 6 months' (Feb 2026) became '12 to 18 months' one quarter later.
CULTURE.quote: FY '26 ROCE is 18.9% versus 20% target, reflecting short-term impact of QIP-led automation investments

MOATTEST.rationale: The composite-cylinder side has real replication barriers — PESO/CPRI/OMC approvals, a decade of OMC supply history, and a 1,080-cascade automated plant — but the 75% of revenue that is drums, jerry cans, pails and PE pipes is commodity conversion whose stated advantages (proximity to customers, automation, power cost) a well-funded entrant could rebuild in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: we have set up a fully automated CNG plant at Morai with a total capacity of 1,080 cascades

RECURRING.rationale: There is a genuine replacement/MRO annuity behind the installed base (distribution 17-19% of sales every year, plus embedded service presence inside customer plants), but across all 15 calls management never discusses licence fees, AMC contracts, attach rates, renewals or customer advances/deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: we must be the only company in India which run more than 26, 27 roll shop inside the steel companies... we are 24*7 – de-choking, choking, mounting, demounting

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales go through OEM engineering approval and industrial distributors, not a reputation-bearing professional who prescribes for a paying end customer; management explicitly says the retail-facing aftermarket channel is price-driven and commoditising, the opposite of low price sensitivity.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: auto aftermarket in India is always going after -- especially believe in going after cheap bearings... going to be commoditized to a large extent

TOLLROAD.rationale: Across Dec-2022, May-2024 and May-2026 calls the bearing is described as a small but mission-critical component whose failure is unacceptable (rail safety, aviation, steel roll shops), sold on life and engineering rather than price, and locked in by PPAP/customer approval and testing regimes in a handful-of-players industry.
TOLLROAD.quote: today morning, only a cement customer was telling me that they see more life out of Timken bearing. So we sell value and engineering

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly refuses volume bought with price, walks away from part numbers it cannot price profitably, and positions against the cheap end of the market; the model is premium engineering with asset turns of only ~2x, not scale-driven low-cost.
LOWPRICE.quote: We don't want to kill our margins by buying the business. We have been always careful about that.

PRICING.rationale: Price realisation is a standing management effort — pushed even when steel prices softened (May 2024) — but the May 2026 call shows recovery is negotiated, lagged and incomplete rather than routine above-inflation increases, with OEMs resisting.
PRICING.quote: we have only begun passing it on, we are at 10% currently... 90% has to be achieved on realizing this price

BRAND.rationale: The Timken name carries real industrial heritage and specification pull (40-year incumbency, global aerospace/rail pedigree, the acquired ABC brand run alongside), but there is no A&P spend, consumer-style distributor leverage or brand-stretch story on any call.
BRAND.quote: every time a Boeing aircraft lands anywhere in the world, it is on Timken bearing s

INNOVATION.rationale: Technology is continuously refreshed — sealing, greasing and metallurgy upgrades for rail, Industry 4.0/robotic lines at Bharuch, 100+ new part introductions in FY26 — but it is imported from the parent and the Indian entity discloses no R&D spend or pipeline economics of its own.
INNOVATION.quote: whether it is sealing technology, whether it i s greasing technolog y, whether it is the material fin ds of it etc., so that there will be a life of these bearings go up

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Leadership is asserted in tapered roller bearings and ~50% of Indian rail, and the INR720 crore Bharuch plant is an explicit import-substitution play into a ~INR4,000 crore SRB/CRB market, but no rising share series versus named competitors is given and the ramp has run behind plan (INR80 crore FY26 revenue, ~30% utilisation versus a 45% exit target).
SHAREGAIN.quote: this market size both put together is INR 4,000 crores market, and we have almost a running rate supply chain available in India

CULTURE.rationale: Sanjay Koul led the calls consistently from 2022 through FY26, the CRB/SRB plant promised in Nov-2022 was tracked on schedule in May-2024 and capitalised and shipping by FY26, capital is committed only against an explicit return test (asset turn >2x), and shortfalls are admitted plainly rather than spun.
CULTURE.quote: It's difficult to tell the exact percentage... I would say we are not definitely 45%, I would say at some 30% level

MOATTEST.rationale: Real time-based barriers exist — decades of application knowledge, parent technology, multi-year PPAP and customer/rail approval cycles, and INR720 crore state-of-the-art plants — but these are barriers an already-funded global peer (SKF, Schaeffler) has also cleared, so it is a strong incumbency rather than an un-replicable position.
MOATTEST.quote: each part has to go through a proper PPAP. And we have to have Timken approvals and then it has to go through the customer approvals

RECURRING.rationale: The catalogue behaves like an annuity — management repeatedly says new content is only 10-15% of revenue while the back-catalogue supplies the rest, and licensing/distribution deals (Warner, YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Sony Publishing) renew periodically with little incremental capital. But there is no attach-rate, deferred-revenue or customer-advance funding discussion; content is paid for upfront and expensed, so customers do not fund the business.
RECURRING.quote: the new content at any time would contribute around 10% to 15% of the revenue and the catalogue would be the remaining

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Revenue is driven by end-consumer streaming and views on YouTube/Spotify/Instagram, not by a professional intermediary recommending the product; across all 17 calls there is no trade channel, installer/prescriber or training-programme discussion.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our cumulative YouTube subscriber base increased to 158.3 million

TOLLROAD.rationale: Tips sits in a rational oligopoly of Indian labels whose catalogue platforms must license, and it claims unique structural positioning ('the only ones' with Warner and Sony Publishing distribution tie-ups); but content royalties are a very large, not tiny, share of a streaming platform's cost base, and there is no certification/standards or regulatory anchoring, so the core toll-road test fails.
TOLLROAD.quote: We are the only ones who have the partnership with Warner Music as a distributor, Sony Music Publishing as a distributor

LOWPRICE.rationale: This is a 65-70% EBITDA-margin, high-margin IP business, not a low-price/high-turns model; the only cost language is tough negotiation on content acquisition, not a scale-driven cost culture passing savings to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: we have maintained around 65% to 70% of EBITDA margin, on a normalized level for a full year

PRICING.rationale: Tips does not set the price of its own output — per-stream realisation is fixed by platforms (India ₹0.04-0.10 vs ₹0.50-0.90 globally) and it suffered YouTube CPM deflation in FY23 — but it does negotiate hard at contract renewals (the 5-year YouTube fight, Warner, the pending Shorts deal) and benefits passively from Spotify/YouTube subscription price hikes.
PRICING.quote: in India currently the subscription price is also lower and the overall percentage revenue is around 15%. So that's primarily the gap

BRAND.rationale: There is a genuine heritage story — a repertoire built from 1988 that spans two generations and is now marketed as 'new retro', plus a 158mn-subscriber YouTube identity that gives distribution leverage — but there is no sustained A&P spend, no premium pricing and adjacency stretch is limited to a related-party film arm.
BRAND.quote: Tips is the appropriate player for these two generations because when your parents were young, they listened to my music and you've grown up on my music

INNOVATION.rationale: Content spend functions as the R&D analogue — disclosed and rising (₹55cr FY23 → ₹80cr FY25 → ₹90-100cr FY27 guidance), with named releases each year carrying revenue impact (Crew, Ishq Vishk Rebound, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai) and a pipeline slate — but this is acquisition of third-party output, not proprietary R&D dominance, and the only technology initiative (the Pulse ERP) was described as 'very minimal' in cost.
INNOVATION.quote: the overall content budget for the year would be in that range of INR90 crores to INR100 crores

FORWARD.rationale: Tips owns its consumer-facing channels and monetises directly — its own YouTube channels with 158mn subscribers, direct claiming of revenue on third-party uses of its music, and music-supply into group-produced Tips Films titles — but it still routes international and much digital distribution through Warner and the platforms rather than owning the storefront.
FORWARD.quote: YouTube gives us authority and we have that tool with us. We can strike it down immediately or we can claim monies on even that as well

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has persistently outrun the industry — the stated 2022 ambition to become the 'top third music company in India' has been backed by 20-40% revenue growth against a single-digit industry, but management never discloses explicit market-share figures or share versus named competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the industry report, I can only say that the growth is in single digit for this year. But for us, we are seeing a strong traction, and we continue to maintain our guidance of 20% growth

CULTURE.rationale: Family-controlled, stable leadership (Kumar Taurani chairman across all 17 calls), deliberately conservative accounting (entire content cost expensed the day a song releases rather than capitalised), habitual under-promising — guided 30/30 and delivered 61% PAT growth in Q1FY25, guided 25% and delivered 30% in FY26 — and consistent return of surplus cash (₹46.6cr buyback FY25, ₹166cr dividend FY26, commitment to return all of FY26's ₹217cr PAT) with ₹345cr net cash and no debt. Bad news is disclosed plainly: the postponed film that dragged content cost, the Shorts view decline, the CEO's exit with no replacement found.
CULTURE.quote: Yes I want to achieve that target. But for the comfort of the people like you, our investors, I don't want to over-promise. So let's keep the target at present 20-20%

MOATTEST.rationale: The moat is a time-stamped copyright library — ~38-42k songs acquired from 1988 onwards, including the 90s Hindi repertoire that a well-funded newcomer cannot rebuild at any price because the recordings and the era are finite; management explicitly attributes growth to this catalogue call after call, with 2026 examples like a Khuda Gawah track doing 3 billion Instagram views. Management concedes rising competition from cash-rich international entrants but argues it is insulated by owned rights and producer relationships.
MOATTEST.quote: our main growth reasoning is, our 90s repertoire, whatever we acquired from 1988 onwards till now, everything is doing so well... it's a new retro now

RECURRING.rationale: Historically pure project/tender manufacturing with no recurring stream, but from Q3 FY26 onward management flags the wagon leasing licence and an anticipated wagon maintenance policy as new annuity-type offerings, with the first leasing contract (Balmer Lawrie, 2 rakes) signed by Q4 FY26; also 'complete grip over the value chain right from the critical components up to the service.' Still nascent and explicitly framed as a sales enabler, not a separate recurring business.
RECURRING.quote: we have been awarded the wagon leasing license... This also would mean that we would be able to make an entry into the wagon maintenance market

TOLLROAD.rationale: Rolling stock is the large end-item of the customer's capex (railways' 'last end of the spectrum for investment'), procured via large competitive tenders, not a sub-1% critical input; margins are set by bid competition rather than by indispensability.
TOLLROAD.quote: the last end of the spectrum for investment is the rolling stock, both for passenger and freight

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly accepts thin, range-bound margins (8-10% guidance in FY23, ~12% freight later) and bids aggressively for volume/share, and is building a genuine cost/integration base — own foundries with resin-moulding, wheel-set JV, aluminium extrusion-to-coach line, in-house traction motors/converters — but there is no evidence of an itemised cost culture or high asset turns that competitors could not match.
LOWPRICE.quote: In the transit business we are new entrants, our pricing strategy is a little more aggressive so maybe in the initial years we will have lesser margins

PRICING.rationale: Across the whole 18-call span pricing is tender-determined and margins are guided down rather than up; the Q4 FY26 margin uplift is attributed to free-supply material accounting, not price, and management explicitly declines to raise its margin guidance.
PRICING.quote: the EBITDA margin goes up in that contract... on a sustained basis, we do not change the guidance that we have given

BRAND.rationale: No heritage/A&P/consumer-brand economics; what management cites instead is technical credentials and 'provenness' earned through defect-liability completion at Pune, and it wins work by aggressive bidding and technology transfer (CRRC, ABB) rather than brand premium.
BRAND.quote: the provenness of this train is now established

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a real, growing engineering base — ~150 people in design/R&D for passenger rail, RDSO approval of the first EMU propulsion set with a ~INR500 crore propulsion order book, a 1.6km test track, and Vande Bharat car bodies — but capability comes largely from licensed technology transfer (CRRC stainless steel, ABB TCMS 750kVA and 25kVA) with no disclosed R&D spend or share of industry R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: we have almost 150 people working in design engineering and R&D

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores or D2C, but the FY26 wagon leasing licence plus the intended entry into wagon maintenance is a deliberate move down the value chain toward owning the customer relationship and the aftermarket; management frames it as a bridge to customers rather than a standalone business.
FORWARD.quote: This is only an extension for our own product offering and maybe a stronger bridge between us and our potential customers

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Claimed freight-wagon market leadership from Aug 2022 and a genuine build-out in passenger rail — INR10,600 crore standalone passenger order book vs INR3,100 crore freight, cars sold up from 12 (FY25) to 63 (FY26) — but explicit share percentages versus named competitors are never given, and share in transit was pursued with admittedly aggressive pricing.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We are already market leaders in the freight wagon segment, now we are targeting to become at least substantial players if not market leaders

CULTURE.rationale: Management disclosed the Firema failure plainly and closed it out with full provisioning, and delivered the multi-year Pune promise (34 trains through defect liability plus a 12-train repeat order) with a conservative standalone balance sheet; against that, several promises slipped — the FY23 Firema EBITDA break-even, the 700-wagons-a-month ramp, and the 100-120 metro cars target that ended at 63.
CULTURE.quote: That unfortunately could not succeed and the company continued to make losses... While we have not been able to achieve that target

MOATTEST.rationale: Some hard-to-copy assets accumulate — the only Indian player with carbon-steel, aluminium and stainless-steel coach capability, RDSO-approved propulsion, a wheel-set JV with a 20-year 80,000-wheels-a-year railway contract, and a 1.6km test track — but the business remains dependent on repeat government tenders and licensed foreign technology that a well-funded global rolling-stock entrant could also obtain.
MOATTEST.quote: the first and only company in the passenger rolling stock to have facilities and capabilities to produce every type of passenger coach

RECURRING.rationale: No licence/AMC/subscription stream, but Titan runs customer-funded advance schemes — Golden Harvest enrolments discussed in Aug 2022 and the Gramage Purchase Plan in the Jun 2026 call — which pre-fund purchases and act as a customer-advance funding source; management never quantifies deferred revenue or renewal/attach rates.
RECURRING.quote: the Jewe llery purchase plan that we have, which is the Gramage Purchase Plan , which is ongoing for the last two years, which does a rupee cost averaging by accumulation in grams

TOLLROAD.rationale: Titan sells a large-ticket discretionary consumer purchase (average ticket ~₹1.9 lakh in Q3 FY26) where price and gold-rate sensitivity dominate the entire discussion, and making-charge discount windows are an established playbook — the opposite of a tiny, non-negotiated share of a customer's cost base.
TOLLROAD.quote: there is pressure at lower price points on account of inflation and rise in gold rate

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost control appears only tactically (overheads management in Q1 FY25, offsetting margin with overhead optimisation in Q4 FY26), while the strategy is explicitly premium/trust-led with traction at higher price points and rising ticket sizes — not a scale-driven low-price, high-turn model.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are seeing a greater traction at higher price points in gold jewellery and in studded

PRICING.rationale: Titan passes through very large gold inflation with buyers holding (ticket size +44%, buyer growth returning to 8% in Q4 FY26) and management credits price elasticity — but this is commodity pass-through, not pricing above cost inflation: gross contribution fell ~100-200bps in Q3 FY26, making-charge discount windows persist, and the mix is being pushed down to 18/14/9-carat to stay accessible.
PRICING.quote: despite such significant increases in raw material costs, we are still able to kind of hold a certain buyer -- buyer s in our hold. So that's really credit to price elasticity

BRAND.rationale: Across all four calls the growth story is brand trust plus formalisation — Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane, Zoya, Fastrack — with A&P explicitly not cut in downturns (Aug 2022) and the Fastrack name stretched into eyewear stores and handbags; management names trust and differentiation as the structural driver of the 15-20% growth guidance in Jun 2026.
BRAND.quote: brands which are providing that trust and, of course, differentiation

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular, named product/format innovation each year — Fastrack smartwatches (2022), made-to-order/bespoke (2024), lightweight and 18/14/9-carat jewellery, the diamond festival campaign and beYon lab-grown pilot (2026) — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed and innovation is merchandising-led rather than a funded R&D moat.
INNOVATION.quote: the pivot to lightweight jewellery across the board, introducing 18 -carat traditional gold jewellery also in certain parts of the country

FORWARD.rationale: Pure forward integrator: manufacturer running its own retail network with aggressive store adds (125 net in Q1 FY23; 40-50 Tanishq plus 70-80 Mia targeted in FY25), a long-standing L1/L2/L3 franchising model, ~6% of jewellery topline from digital in 2022, and the 67% Damas acquisition in FY26 converting an overseas retail network to Tanishq.
FORWARD.quote: our aim is to target around 40 to 50 stores in Tanishq and about 70 to 80 stores in Mia and a substantial similar number in CaratLane

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share quoted rising from 4-5% to 6-7% (Aug 2022) with new-buyer contribution at 45-46%, and formalisation plus stronger balance sheets cited as a durable share tailwind through Jun 2026; management was candid that FY25 was 'even steven' with no share gained, and international expansion (GCC/Damas, ~3% of jewellery in 2024) is being localised — gains look organic rather than bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our market share earlier we used to quote 4 -5%, roughly, right now we are quoting at 6 -7%

CULTURE.rationale: Tata-owned with unusually stable, internally-promoted leadership (Sonthalia CFO across all 16 calls; Chawla Jewellery CEO in 2022 to MD by 2026), prompt disclosure of bad news quantified up front (₹500-550cr custom-duty hit in Aug 2024, ₹152cr labour-code charge and 50bps margin drop in Feb 2026), refusal to flatter guidance, and profit-sharing with employees on a good year.
CULTURE.quote: we have a tradition of sharing that superlative performance by sharing, we call it special reward

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but not unassailable barriers: a 270-town prime-location network being upsized rather than just extended, Tata trust and hallmarking credibility, and balance-sheet capacity to carry gold inventory as prices spike — yet management itself repeatedly concedes competitive intensity 'has only gone up' with 40-50 tracked players and rapid national expansion by rivals.
MOATTEST.quote: it's not increasing the count, I think is substantially increasing our presence and competitive advantage

RECURRING.rationale: No discussion of attach rates, renewal rates, AMC/subscription streams or deferred revenue as a funding source; deposit funding is discussed as ordinary bank liability management, not as a product-linked recurring annuity.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Nothing across the 14 calls describes sales via professionals, prescribers or trained intermediaries; origination is via own branches, relationship managers and feet-on-street hired directly.

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification, standards, or 'tiny share of customer cost but critical' language anywhere in the transcripts.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is only half met: operating costs are genuinely low and improving (cost-to-income ~39-45%) and loan quality is exceptional (GNPA 0.73% FY26, 0.69% Q1FY27, credit cost 9bps, unsecured just 10bps of book), but the deposit franchise is not cheap — cost of deposits ~5.68-5.92% and CASA only ~26-28%, and management competes on yield (advances yield 10.1%) rather than passing savings to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: the cost-to-income ratio is just about 39.54% for quarter 4

PRICING.rationale: TMB sustains one of the industry's highest NIMs (4.47% in FY23, 4.18-4.29% in FY26-27) and double-digit advance yields in RAM/gold, but in Nov 2022 management said it consciously withheld a rate pass-through, and NIM has drifted down from 4.47% to ~3.98% for FY26 — pricing is defended rather than repeatedly raised.
PRICING.quote: we have not passed on consciously to the customers

BRAND.rationale: A genuine 105-year heritage franchise with deep trust among Tamil Nadu MSME/trader communities is repeatedly invoked as the USP, but there is no premium pricing, A&P investment or brand-stretch evidence; management concedes it needs 'local connect' and hired 170 outside officers because the brand does not travel beyond the home state.
BRAND.quote: this bank is known for its customer service

INNOVATION.rationale: The record is catch-up, not dominance: in Nov 2024 management admitted service deficiencies, was still integrating GST/CBDT payments, was benchmarking net banking against peers and hiring 47 IT staff, describing itself as a late mover; product launches (GST OD, Mini LAP) are standard offerings peers already had.
INNOVATION.quote: some of the deficiencies that we have noticed in our services, we are addressing them

FORWARD.rationale: Branch expansion (578 to 628 branches, 171 outside Tamil Nadu) is ordinary bank distribution, not a manufacturer integrating toward the customer; no franchising, licensing or D2C economics are discussed.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is real but recent and narrow: FY26-Q1FY27 shows 23% business growth vs an 8.8% 10-year CAGR and explicitly ~7% above industry, achieved with improving not deteriorating credit (GNPA 0.69%, SMA 1.29%), but ~46% of advances is gold loans and MSME was actually de-growing until Q1 FY26, so the gain is commodity-price-assisted and only two years old.
SHAREGAIN.quote: It is 7% over the industry growth.

CULTURE.rationale: Across FY26-FY27 management set explicit quarterly guidance and beat it seven consecutive quarters (CASA 15% guided/22.35% delivered; advances 16-17% guided/20.32% delivered; ROA 1.85%+ guided/2.05%), openly disclosed the missed 50-branch promise, the ED show-cause notice, and MSME de-growth, and provisioned early for ECL (₹250cr COVID buffer retained plus ₹26cr on non-fund-based, not required under IRAC) while running 32-33% capital adequacy.
CULTURE.quote: One thing we have not been able to deliver as per our commitment, we did promise to the investor community that we will open 50 branches in FY26.

MOATTEST.rationale: The un-replicable assets are a banking licence, a 105-year Thoothukudi-region deposit and MSME relationship base, and a 622-branch network — but management's own admission that it must buy 'local connect' outside Tamil Nadu, and that today's growth engine is a gold loan book (46% of advances) any lender can build, shows the current earnings advantage is not itself hard to copy.
MOATTEST.quote: the bank very well understands the pains of the MSME

RECURRING.rationale: Across all three calls management tracks a deliberately built 'non-cyclical' stream — parts & service penetration, Fleet Edge telematics subscriptions with Lite/Prime tiers, AMC-style Smart City uptime contracts — riding on an installed base of ~1 million connected vehicles, with renewals rising from 26% to 37% (Nov 2025) and then doubling from Q1 to Q4 (May 2026); the business is self-funding on working capital at negative 31 days cash conversion with customer advances (Indonesia order) cited in FCF.
RECURRING.quote: non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR... Our cash conversion cycle best-in-class at negative 31 days. It means the business continues to be self-funding on working capital

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is the customer's core capital asset and largest cost decision, not a trivial line item — management repeatedly frames demand through TCO, EMIs and diesel being '30% to 50%' of total cost of ownership, and buyers negotiate hard enough that discounts and price pass-through are recurring call topics.
TOLLROAD.quote: diesel... will have at least 30% to 50% impact on the total cost of ownership

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost culture — capex held to a guided 2–4% of revenue, fixed-cost savings itemised in every EBIT walk, and an explicit choice to absorb commodity inflation via 'cost levers' rather than price — plus affordability positioning (Ace Pro as India's most affordable four-wheel mini truck) and very high asset turns (ROCE 45%→53%→72%); but this is a premium-share incumbent with expanding margins, not a no-frills low-price model.
LOWPRICE.quote: we have decided to not pass on the entire commodity increases and we will work on the cost levers

PRICING.rationale: Management does take regular price increases without losing volume (1% in January 2026, 2% in April 2026, alongside 25% YoY Q4 volume growth) and cites 'pricing discipline' and better realisation as the main margin driver; but it explicitly declines to pass through full input inflation for fear of denting demand, and headline ASPs fell YoY on mix — so pricing power is real but conditional.
PRICING.quote: we have taken a 2% price increase in the month of April, but we have decided to not pass on the entire commodity increases... because we don't want to impact the demand momentum

BRAND.rationale: Evidence of trust and scale distribution leverage — leadership share sustained near 35%, quality awards (Golden Peacock, Apollo CV Awards 2026), and brand stretch into EV, LNG and international markets under one name — but the calls contain no A&P spend, heritage narrative or consumer-brand pricing premium discussion.
BRAND.quote: Pantnagar plant received the Golden Peacock Award for Quality, and we also won multiple honors at the Apollo CV Awards 2026

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is regular and named with volume impact — Ace Pro, Ace Gold LNT, Azura ILMCV platform, Intra EV, 17 next-gen trucks in Q4 FY26 on an in-house modular electric architecture — and R&D is disclosed at ~₹1,700 crores in FY26; but R&D is a modest share of revenue and margins are industrial, not the high-gross-margin innovation flywheel the pattern describes.
INNOVATION.quote: we also launched... 17 new trucks... developed on the Intelligent Modular Electric Vehicle architecture... in-house battery management systems, and e-axles that we have developed

FORWARD.rationale: Real movement toward the customer via digital direct channels — Fleetverse online sales (22,000 platform-assisted retails in a quarter, 27% of retails digitally generated), E-Dukaan spares with 10,000 customers and new own last-mile delivery in eight cities, and Smart City operating its own 3,815-bus e-bus fleet rather than just selling buses — but no owned-store or franchise-royalty economics are disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: E-Dukaan, our online spare part sale, we now have 10,000 customers and 33,000 retailers... started direct-to-customer delivery - last-mile delivery across eight cities

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is explicit, quantified and recovered across the three calls: after a subdued Q1 FY26 the company outgrew industry in Q2 (12% vs 8%), added 100bps sequentially in Q3, and by Q4 posted its highest HCV offtake share in a decade while growing 25% YoY against 19% industry — with international volumes up 54% for FY26 and a 70,000-unit Indonesia order, and management insisting share be won profitably.
SHAREGAIN.quote: in HCVs, we posted our highest offtake market share in a decade... Tata Motors volumes outpaced the industry at 25% YoY growth

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made are visibly delivered — the demerger and TMCV listing completed 'as committed previously', capex kept inside the guided 2–4% band across all three calls, FCF guidance met, 11 consecutive quarters of double-digit EBITDA — and bad or awkward news is owned promptly (losing bus tenders, 'we are not L1 in any of these tenders', discontinuing the sentiment survey, admitting replacement-demand data is weak); the CFO even publicly corrected the CEO's margin guidance on air, and the balance sheet moved to ₹7,500 crores net cash.
CULTURE.quote: And if I may just add in just a correction, Gunjan. Our guidance was teens and not mid-teens

MOATTEST.rationale: There are articulable barriers a funded newcomer could not quickly rebuild — a nationwide parts/service and financier network, four flexible truck plants, 11 scrappage centres, and a telematics data set spanning ~1 million vehicles that underwrites the company's own demand forecasting — but the calls also show the advantage is contestable: share was lost in SCV and in bus tenders, and competitors operate the same segments.
MOATTEST.quote: this is actually based on the data that we have internally, based on around 1 million Fleet Edge installations in trucks and buses

RECURRING.rationale: Only thin, mostly CV-side evidence of an aftermarket annuity (spare parts/service penetration, Fleet Edge/Mileage Sarathi digital subscriptions in the Aug 2024 call) — and that business was demerged out; on the PV/JLR side the recurring language is warranty (a cost, not a stream) and working capital is a cash drain, not a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: We will continue growth in downstream by increasing our penetration of service and spare parts.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is driven by end-consumer marketing, launches and dealer incentives, not by a professional prescriber; across FY26 calls management cites 'high fixed marketing expenses' and rising VME paid to retailers to pull retails, the opposite of low end-customer price sensitivity.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: the high ■xed marketing expenses that we had to sustain for a very busy launch calendar

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is a car — the customer's largest discretionary purchase — not a sub-1% critical input; the calls describe heavy negotiation dynamics (VME, retailer margins, luxury tax, tariffs) rather than customers paying without haggling.
TOLLROAD.quote: VME continues to grow as we try and secure order intake in retails in a very competitive environment.

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, repeated cost programme — JLR's Refocus (GBP1.5bn), then GBP1.7bn of savings over two years to cut breakeven back to 300k units, and India's 'structural cost optimization' — but the savings are consumed by commodities rather than converted into price advantage plus returns, and margins/asset returns collapsed in FY26.
LOWPRICE.quote: the 2% cost reductions that we have done has completely gone to absorb the commodity increases

PRICING.rationale: The record is price deflation, not pricing power: India took no price increases in FY26 with 'adverse pricing impact' for nine months and GST cuts passed through, while JLR's sales allowances rose from ~2.4% (FY24) to 5% then 7% and China retail incurred hit 7.7%.
PRICING.quote: last year, we didn't take any price increases

BRAND.rationale: Real heritage assets — Defender winning Dakar on debut, Range Rover/Range Rover Sport at 77% of Q4 mix with average revenue per car still rising, and Tata's Nexon/Punch as #1 and #3 models in India — but brand strength is not translating into premium pricing (rising discounts) and China volumes fell 26-27%, so durability is being tested rather than proven.
BRAND.quote: the JLR brand remains strong and resilient

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches every year with revenue impact (Curvv, Sierra with 70,000 day-one bookings, Punch facelift, Harrier.ev, Defender OCTA, EMA/Panthera architectures) and disclosed, growing engineering spend (GBP2.6bn of GBP3.57bn investment in FY26 at 64% capitalisation) — but it is capital-hungry catch-up spend funded from thin margins, not high-gross-margin innovation converting into pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: we spent GBP3.57 billion, of which GBP2.6 billion was engineering as we progressed three new architectures

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gains across the period: CV at ~39% (Aug 2024), and in FY26 India PV rose ~1.5pp from Q1 to exit above 14% and the #2 Vahan rank, with EV share exiting above 40% and volumes growing 15% versus an 8% industry — gains driven by product launches rather than by discounting alone, though JLR simultaneously lost share-quality ground in China.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we consolidated our position as the number two player in the domestic market basis Vahan data with a market share crossing 14%

CULTURE.rationale: Management does own bad news candidly and repeatedly (Q1FY23 'disappointing quarter... not a number we are proud of'; FY26 'far from what we had intended... corrective action is necessary') and did hit its restated FY26 guidance on both EBIT and cash — but the multi-year record includes CEO churn at JLR (Bolloré→Mardell→Balaji), a leveraged balance sheet, and repeated resets of promises.
CULTURE.quote: delivered what we promised in Q4, it is accepted that our full year financial performance is far from what we had intended

MOATTEST.rationale: Defender and Range Rover are decades-deep brands with capital barriers (three new architectures, Wolverhampton BEV propulsion) a copycat could not rebuild cheaply — but management's own China commentary concedes well-funded new entrants are permanently eroding the premium position, which is exactly the failure case of the replication test.
MOATTEST.quote: This is not a short -term boom -bust cycle. This is structural and permanent in China

RECURRING.rationale: Across all twelve calls management never discusses attach rates, AMC/service revenue, renewals, deferred revenue or customer advances; revenue is discussed purely as product sales by geography.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The entire India and Brazil model is prescriber-driven: growth is explained by medical-rep count (5,500 in FY23 to 7,100 by FY26, guided to 7,500), division/headquarter expansion and 'field force productivity', with the doctor choosing and the patient paying; Brazil commentary even notes pharmacists cannot substitute against a prescription, and Brazil CNS reps were added specifically to widen therapy coverage.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Our field force at the end of the year stands at 7,100 ex of JB.

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification, standards or tiny-share-of-cost criticality language; instead pricing is externally constrained — Brazil prices are set annually by government and US/Brazil generics face 45-90% price erosion, the opposite of a toll-road's uncontested pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: in Brazil every year, the prices get revised by the government, which is implemented in April

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine, itemised cost discipline (Q3FY25 broke down freight, energy and BRL savings rupee-by-rupee; Germany 'cost optimization to improve our competitiveness in the tender segment'; US 'stop the bleeding'; INR400-450cr JB synergies tracking ahead of plan), but the business is a 76% gross margin / 32.7% EBITDA branded model, not a low-price high-turns one.
LOWPRICE.quote: there is a savings in manufacturing cost which we have seen to the extent of Rs. 10 crores

PRICING.rationale: In the branded businesses (75%+ of revenue) price is the largest growth component and consistently above market with no volume loss — FY23 India growth was 3% volume/7% price, Q3FY25 was 8% price vs market's 5%, Q3FY26 5.8% vs 5.6% — and Brazil delivers 'healthy volume growth coupled with mid-single-digit pricing increase'; the offset is US/generic price erosion, which management has deliberately shrunk to a niche.
PRICING.quote: That's broken up into 1.5% volume, 8% of price, and 2.5% of new products. The volume of the market is close to zero.

BRAND.rationale: Brand-led model widened over the three years — 18 brands in IPM top 500 in FY23 to 20 by FY25 with 13 above Rs.100cr — and the Curatio/Shelcal consumer platform was built out from a four-state pilot into sustained A&P that delivered 27% growth in FY26, i.e. share gain plus above-market pricing under the same names.
BRAND.quote: The Curatio business grew at 27% in FY26, driven by strong demand generation on account of OTC ad spends and field force expansion

INNOVATION.rationale: There is regular, named, revenue-relevant innovation — first-to-market generic Brexpiprazole after own clinical trials, oral plus injectable Semaglutide taking 38% generic share, a Resmetirom Phase 3, 58-60 molecules pending at ANVISA — but R&D is being reallocated rather than scaled ('not going to lead to any real material increase in R&D spend') and spend is never disclosed as a growing line or share of industry.
INNOVATION.quote: we were the first to launch generic Brexpiprazole in April in the India market after conducting the clinical trials

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing royalties or D2C revenue is discussed; the consumer healthcare 'platform' is trade distribution reach (75,000 outlets), not forward integration to the end customer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified outperformance in every call: IPM rank went 8th to 6th, India grew 12-15% against IPM 8-10% quarter after quarter across FY23-FY26, Brazil grew 13-17% on IQVIA against a 6-12% market, and the gain is funded organically with margins rising (29.2% to 32.7%) and leverage falling, not bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the company's IPM rank has gained two ranks and now is the 6th largest player in the Indian pharmaceutical market

CULTURE.rationale: Old promises show up delivered in later calls — Curatio integration and margin accretion (FY23) delivered, field force guided 'just over 7,000' (Feb-26) landed at 7,100 (May-26), deleveraging from 1.55x net debt/EBITDA to 0.51x, insulin facility release timed as guided — and bad news is stated plainly rather than spun (Germany supplier disruption 'fully there' with no timeline given, US 'we are not happy with this current level').
CULTURE.quote: we are not happy with this current level of $150-$160 million

MOATTEST.rationale: A concrete barrier is visible in the numbers — a 7,100-rep prescriber network plus 20 top-500 brands and decades of chronic-therapy equity that a funded entrant cannot assemble quickly (Torrent itself bought Curatio and JB rather than build) — but management never articulates the replication barrier itself, and the generics arms (US, German tenders) demonstrably have none.
MOATTEST.quote: with the base of the Torrent reps plus JB reps, there is no need to add MRs

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is regulated tariff and PPA-based, and growth consumes enormous capital rather than little — FY26 capex was ~INR1,600cr distribution + INR6,500cr renewables with FY27 guided 'much, much higher'; no attach rates, AMC/licence streams, renewals or customer-funded deferred revenue anywhere in five calls.
RECURRING.quote: renewable is a substantial chunk, close to INR6,500 crores capex we spend for the renewables

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No evidence of professionals, installers or prescribers driving demand; sales are to regulated consumers, DISCOMs and NVVN tenders.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Electricity is a large, negotiated line item for industrial buyers, not a sub-1% critical input — management repeatedly notes offtake is price-elastic, with merchant sales dying at high LNG prices and Surat volumes falling with diamond/textile activity.
TOLLROAD.quote: at current prices, that would be very difficult to sell power on the merchant prices at current $20 or $16 sort of gas prices
