LOWPRICE.rationale: Genuine, itemised operating-cost obsession — 2.34% licence distribution loss described as among the lowest nationally, Agra franchise AT&C down from 58.77% at takeover (2010) to 6.94%, and an INR800cr reduction in regulatory gap on efficiency — but the savings accrue via regulated incentives rather than being passed to price for volume/share.
LOWPRICE.quote: Agra achieved its historical low AT&C losses of 6.94% compared to 58.77% when it was taken over in 2010

PRICING.rationale: Prices are set by regulators, not the company: ROE/ROCE frameworks (14% moving to 13-15.5% with milestones), fuel as pass-through, and a INR171cr disallowance on UNOSUGEN power purchase cost show tariff outcomes are contested downward, not raised at will.
PRICING.quote: nonrecurring provisions of INR171 crores arising due to capping of power purchase cost for UNOSUGEN

BRAND.rationale: No discussion of brand, A&P spend, heritage or consumer-facing premium across the five calls.

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline economics or named product launches are disclosed; the one technical initiative mentioned (green hydrogen blending in city gas) has no stated revenue or margin impact.

FORWARD.rationale: The company is integrated from generation through to the end consumer via licensed distribution in Ahmedabad/Surat and distribution franchises (Agra, D&H), which does capture the customer relationship — but there is no own-store/D2C/royalty economics of the kind this pattern describes, and the franchise role is as operator, not brand licensor.
FORWARD.quote: In our franchisee business area, Agra achieved its historical low AT&C losses of 6.94%

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Footprint is expanding — installed capacity 4.8GW (Mar'25) to 5.1GW (Mar'26), RE pipeline 3.1GW to 4GW, a 1.6GW MP coal LOA, Nabha Power acquisition and UP privatisation bidding — but no market-share figures are given, and FY26 renewable commissioning (~250-360MW against 500-600MW guided) fell short.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our aspiration is to reach a 10 gigawatts of renewable capacities

CULTURE.rationale: Conservative and disciplined — net debt/equity 0.40 and net debt/EBITDA 1.41x, maiden QIP in three decades, bidding held to a 'threshold IRR', prudent provisioning for a contested disallowance, and the multi-year Agra turnaround delivered as promised; against that, management declines several fair questions ('we are not disclosing', 'we'll explain after the call') and missed its own FY26 renewable commissioning guidance without owning the miss.
CULTURE.quote: we are bidding for most of the projects, I would say, but we restrict ourselves with our threshold IRR

MOATTEST.rationale: Parts of the base are genuinely un-replicable — statutory distribution licences in Ahmedabad/Surat, a 40-year 2,000MW energy storage facility agreement with MSEDCL, and finite pumped-storage/transmission sites — but management never articulates the barrier, and the growth engine (renewables, coal, PSP) is competitively tendered work any well-funded rival can bid for.
MOATTEST.quote: Energy Storage Facility Agreement with MSEDCL for supplying 2000 MW from storage hydro project for 40 years

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is 100% lumpy turnkey EPC contract execution booked off an order book; across all six calls there is no mention of AMC, service contracts, licences, attach rates or renewals, and working capital is structurally positive (receivables, retention, contract assets of ~Rs.2,643 crore) rather than customer-funded, with management itself calling it a working-capital-heavy business.
RECURRING.quote: Basically, this is a high working capital intensive industry.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Orders are won by direct competitive tender from utilities and developers (Power Grid, Adani, Renew, multilateral-funded overseas clients) — the payer and the specifier are the same entity, with no professional/installer channel or trade training programme mentioned in any call.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: in Africa, we are facing competition from 4 to 5 players per tender

TOLLROAD.rationale: Transrail's scope is the transmission line itself — the dominant share of the customer's project cost, not a sub-1% critical ingredient — and it is repriced at every tender against several bidders, the opposite of a no-negotiation toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: conductors and towers are almost 60% of a value of an EPC turnkey job

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine structural cost advantage — full backward integration into towers, conductors and poles plus design-engineering optimisation to cut steel weight, and repeated cost-discipline language (ERP upgrade to SAP RISE 'aiming at deepening cost discipline', inventory built to capture low steel prices) — but management explicitly does not pass this to price, instead using it to run 400-500bps above peer margins and bid selectively.
LOWPRICE.quote: We basically depend on our design engineering strength as Transrail, which helps us to look at waste volumes and be competitive in our bidding.

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is set by competitive fixed-price tenders with no ability to raise prices on booked work; EBITDA margin has drifted down across the period (13.04% 9M FY25 → 11.92% FY26 → ~11% guided for FY27) on geopolitical cost escalation, i.e. the company absorbs input inflation rather than passing it on.
PRICING.quote: Keeping due prudence and caution, we have given a guidance around 11%

BRAND.rationale: There is a 41-year track record, POWERGRID A-grade certification of the Deoli plant, safety/quality awards and 'most admired emerging EPC Company' recognition that function as pre-qualification credentials in a B2B tender market — but no premium pricing, no A&P spend and no consumer-style brand stretch; reputation here buys the right to bid, not price.
BRAND.quote: an established and trusted long standing partner for many of our clients

INNOVATION.rationale: Across six calls no R&D spend, pipeline or named new product is ever disclosed; incremental capability additions (solar EPC, HVDC, monopoles) are new bid categories rather than proprietary innovation, and differentiation is consistently attributed to backward integration and execution discipline instead.
INNOVATION.quote: we are fully backward integrated and we have conductors, poles and tower manufacturing facility which not all our competitors have

FORWARD.rationale: The entire capital-allocation programme runs the other way — Rs.325 crore Phase-1 plus Rs.203 crore new capex into upstream tower, conductor and construction-equipment capacity; there are no owned stores, franchising, licensing or D2C channels in an order-book tender model.
FORWARD.quote: we already are fully backward integrated for towers, conductors and testing and including our poles

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, profitable share gain across the whole period: revenue 3x in five years and +30% in FY26 to Rs.6,880 crore (beating the 25% then 27% guidance), order book Rs.15,643 crore → Rs.18,216 crore, entry into new geographies every year (Eswatini, Nicaragua, GCC/MENA, Abu Dhabi, Tunisia, Djibouti, Botswana), all while running peer-beating margins and ROCE consistently above 24% — share not bought with profitability, and management explicitly bids selectively rather than chasing volume.
SHAREGAIN.quote: With 3x growth in revenue for last five years, we are stronger than ever.

CULTURE.rationale: The delivery-vs-promise record across the six calls is clean: FY25 30% growth guidance met, FY26 guided 25% → raised to 27% → delivered 30%, margin guidance of 11.5-12% delivered at 11.92%, the IPO capex programme announced in Feb 2025 completed (tower capacity more than doubled) and working capital promises kept (91 → 81 days, operating cash flow doubling to Rs.817 crore), with debt/equity held at ~0.38x; management also owned the FY26 order-intake miss openly rather than reframing it, and the founder-promoter has run the business 40+ years.
CULTURE.quote: against INR10,000 crores, we did INR8,520 crores new order intake

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real time-based barriers — 41 years of operating history, a modern tower-testing facility, POWERGRID A-grade plant certification, 200+ completed EPC projects across 58 countries and multilateral-agency prequalifications a newcomer cannot buy quickly — but the core activity is repeat competitive tendering against several well-capitalised incumbents and Chinese bidders, so a funded entrant is not structurally excluded, only delayed.
MOATTEST.quote: we are a few players with integrated manufacturing facilities for lattice structures... with a very modern tower testing facility

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is contract-based rather than product-plus-service: 94% contract renewal since 2009, long-term master concessions, management fees from JV-operated units and a lounge-aggregation/bank-access stream via the EATS platform. But no attach rates, AMC share, deferred revenue or customer advances are discussed, and Q4 FY26 showed receivables rising ~INR1bn on EATS ramp-up rather than negative working capital.
RECURRING.quote: we have a contract renewal rate of 94%, since the inception of our business in 2009

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Two intermediaries matter: airport operators award master concessions (TFS never markets to the passenger to win the site), and in lounges the banks/credit-card issuers pay for access on the traveller's behalf — a genuinely price-insensitive payer. But there is no trade-training or professional-prescriber lock-in of the classic kind.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: rolled out a technology solution enabling direct collaborations with banking and credit card partners, eliminating intermediaries

TOLLROAD.rationale: TFS sells discretionary food and lounge experiences directly to passengers; it is not a small-but-critical input into a customer's cost base, and there is no certification, standards or regulatory-anchoring language. Its captivity comes from location, not from being an unswitchable ingredient.
TOLLROAD.quote: people are spending more money towards experiences, F&B dining, premiumization

LOWPRICE.rationale: The model is the opposite of low price: gross margin rose from 81.7% to 84.7% for FY26 (87.3% in Q4) on premiumisation, Gordon Ramsay/Nando's/Wagamama tie-ups and higher spend per pax. Cost discipline is real (procurement, manpower, central kitchens) but it is used to expand margin, not to fund lower prices.
LOWPRICE.quote: Gross profit margin increased to 87.3% compared to 83.0% in the same period last year

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly says price is taken only in line with inflation, so it fails the 'above cost inflation' test, yet it consistently converts ~1% passenger growth into 12.5% system-wide LFL via premiumisation, ATV and mix — pricing-for-value rather than raw pricing power, with rising gross margins.
PRICING.quote: Our price normally is largely in line with the increases with inflation

BRAND.rationale: TFS is a multi-brand platform (130 brands in Aug 2025 to 145+ by Jun 2026) leveraging others' heritage brands, plus its own in-house names (idli.com, Cafeccino, Delhi Street); the reputational asset that wins tenders is TFS's operator credibility with airport partners, not consumer brand equity, and no A&P spend or heritage story is presented.
BRAND.quote: our brand portfolio now spans over 145 brands with a wide mix of global, regional, and in-house brands

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular, named incremental innovation each year — 15 new brands added, Gordon Ramsay Street Burger, premium sleeping pods at Bengaluru, automated cocktail dispensers, signature filter coffee, boba tea, the EATS tech platform — but no R&D spend disclosed and no claim to a share of industry R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: we launched premium sleeping pods at the Bengaluru International Airport lounge... creating an incremental experience-led revenue stream

FORWARD.rationale: TFS already owns the customer-facing outlet and is pushing further forward by disintermediating lounge aggregators with its own EATS platform selling bank-to-lounge access direct, and by operating in-house brands rather than only licensed ones; there is no franchising or third-party-funded store growth.
FORWARD.quote: Through our EATS platform, we have enabled direct bank-to-lounge access as an integrated service

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit and rising leadership — 26% travel QSR share and 45% lounge share, network from 491 units/19 airports to 550+ units/20 airports with 76 QSR units mobilised in FY26, wins at Delhi T1 (33 units, 11 years), T2, Cochin, Navi Mumbai, plus Malaysia/Hong Kong — and the share is not bought cheaply, with ~50% ROCE and an explicit refusal to compromise return metrics.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we would not compromise our return metrics

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on earlier calls were delivered: ~50 units guided in Q1 FY26 became 76 mobilised, Cochin opened 'on schedule', Navi Mumbai and Delhi T2 came online as flagged; bad news is disclosed promptly (labour-code one-off, litigation provision, JV deferred-tax base effect flagged in advance, Delhi T3 contract going to open tender), leadership is stable, and the balance sheet is zero-debt with INR8.4bn cash through a year of repeated shocks.
CULTURE.quote: we remain a zero-debt company with a healthy cash and investment position of approximately INR8.4 billion

MOATTEST.rationale: A concrete replication barrier is articulated: airside real estate is finite and awarded by long-term master concession, with security clearance, restricted-space construction, central kitchens and back-of-house capital — and a 94% renewal record since 2009 means a funded newcomer must wait years for a tender and then out-bid the incumbent. The Delhi T3 open re-tender is the honest limit on that moat.
MOATTEST.quote: Our ability to navigate through these complexities... acts as a high entry barrier for others and a competitive moat for our business

RECURRING.rationale: Across all calls the Aftermarket (spares, service, refurbishment) is a distinct, high-margin ~34% of turnover growing off a 25-year installed base, extended even to other OEMs' machines and to third-party rotating equipment; management repeatedly ties the cash pile to customer advances and negative working capital.
RECURRING.quote: a lot of the cash pile that we have is driven by negative working capital, as well as high customer advances

TOLLROAD.rationale: Management describes a duopolistic domestic / oligopolistic international structure with a 25-year lifecycle relationship and API/refinery qualification credentials, but the turbine itself is a substantial capex item for the customer, not a sub-1% consumable — only the aftermarket spares fit the toll-road economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: we operate in a duopolistic market domestically and oligopolistic market internationally

PRICING.rationale: PBT margins are held above 20% and EBITDA expanded 240bps in Q1 FY25, but management explicitly chooses not to exercise pricing power, preferring to absorb input costs and 'take customers along'; margin moves are attributed to mix (exports/aftermarket) and commodities rather than price rises.
PRICING.quote: while we have the ability to increase prices... we believe that it's more important to take our customers along with us

BRAND.rationale: Reputation shows up as quality systems 'well regarded' by customers, an all-time-high Net Promoter Score and 'prestigious' refinery/international orders, but there is no heritage story, A&P spend or distribution-brand leverage of the classic consumer type.
BRAND.quote: the recently concluded Net Promoter Score study seems to indicate that our customer satisfaction is at an all-time high

INNOVATION.rationale: Every year brings named, R&D-led product extensions with disclosed traction — supercritical/transcritical CO2 (2022), the >120MW range (2024), heat pumps, MVR compressors, geothermal and organic Rankine cycle (2026) — funded by 24%+ EBITDA margins in what management calls a technology business.
INNOVATION.quote: our research and development continues to innovate and deliver new products... includes our carbon dioxide-based platform as well as the introduction of our organic Rankine cycle turbine

FORWARD.rationale: Triveni is moving toward the customer through owned service infrastructure rather than retail — the TSE Engineering acquisition taken to 100% control in South Africa and the commissioned Houston facility — explicitly to be closer to customers for spares and service, though there is no franchising or D2C model.
FORWARD.quote: We are investing into capabilities to be closer to our customers internationally so that we can cater to their third-party product requirements

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed repeatedly and qualitatively (high domestic share, rising share in >30MW turbines, record export order booking up 174% in Q4 FY26, entry into US/Sub-Saharan Africa), but the calls give almost no explicit share percentages tracked over time.
SHAREGAIN.quote: a lot of our growth and visibility is coming from these larger megawatt (MW) turbines, which we are increasingly getting a better market share in

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable across the full 2022–2026 span (Sawhney, Prasad, Parab, Mote), the balance sheet stays net cash (₹10.37bn investments, negative working capital), and bad news is disclosed promptly and specifically — muted domestic order booking, the ₹21 crore US subsidiary loss, receivable days worsening from 49 to 84, dispatch delays that 'will not be able to be caught up'.
CULTURE.quote: Some of the delays will not be able to be caught up

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barrier is concrete: a duopolistic domestic position built on a 25-year installed base that feeds refurbishment/spares, customer qualifications in API/refinery segments, and metallurgy and fluid-dynamics competence a newcomer cannot buy quickly — evidenced by the ability to service other OEMs' and utility-scale machines.
MOATTEST.quote: it is extremely demanding from a technical perspective of metallurgy as well as fluid dynamics, but also the reliability and robustness that has to be delivered

RECURRING.rationale: The Water business carries a large long-duration O&M annuity tail (₹1,077 crore of a ₹1,500 crore order book in Q4 FY26; ₹867 crore of ₹1,200 crore in Q1 FY25) and Power Transmission has a stated aftermarket stream, but management never discusses attach rates, renewals, or deferred revenue as a funding source — and the bulk of revenue is spot commodity sugar/ethanol.
RECURRING.quote: closing order book for this business stood... at just over ₹1,500 crore, out of which longer duration O&M maintenance contracts comprised just over about ₹1,077 crore

TOLLROAD.rationale: The gearbox business shows toll-road traits — a small-value but mission-critical component inside compressor trains and turbines, anchored to API oil-and-gas standards and to import-substitution/indigenisation, plus a first-of-a-kind axial compressor test gearbox — but this is a minority of group revenue and no 'don't switch once converted' or cost-share evidence is offered.
TOLLROAD.quote: high power API, which is adhering to the requirements of the oil and gas and petrochemical sector... indigenisation of imported gearboxes

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine cost culture recurs across the later calls — maize procurement and supply-chain sourcing, steam and energy optimisation, borrowing cost cut to 6.1% and working capital to 6.5% — and this offset the record ₹300/tonne UP cane price rise; but this is commodity cost defence, not a scale-based low-price-plus proposition to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: The higher recoveries and cost optimisation measures insulated our margins against the ₹300 per metric tonne increase in cane pricing

PRICING.rationale: Prices are set by the State (cane SAP, sugar MSP unchanged since 2019, OMC ethanol rates), and management spends calls lobbying rather than pricing — ethanol realisation actually fell to ₹61/litre on FCI-rice mix while cane cost rose ₹300/tonne, the opposite of pricing power.
PRICING.quote: The MSP... has remained unchanged since 2019, while input costs and sugarcane price, both FRP and SAP have risen significantly

BRAND.rationale: A brand build has started — IMFL launches in July 2024 (The Crafters Stamp, Matsya) with IMIL now among the top five players in Uttar Pradesh, and brand-presence exhibitions in the Middle East for gearboxes — but there is no heritage story, no disclosed A&P spend, and it is only two years old.
BRAND.quote: Our branded IMIL business outperformed the broader industry growth metrics in Uttar Pradesh as well, solidifying its position amongst the top five players

INNOVATION.rationale: Power Transmission shows a real, repeated R&D thread that converts into cost reduction and new addressable markets (compressor gearboxes, small hydro, API, and the Q4 FY26 first-in-Asia axial compressor test gearbox), but R&D spend is never quantified and the sugar/ethanol majority of the business is agronomy, not innovation-led.
INNOVATION.quote: we have made continuous investments in Research and Development... which has resulted in a material cost decreases

FORWARD.rationale: Triveni has moved forward from bulk alcohol into its own branded IMFL/IMIL spirits, and in sugar toward premium refined and pharma-grade product (70% of output by FY25), but there are no own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C economics discussed.
FORWARD.quote: The Company's IMFL business commenced its operations in the month of July 2024, with the launch of two brands

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Repeated evidence of share gain in the non-commodity pockets — export gearbox share in compressors and pumps, record order books (₹243cr FY23 → ₹306cr FY25 → ₹500cr FY26), top-five IMIL in UP, plus the SSEL acquisition — and sugar recovery beating the UP state average, but no explicit market-share percentages tracked over time.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The export growth is primarily driven by market share gains in the Compressors and Pump segment

CULTURE.rationale: The same leadership team (Sawhney, Taneja, Sinha) runs all 16 calls, targets set in earlier calls are delivered and reconciled later (660 KLPD distillery capacity, Co0238 variety reduction 77%→50%, ₹340 crore capex tracked tranche by tranche), misses are owned plainly, and the balance sheet stayed conservative through the cycle to an ICRA AA+ reaffirmation.
CULTURE.quote: The hope was that Q3 would result in significant increases in order booking and that did not transpire.

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are real but unarticulated by management: regulated UP cane command areas and licensed mill capacity cannot be replicated by a funded entrant, and the defence/test-rig gearbox technology is described as first-of-a-kind in Asia; against that, distillery KLPD capacity and water EPC bidding are straightforwardly buyable with capital.
MOATTEST.quote: a landmark order of an axial compressor test gearbox from a premier defence establishment, the first of a kind in Asia

RECURRING.rationale: Spare-parts revenue is disclosed every call and grows steadily (INR670cr in Q2FY23 to INR930cr in Q2FY25), dealer dispatches are cash-and-carry with under 30 days stock (customer-funded working capital), and BaaS battery subscription was launched in FY26 — but management never discusses attach rates, AMC share, renewals or deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: we don't keep more than 30 days of stock with our dealers in India... they are all cash and carry

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are driven by direct consumer brand pull and heavy end-customer marketing, not by a professional who prescribes while someone else pays; the Jul 2026 call attributes share gain to customers willingly paying a premium versus a discounting rival, and no trade-training or prescriber economics appear in any of the 16 calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: customers are willing to pay a reasonable premium... over competitive models

TOLLROAD.rationale: A two-wheeler is the customer's major purchase, not a sub-1% critical input; the calls discuss retail finance penetration, affordability and GST relief — the language of a big-ticket consumer decision, and the economy segment is explicitly flagged as inflation-sensitive.
TOLLROAD.quote: Economy category, the challenge will be a little higher because that is where most of the customers who have challenges in terms of higher inflation

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine, repeated cost culture runs through all 16 calls ('sustained cost reduction initiatives' appears in Nov 2022, Oct 2024, May 2026 and Jul 2026) with rising asset turns, but the positioning is deliberately feature-rich premiumisation rather than no-frills low price, and margins rose from 10.2% to 13.1% rather than being passed to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: we will continue to leverage scale benefit, better product mix, sustained effort and cost reduction

PRICING.rationale: Price increases are taken repeatedly and explicitly without volume loss — ~1% in Q2FY23, and in FY26 roughly a third of a 3-5% commodity shock was offset by price while volumes grew 24-28%; Jupiter 110 ran a waiting list in Oct 2024 and in Jul 2026 TVS gained share against a discounting scooter rival while holding a premium.
PRICING.quote: we were able to increase prices 35% of the price increases we were able to offset by increasing prices

BRAND.rationale: Heritage milestones recur across the record — Jupiter crossing 5 million (Nov 2022), HLX crossing 5 million after 13 years with the last million in one year, iQube crossing 1 million (Jul 2026) — alongside sustained deliberate marketing spend and clear adjacency stretching of the same names (Jupiter 110/125, Ntorq 125/150, iQube S/Orbiter).
BRAND.quote: I don't look at it as marketing cost. I look at the marketing investment

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products arrive every single year with visible revenue impact (Ronin and iQube 2022, Jupiter 110 and Apache RTR 310 in 2024, Orbiter, iQube S, King Kargo CNG and the Norton Manx/Atlas range in 2026), funded by an openly higher-than-peer employee and depreciation load for in-house software, electronics and digital capability — ~500 specialists disclosed in Oct 2024.
INNOVATION.quote: we have almost 250 software people and have about 250 digital

FORWARD.rationale: Forward moves are real but limited: captive finance TVS Credit funds ~44% of TVS two-wheeler purchases and has grown to a INR32,053cr book across ~62,000 touchpoints, and TVS Paddock was announced in Jul 2026 as a bespoke premium retail channel — but no own-store counts, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share are ever disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: our premium bespoke experience channel TVS Paddock... redefining premium ownership

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Every one of the 16 calls reports growth ahead of industry and the numbers bear it out — domestic ICE +21% vs industry 12% (Nov 2022), +19% vs 10% for FY26, EV share from 2.9% to 9.9% within a year, international sales up 33% — and crucially the share was won while EBITDA rose from 10.2% to 13.1% and credit quality improved, not bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Total 2-wheeler ICE sales grew by 22% compared to last year as against industry growth of 12%

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable and family-anchored (Venu Srinivasan chairman, Sudarshan Venu MD, with Radhakrishnan and Desikan on every call from 2022 to 2026), promises made in old calls were delivered in later ones — the EV ramp, the promised EV three-wheeler, Norton products promised in 2021 and launched 2026, and the repeated 'EBITDA better quarter after quarter' pledge that went 10.2% to 13.1% — with supply-chain misses admitted openly and the balance sheet upgraded to AAA.
CULTURE.quote: our long-term facility credit rating has been upgraded from CARE AA+ to AAA

MOATTEST.rationale: There are hard-to-copy assets — decades-deep dealer and distributor networks across India, Africa, Asia and LATAM, TVS Credit's 2.6 crore customer base and 62,000 touchpoints, and 13 years of HLX brand equity in Africa — but two-wheeler manufacturing remains contested by equally well-funded rivals (Honda, Hero, Bajaj, EV entrants), and management cites no barrier a determined newcomer could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: HLX brand stands for its customer durability, reliability and in terms of low maintenance costs across Africa, Middle East and LATAM

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is contracted and multi-year (10+ year customer relationships, a 7-year UK framework deal, a >5-year USD 30m North America engagement) and 'encirclement' expands existing accounts, but across all 11 calls there is no product-upfront sale, no attach/renewal rates, no AMC/licence share and no deferred revenue or customer-advance funding — it is outsourcing contract revenue, not an installed-base annuity.
RECURRING.quote: our customer contracts are generally long-term in nature and our customer services are predominantly in the 3PL space

TOLLROAD.rationale: Logistics is a large, negotiated line of the customer's cost base, not a sub-1% critical ingredient: freight rates are repeatedly described as 'under pressure', the company exited unprofitable contracts to protect margin, and it won North America work by displacing an incumbent — the opposite of customers who don't switch once converted.
TOLLROAD.quote: Freight rates continue to be under pressure

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is itemised cost discipline — Project One with INR 110-120 crore annualised savings, rightsizing/right-shoring, tight employee-cost rein — but this reads as turnaround cost takeout rather than a structural low-cost culture, and returns remain thin (FY26 adjusted PBT of only INR 99.3 crore on INR 11,003 crore of revenue).
LOWPRICE.quote: we expect an annualized savings of around INR110 crores to INR120 crores

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory shows price deflation, not pricing power: ocean rates fell ~55% y/y in Q1 FY24, and by FY26 freight rates were still 'subdued', with GFS margins at 2.4%; profit improvement came from mix, volume and cost takeout, and the NS/GFS 7% margin promised in Nov 2024 was never delivered.
PRICING.quote: the GFS business continues to operate at structurally lower margins

BRAND.rationale: There is B2B reputational pull — TVS group provenance, marquee/Fortune 500 logos rising from 91 to 100 in FY26, and repeated 'trust our customers place in TVS SCS' language — but no heritage-led premium pricing, no A&P spend, and no evidence the name commands price.
BRAND.quote: we added 9 new Fortune 500 customers, taking the total number of active Fortune 500 clients from 91 last year to 100

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent 'tech-led' positioning with named initiatives across the calls — AI bid-support LLM pilot and damage-detection (Nov 2024), robotics in North America and an accepted patent for a unified logistics platform (FY26) — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed, gross margins are thin, and nothing quantifies revenue from innovation.
INNOVATION.quote: We have also applied a patent for our unified logistics platform which has been accepted

SHAREGAIN.rationale: New-business wins are quantified and rising (INR 280 crore in Q2 FY25, an all-time-high INR 523.7 crore in Q4 FY26, INR 1,206.7 crore or 12.1% of FY25 revenue for the year) with a INR 6,100-6,300 crore pipeline and genuine international breadth, but management never cites a market-share number or share versus named competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: In Q4, we recorded new business wins, which is an all-time high in a quarter of Rs. 523.7 crores

CULTURE.rationale: Some promises were kept — Project One savings landed as guided and the Q4 FY26 ISCS growth commitment was explicitly delivered — but the record also shows repeatedly slipped promises (IFM 'run rate profitability by Q3 FY24', then end-FY25; the 7% Network margin promised 'in the next three to four quarters' was still 2.4% in Q4 FY26) and heavy leadership churn, with three CEOs and the MD exiting in FY2025 and the MD retiring in FY2026.
CULTURE.quote: we have delivered on our commitment that we made in the previous quarter on our quarter 4 growth

MOATTEST.rationale: Management itself describes the business as asset-light 3PL/freight forwarding won through competitive bids — it displaced an 'incumbent supply chain provider' in North America, which shows how contestable these mandates are — and nothing across 11 calls articulates a barrier a funded entrant could not rebuild in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: a significant difference from what the customer was used to, in with an incumbent supply chain provider

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 13 calls the model is one-off case sales into state-controlled trade channels with no licence, AMC, subscription or attach-rate economics; far from customers funding the business, UBL was chasing overdue receivables from a state corporation in FY25.
RECURRING.quote: Right now, another focus in Telangana is to get the payment back. There is overdue

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is driven by consumer brand pull — IPL/World Cup/Sunburn sponsorships, brand-power tracking, 'consumer-first mindset' — not by a professional or installer who specifies the product; trade work is distribution coverage and visi-coolers, not expert prescription.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we are leveraging a lot of -- really consumer -first mindset

TOLLROAD.rationale: Beer is a discretionary end-consumer purchase whose price is the central constraint on volume — management repeatedly names affordability as the number-one threat and reports double-digit category declines after duty-led price increases in Karnataka, Orissa and Telangana (May 2025, Oct 2025 calls).
TOLLROAD.quote: affordability is the biggest threat to growth of this category

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is itemised cost work — bottle-return improvement, Mangalore brewery closure, network optimisation, fixed-to-variable conversion, trade-spend streamlining (Oct 2025) — but it is reactive margin defence rather than a scale-based low-price model; the stated strategy is premiumisation, and EBIT margins remain thin/volatile (8.9% in Q1FY23, EBIT down 18% in H1FY26).
LOWPRICE.quote: we are accelerating some of our productivity and efficiency measures, which include network optimizations, for instance, like we have announced the closure of our brewery in Mangalore

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is granted by state excise committees, not by the company, and management says explicitly it cannot pass cost inflation to consumers; where prices did rise (Telangana +20%, Karnataka duties) volumes fell double digits — the price-deflation-risk opposite of pricing power.
PRICING.quote: in India , we cannot translate cost price increase into consumer pricing

BRAND.rationale: Kingfisher is a heritage brand with sustained and rising A&P (brand investment up over 20% YoY in Q2FY26 even into a loss-making quarter), tracked brand-power scores at all-time highs on Ultra and Kingfisher, and repeated adjacency stretches (Ultra Max, Heineken Silver, Amstel Grande, revived Kalyani Black Label).
BRAND.quote: We actually have hit the highest ever brand power on Ultra and Kingfisher

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year with revenue impact — Heineken Silver, Heineken Draught, Ultra Max, Amstel Grande, London Pilsner, Kalyani Black Label — but there is no disclosed R&D spend, no share-of-industry-R&D claim, and gross margins (42-44%) are not high enough to fund outsized innovation; it is portfolio/packaging extension rather than R&D dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: Our plan is t o expand our innovation like Heineken Silver innovation, Heineken Draught innovation

FORWARD.rationale: Regulation bars own stores, franchising or D2C, but UBL is pushing toward the customer through route-to-market changes (taking over from agency partners in Tamil Nadu/AP), a redesigned Maharashtra distribution network targeting next-day delivery from 62% to 95%, and 37,000 owned visi-coolers in trade.
FORWARD.quote: we have installed 2x number of fridges already... Our coolers penetration is now around 37,000 stores

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Premium share gain is persistent and quantified across the whole window — premium volumes +14% (Q3FY24), +32% FY25, +17% in a down Q2FY26 — with share still 'mid-single digit and growing' toward a stated 35% ambition, and share gains in Karnataka even as the category declined double digits.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our premium segment continued to do really well with volumes up 17% and also meaningful market share gains

CULTURE.rationale: Management does own bad news candidly — grading its own peak-season execution '7 out of 10', admitting 13 Maharashtra districts had zero distribution, disclosing flooded breweries and Q2FY26 disappointment — and kept investing through the downturn; but leadership has churned heavily (MD Pardal→Gupta, three CFOs Odink→Sikorsky→Kersten, multiple board exits) and repeated guidance of sustained 7-8% volume growth and improving margins ended in -3% volumes and EBIT down 18% in H1FY26.
CULTURE.quote: if you ask me , how did we execute that plan? I think 7 out of 10

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — 'one of the biggest brewery network in India', state-by-state excise licensing, interstate export restrictions and the Kingfisher heritage brand plus exclusive access to Heineken's global portfolio — but the same regulatory system caps pricing and returns, and well-funded rivals (AB InBev, the craft player) compete effectively, so the advantage is not clearly un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: beer is a lot of scale business. And we have one of the biggest brewery network in India

TOLLROAD.rationale: Far from a toll road: the bank is a price-taker in its most negotiated segment, repeatedly walking away from corporate loans because customers dictate the rate, and PSU exposure shrank ~Rs.6,000 crore on pricing alone (Jan 2026, May 2026).
TOLLROAD.quote: we have certain sanctions already in place, but because of the pricing issue, we are not able to disburse

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is only half-present: cost discipline is real and itemised (cost-to-income 60%+ down to 52.66%, surrendering 40,000 sq ft to save >Rs.2 crore rent, avoiding bulk deposits, leveraging TREPS) and loan quality has improved sharply (GNPA 7.89%→2.17%, PCR 98%), but the deposit franchise is not cheap — CASA has been stuck at ~38% versus an industry average management itself puts at 45-46%.
LOWPRICE.quote: our banks CASA which is around 38%, is low compared to the general banking average

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is externally determined — NIM moves with repo, deposit repricing and CD-ratio mechanics, and management concedes deposit rates are not falling in line with the repo cut (Jan 2026); corporate yields are set by borrower bargaining power, which management flagged as early as Feb 2023.
PRICING.quote: corporates, as you all know, have a better bargaining power to dictate interest rates to the banks

BRAND.rationale: There is heritage (founded 1943, 'Honours Your Trust', 4 crore customers, 3,412 branches, 61% rural/semi-urban) and improving service metrics, but no A&P spend, no premium pricing and no evidence the name commands anything beyond PSU trust; government holding of ~91% is the real depositor comfort.
BRAND.quote: Founded in 1943, UCO Bank has grown into one of the leading Public Sector Bank with a pan India presence

INNOVATION.rationale: Technology investment is named, disclosed and rising each year (IT spend Rs.576cr FY24 → 642cr FY25 → 899cr FY26, Project Parivartan with 31 digital journeys live, Rs.25,000 crore digital business, tab banking 66% of new accounts, WhatsApp banking 20 lakh users, Murex treasury), and it has visibly lifted efficiency — but this is catch-up digitisation funded by a thin-margin balance sheet, not R&D-led industry dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: in 2023–24, it was Rs.576 crore; in 2024–25, it was Rs.642 crore; and in 2025–26, it is Rs.899 crore

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Credit growth has run persistently above system for three years (16% FY24, 17.72% FY25, 19.44% FY26) with RAM up ~24-26% and business per branch rising Rs.155cr→173cr, and it has been gained while NPAs fell and credit cost dropped to 0.62% — but management never cites market-share numbers and deliberately caps ambition rather than pressing the advantage.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we don't want to outgrow beyond a reasonable margin

CULTURE.rationale: A four-year record of promises kept and conservatism: explicit guidance-vs-actual scorecards each year with every metric beaten (May 2026), bad news owned publicly ('we are the only bank where we had a negative operating profit in '22-23'), and buffer provisions built and deliberately not reversed — Rs.1,000cr in Nov 2024 rising to ~Rs.1,900cr of ECL/contingency/COVID buffers by May 2026, plus branch and IT commitments delivered on schedule.
CULTURE.quote: in '22-23 our operating profit was negative over the previous year. And we are the only bank where we had a negative operative profit

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing here a funded entrant could not rebuild: deposits are commoditised, the tech stack (Parivartan, Murex, WhatsApp banking, chatbot) is bought-in and explicitly benchmarked against peers, and the only genuinely un-replicable asset — the sovereign owner — is being diluted down toward 75%.
MOATTEST.quote: our Chatbot response is much better than the Chatbot of many other banks, which is just like a private sector banks Chatbot

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant requires cheap deposits and low operating cost; Ujjivan runs the opposite — FY26 cost of funds 7.2%, cost-to-income 65.6%, opex/ATA 6.4% and credit cost 2.2% of gross loan book, with no cost-obsession language anywhere across the 17 calls.
LOWPRICE.quote: opex to ATA for financial year '26 came in at 6.4%, and cost to income for financial year '26 at 65.6%

PRICING.rationale: NIM is structurally high (8.5% in FY26/Q1FY27) and management defends yields via ticket-size and geography mix, but the Jul 2026 call shows yields flat for 6-8 quarters and explicit competitive pressure rather than repeated above-inflation price increases; earlier calls describe 'risk-based pricing' and market-competitive rates, not scarcity or negligible elasticity.
PRICING.quote: it has been hovering around 12.2%, 12.3% for the last maybe six, seven, eight quarters... even if we want to increase the price, the market is not going to allow us

BRAND.rationale: A 16-year microfinance franchise with customer-facing brand investment (Hello Ujjivan vernacular app with 10 lakh+ downloads, Maxima CASA, Ivory HNI programme, planned branding spend in FY27), but the calls never evidence brand-driven premium pricing or share gain, and deposits are won on rate and service rather than heritage.
BRAND.quote: Hello Ujjivan app, India's first voice visual vernacular app launched for micro finance customers, is available in 11 languages

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent, named product launches with disclosed revenue impact across the period — micro mortgages, gold loans, vehicle finance, agri, supply chain finance, invoice discounting, Fast Track digital loan, co-branded card — plus rising tech/AI/analytics investment; but this is product extension in a commoditised lending market, with no R&D disclosure or industry-share-of-R&D dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: gold loans, vehicle finance, and agri banking, scaling up rapidly by 292%, 101%, and 126% Y-o-Y respectively... these 3 newer lines now contribute around 6% of our loan mix against 3% in the financial year 2025

SHAREGAIN.rationale: FY26 loan growth of 26.6% and deposit growth of 21.4% ran well ahead of system growth of 16% and 13.4% respectively, and Q1FY27 deposits grew 25%; but no explicit market-share figures or comparisons versus named competitors are given, and micro banking contracted materially in FY24-FY25 before recovering.
SHAREGAIN.quote: overall Bank credit recorded strong growth of 16%... while deposits increased by 13.4 percentages... The gross loan book reached INR40,655 crores, growing 26.6% Y-o-Y

CULTURE.rationale: Management flags bad news early and delivers stated targets — credit cost deterioration was pre-announced in FY25, the RBI's return of the universal bank application was disclosed plainly, and the multi-year promise to shift the mix to secured was delivered (30% in Jun-24 to 50.4% in Jun-26); against that, three MD changes in five years (Chugh, Davis, Nautiyal) plus chairman exit undercut the stable long-tenured leadership test.
CULTURE.quote: The regulator, while returning our application, has acknowledged our ongoing efforts towards diversification of our loan portfolio

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in the calls articulates why a funded newcomer could not replicate the model — the bank competes on rate in deposits, faces 'competitive pressure' on affordable-housing yields, and its own new lines (gold, vehicle, pre-owned cars, mid-corporate) are built from scratch in a few quarters, which is itself proof the barriers are low.
MOATTEST.quote: There is definitely some competitive pressure

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 17 calls the revenue model is one-off bagged/bulk cement sales; there is no discussion of attach rates, AMCs, renewals or deferred revenue, and the only negative-working-capital reference is about fuel inventory swings, not customer prepayment funding the business.
RECURRING.quote: After enjoying a long run of negative working capital, we ha d no choice but to give up the ga ins w ith rising costs

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through a vast trade channel — ~150,000 channel partners, 5,000+ dedicated UBS outlets, dedicated transporters — but management explicitly frames the decision-maker as the end customer (the individual home builder), and no trade training programmes or professional prescriber lock-in are described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The retail market is built around the individual customer IHP, the person, who decides what their house will be built with.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cement is a material input whose price is negotiated and tracked quarter by quarter — every call is dominated by regional price movements and realization per tonne — the opposite of an unnoticed sub-1% critical spend; no certification, standards or regulatory anchoring is claimed.
TOLLROAD.quote: gr ey cement pricing strengthened about 2.5% in most geographies

LOWPRICE.rationale: The cost culture is real and itemised — a 'specific, precise and measurable' efficiency programme covering WHRS, renewables to 1,897 MW, clinker conversion ratio, AFR mix and lead distance cut to 360 km — but the savings are retained/reinvested while the company deliberately prices at a premium, so this is scale-cost leadership, not low-price positioning.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our efficiency improvement program is very specific, precise and measurable.

PRICING.rationale: UltraTech consistently realizes above the industry through premiumisation, trade mix and brand premium, and by FY26 converted acquired B/C-grade brands to price-premium UltraTech volumes; but the record also includes genuine price deflation years (Q2 FY25 EBITDA/t at a 4–5 year low, putty prices 'taken a beating'), so pricing power is cyclical rather than unconditional.
PRICING.quote: converting the customers who were buying a B or C category brand of cement into a A category brand of cement willing to pay a price premium

BRAND.rationale: Brand premium is asserted and evidenced repeatedly from Oct 2022 through Jul 2026 — superior realization versus peers every quarter, 19–21% brand volume growth, and the ICL/Kesoram brand migration converting acquired volumes to premium realization — supported by decades of consistency and adjacency stretch (Birla White, putty, construction chemicals, cables & wires).
BRAND.quote: UltraTech is a brand that customers trust. Decades of consistent delivery, bag after bag, site after site

INNOVATION.rationale: There is steady product-mix innovation — value-added products above 18% of sales, white-cement-based liquid primer, putty capacity, GreenPro/EPD-certified green portfolio, and now cables & wires — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed and no claim to a share of industry R&D is made.
INNOVATION.quote: va lue added product is continuously going up. It's reached more than 18% now.

FORWARD.rationale: Clear movement toward the customer — 477 RMC plants, 5,000+ dedicated UBS outlets, an expanding bulk-terminal network (Lucknow, JNPT, Mangalore, Cochin) and an owned Gujarat jetty — yet these remain distribution/dealer assets with no disclosed own-store sales share, franchise royalties or D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: 477 RMC plants, 5,000 -plus UBS stores, which are dedicated dealers

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is quantified call after call — capacity from ~65 mt (2016) to 200 mt (2026) reached a year early, plus a quarter-by-quarter volume comparison against the rest of the industry, and it is explicitly gained profitably (EBITDA/t consistently above industry), not bought with price.
SHAREGAIN.quote: December '25 quarter, we grew 15%, industry grew half our growth. March '26, we grew 9%, industry growing again less than half our growth.

CULTURE.rationale: The promise-to-delivery record across the 5 years is explicit and checkable — 131 mt by FY23, 157/159 mt by FY25, 200 mt (delivered a year early), ICL/Kesoram brand migration (a quarter early), cables & wires on schedule and budget — alongside prompt bad-news disclosure ('let me talk about all the negatives first'), long-tenured leadership (Atul Daga CFO throughout), capex fully from internal accruals and net debt/EBITDA held below 1x.
CULTURE.quote: We said we will cross 200 million tons; we did a year early. We said we would complete brand migration of India C ements and Kesoram, we did a quarter early

MOATTEST.rationale: Management articulates concrete, non-replicable barriers: secured limestone behind every committed tonne of expansion, 76 operating facilities with ~2,000 warehouses and 150,000 channel partners, and the arithmetic that greenfield capacity costs $110–120/t and takes 7 years — a well-funded copycat cannot rebuild a 200 mt footprint or the reserve base in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: Every ton of committed expansion at UltraTech is fully backed by secured limestone.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is partly visible in the FY26 calls — a deliberate churn out of ~INR70,000 crores of bulk deposits into CASA/retail term deposits, cost of deposits down 18bps, cost-to-income down ~500bps — but the asset quality history (GNPA 10.22% in Jun 2022, credit cost above 2%) undercuts the 'high-quality loans' leg, and CASA at 35% is not a structurally cheap-funding franchise.
LOWPRICE.quote: my average cost would be somewhere 4.5 or maybe 4.75 levels... the deposit cost has reduced by 18 bps

PRICING.rationale: A price-taker: NIM fell from 3.05% (Jul 2024) to 2.70% and then 2.64% as repo cuts passed through, and management's stated ambition is only to 'defend' NIM, with yield on advances declining and MCLR resets limited to 25bps.
PRICING.quote: the NIM of our bank which was 2.91 is right now at 2.70... we want to defend our NIM

BRAND.rationale: No premium pricing or brand-led share gain anywhere across the 17 calls; growth is defended by rate competitiveness and CASA campaigns, and deposits grew just 2.72% YoY in FY26 while analysts repeatedly flag lagging business growth versus peers.
BRAND.quote: we are very competitive in the market with regard to deposit rate

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent share loss rather than gain: Jul 2024 deposits +8.5% vs system 10.6% and advances +11.5% vs system 13.9%, FY26 deposits +2.72% YoY, with management aiming merely to hold share ('keep our market share at the existing level').
SHAREGAIN.quote: SCBs reported 10.6% YoY deposit growth and 13.9% growth in credit vis-à-vis our Bank reported 8.5% growth in deposits and 11.5% growth in advances

CULTURE.rationale: Genuine positives: explicit guidance-versus-actual scorecards, sustained delivery on the asset-quality promise (GNPA 10.22% Jun-2022 → 2.82% Mar-2026, PCR 93.5%), prompt disclosure of frauds and of one-off standard-asset provisions, and conservative buffering (INR700 crores contingency). Offset by government ownership with rotating MD/ED and short chairman tenure rather than stable long-tenured leadership.
CULTURE.quote: we have kept INR 700 crores of an additional provision, general provision sort of... it is not like any dent or any suspicion on the book

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing on the calls articulates why a competitor could not replicate the franchise — the levers described (branch openings, retail/MSME loan points, verticals, relationship managers, premium CASA branches) are all buyable, and private banks are visibly taking the deposit share.
MOATTEST.quote: We have opened about 215 Retail loan points to push Retail

RECURRING.rationale: Nothing in the call touches recurring/subscription revenue, attach rates, renewals or customer advances as a funding source; the model is one-off spirits sales through state route-to-market.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is built through experiential/on-trade channels where bartenders and outlets shape choice — roughly a third of business is on-premise and management is investing in on-trade execution — but there is no professional prescriber economics or trade training programme described, and the end consumer is directly targeted via mass media and celebrity campaigns.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: it is a very, very important channel where you can drive sampling and build habit over a period of time... that's where roughly one-third of our business happens

TOLLROAD.rationale: United Spirits is a branded consumer product bought and paid for by the drinker, not a small-share critical input to a customer's cost base; the call is about consumer aspiration, penetration and excise policy, not certification or oligopoly toll economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: what is good for the consumer is good for Diageo India

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated strategy is the opposite — premiumisation up the ladder with 70% of growth from the top half of the portfolio; the productivity programme funds A&P and margin, not lower prices.
LOWPRICE.quote: 70% of our growth is coming from the top half of the portfolio, which kind of suggests that the premiumization ladder is very much intact

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly frames brand-building as creating pricing power and had three good years of headline pricing (~2%) plus revenue growth management, but pricing is state-legislated and lumpy — only 0.2–0.3% a year through FY17–22 — and they guide it to moderate and intend to pass the entire Scotch duty cut to consumers rather than keep it.
PRICING.quote: 5 years from 2017 to 2022, we had headline pricing of the average of 0.2% to 0.3%... The last 3 years, it's been in the range of 2%

BRAND.rationale: The portfolio is built on heritage trademarks (Johnnie Walker, Black Dog, McDowell's — the world's largest selling whisky at 30 million cases) with sustained A&P at 9–10% of sales that management wants to grow, equity leadership measured against named competitors, and repeated adjacency launches under the same names (McDowell's X-series, Double Oaked Barrel, flavoured vodka).
BRAND.quote: Black Dog continues to maintain its equity leadership in the BII Scotch segment, 1.3x to the nearest competitor

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a named annual innovation calendar (X-series, Don Julio, Godawan, flavoured Smirnoff, pocket packs) and a stated ambition to double innovation's NSV contribution from high-single/low-double digit over 3–5 years, but no R&D spend is disclosed and execution is admittedly patchy — X-series is only in 5 markets a year after launch.
INNOVATION.quote: Our target over the next 3 to 5 years is to double the innovation contribution to growth in NSV, which currently is at a high single digit, low double digit

FORWARD.rationale: Route to market is legislated and retail is state- or licensee-controlled; management's complaint is precisely that restrictive route-to-market policy blocks access, and the only distribution 'wins' come from excise reform doubling third-party outlets, not from any owned stores, franchising or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: some restrictive route-to-market policies in Delhi and some other states has hindered our brand presence

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share regained to national levels in Andhra on re-entry after a 5-year hiatus and equity leadership at 1.3x the nearest BII Scotch competitor, but management concedes multi-year share loss in the large UP market and much of FY25 growth was Andhra re-entry (3.1 of 8.2 points of NSV growth) rather than broad share gain.
SHAREGAIN.quote: for the last few years, we have struggled to really grow our share in that state

CULTURE.rationale: The CFO delivered a margin goal promised across a decade (high-teens EBITDA, ROCE 26.4%, EPS above INR20 for the first time) and openly flags bad news — subdued demand, UP share struggles, slow X-series rollout, moderating luxury growth — but leadership has churned (Kripalu out, Someshwar in three months, CFO subsequently exiting) and this is a subsidiary of Diageo rather than a long-tenured family/employee-owned culture.
CULTURE.quote: Our EBITDA margin, I have to say, is in the high-teen range now, something that we have been talking over the last 10 years. So, we are finally there.

MOATTEST.rationale: The advantages are genuinely hard to rebuild: aged Scotch inventory and global trademarks like Johnnie Walker, Black Dog and Lagavulin cannot be manufactured quickly, a 30-million-case anchor brand plus state-by-state licensing and route-to-market approvals block fast entry, and management notes each state needs its own clearances before a product can even ship.
MOATTEST.quote: Each state is unique, and you need to... make sure that you get the legislation and all clearances before you take it to market

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls the business is one-time component sales to OEMs (93% of revenue by Q1 FY25), with aftermarket at only 7-9% and no licence fees, AMCs, subscriptions, attach rates or renewal metrics; working capital is a cash drain funded by rising debt, the opposite of customer-funded negative working capital.
RECURRING.quote: Finance costs for the quarter increased to INR36 crores due to higher borrowings to fund capex, land acquisitions and working capital.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The calls are silent on professional recommenders, installers or trade training programmes; specification is done by OEM engineering teams who are also the paying customer, and no channel-professional dynamic is described.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Products are designed into a model and stay for its life, and regulatory anchoring repeatedly creates captive demand (AVAS mandate from Oct 2026, side/curtain airbags via TG, LED transition), but the components are a meaningful share of vehicle cost (INR 90,000-95,000 kit value) and pricing is actively negotiated with OEMs rather than accepted without question.
TOLLROAD.quote: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has notified mandatory implementation of acoustic vehicle alerting systems called as AVAS for electric vehicles

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly leans on India's structural cost advantage, localisation depth and operational efficiency to hold ~11% margins through commodity and energy shocks (Aug 2022 gas costs, May 2026 input volatility), but there is no itemised cost-saving culture or no-frills scale model of the classic Low Price Plus kind.
LOWPRICE.quote: We have managed to maintain these margins despite a volatile input cost environment, reflecting our disciplined focus on operational efficiencies.

PRICING.rationale: Price moves are cost pass-throughs negotiated with OEMs, not above-inflation increases: EBITDA margin was 10.4% in Q1 FY23 and 11.1-11.3% in FY26, essentially flat across four years, with earnings growth coming from volume, capacity and kit-value mix rather than price.
PRICING.quote: commodity, I think we are happy that we have been able to pass fully actually

BRAND.rationale: The Aug 2022 rebrand to UNO Minda with the 'Driving the New' tagline, focused aftermarket branding across 44,000+ retailers, and the Minda family heritage give real B2B and replacement-market brand equity, but there is no consumer A&P spend, premium pricing or brand-led adjacency evidence in the calls.
BRAND.quote: The renaming initiative will further strengthen and unify the brand UNO Minda.

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products arrive every year with revenue impact (Roof Star Liner and TFT versions, illuminated logo, TPMS, AVAS, sunroof, e-Axle/EDU, DHT) backed by the in-house CREAT centre, but much of the technology is licensed in via TLAs and JVs (FRIWO, StarCharge, Inovance, Aisin) and R&D spend as a share of sales is never disclosed, so this is technology assembly more than R&D-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: continuous addition of emerging technologies through our in-house R&D center CREAT combined with globally renowned partners

FORWARD.rationale: The aftermarket division has been built out toward the end user — 620 cities, 1,400+ business partners, 44,000+ retailers, own-brand marketing and new categories like alloy wheels and seats — but there are no own stores, franchise royalties or D2C economics, and aftermarket's share of revenue actually fell from 9% (Q1 FY23) to ~6% (Q1 FY25).
FORWARD.quote: covering 620 cities in India with 1,400 plus business partners. We now have 44,000 plus retailers on board

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified outperformance of industry volumes in every year of the record — 59% vs 37% industry in Q1 FY23, 20% and 18% revenue growth against a strong FY26 industry, 2-wheeler switch growth of 26-30% on rising share of business, lighting share gains, and a new 2-wheeler lighting order worth ~INR 450 crores (25% of current 2W lighting revenue) explicitly to raise share of business.
SHAREGAIN.quote: supported by sustained market share gains built over the past few years

CULTURE.rationale: Exceptionally stable leadership (Nirmal Minda as Chairman/CMD and Sunil Bohra as Group CFO presenting all 16 calls), guidance delivered as promised (11% ± 50bps margin held from FY23 through FY26; Bawal, Supa, Khed, Kharkhoda and Indonesia capacities commissioned on the timelines announced years earlier), and candour about bad news — the FY26 call openly flagged alloy wheel penetration softness and customers switching back to steel wheels, and the INR 28 crore labour-code hit was disclosed separately rather than buried.
CULTURE.quote: As promised, we have continued to outperform the industry with 59% growth against industry volume growth of 37% year-on-year basis.

MOATTEST.rationale: Barriers are real but not un-replicable: decades-old JV web with Japanese and global tier-1s (Denso Ten, Roki, TG, Tachi-S, Aisin, Inovance), OEM design-in qualification, and heavy capital intensity (INR 764 crore alloy wheel plant, INR 550 crore EV powertrain plant) — yet the company itself keeps buying capability through licences, which shows a well-funded entrant can do the same.
MOATTEST.quote: In June '24, we have further entered into TLA with Suzhou Inovance Automotive for manufacture and sale of select high-voltage category electric vehicle products

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls the revenue discussion is entirely one-off product sales (volume x price) plus a cost-plus CMO arm; no attach rates, AMC/licence/subscription streams, renewal rates or deferred revenue-as-funding are ever discussed. Working capital is a cash drain (116 days at Dec-2025), not customer-funded.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through distributors, dealers and retailers who influence the grower, and management repeatedly thanks 'channel partners' and cites field trials that convert growers (Feb 2026 on Feroce). But the channel is transactional, not a locked-in professional prescriber base — the same calls report rebates, returns, credit-driven sales postponement and ECL provisions on distributors.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: our constituents who are distributors, dealers, and farmers

TOLLROAD.rationale: Crop protection is a large, negotiated line in a farmer's cost base, and the calls show the opposite of toll-road economics: 14% price decline (Aug 2024), Chinese overcapacity, MIP/anti-dumping petitions, and customers switching on price. No certification/standards anchoring anywhere.
TOLLROAD.quote: persistent pricing pressure in most molecules, limiting value recovery

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost story — India-based backward integration, $100m SG&A savings target in FY25, capacity utilisation and input-cost gains lifting contribution margin 220bps in FY26 — but scale has not produced high asset turns or strong returns; leverage peaked at 4.6x net debt/EBITDA in FY24 with a credit downgrade.
LOWPRICE.quote: from a quality, reliability and a cost standpoint, we can compete against anybody in the world

PRICING.rationale: The record is sustained price deflation, not pricing power: FY25 opened with a 14% price decline against 16% volume growth, and by FY26 the premium brand Sperto is suffering price erosion while management explicitly rules out material price increases.
PRICING.quote: I don't think there's going to be very material price increase opportunities

BRAND.rationale: Named brands exist and occasionally defend position (glufosinate in India 'we are not competing with the other generics'; Feroce, Propose, Constel gaining traction in Brazil), but the flagship Sperto lost price, and there is no heritage premium or sustained A&P-driven share-plus-price combination.
BRAND.quote: we think we have a different position in terms of the brand

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is named and quantified — new-launch revenue targets rising $85m (FY25) to over $130m (FY26, exceeded), Flupyrimin, Preview, a claimed 30% IP-protected portfolio — but it is funded off ~37-43% contribution margins in a post-patent business, and R&D spend is never disclosed as a share of sales or industry.
INNOVATION.quote: on track to exceed our $130 million revenue target for new product launches this year

FORWARD.rationale: Repeated moves toward the customer — the Origeo JV with Bunge to sell direct to large Brazilian growers (Aug 2022), a deliberate B2C transition in Southeast Asia and at Advanta, DECCO post-harvest integration — but no own-store counts, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share are ever quantified.
FORWARD.quote: our southeast Asia business where we're transitioning that business to a B2C model

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed persistently and volume growth supports it (25% volume growth Q1 FY25, 66% North America revenue growth, FY26 revenue +11% 'largely led by volume'), but the claims are never backed with explicit share percentages versus named competitors, and some gain came alongside credit losses and ECL provisions in LATAM.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we continue to gain share in most key regions as the market normalizes

CULTURE.rationale: Poor mid-cycle record — FY23 guidance was raised to 12-15% revenue/15-18% EBITDA and 80 working-capital days promised, then FY24 brought a 32% EBITDA collapse, a credit downgrade and years of heavy leadership churn (multiple chairmen, CFO and CEO exits) — but FY25-FY26 shows visible repair: bad news owned, guidance beaten (11% vs 4-8%; 18% EBITDA vs 10-14%), debt cut 48%, and an explicit list of investor criticisms addressed point by point.
CULTURE.quote: there were five [key] feedback or inputs which were given to us, and I would like to call those feedback that were given

MOATTEST.rationale: The claimed barriers — backward integration and supply-chain scale — were tested and failed: Chinese overcapacity drove multi-year price erosion, EBITDA down 28-32%, a ratings downgrade and a rights issue, and by Feb 2026 management still describes overcapacity as the anchor on the market. Nothing described is un-replicable by a well-funded competitor.
MOATTEST.quote: This market reality is anchored by continued overcapacity in China

RECURRING.rationale: Native sells water purifiers and smart locks upfront and then earns recurring filter-replacement and service revenue off the installed base, with 75% of first-cycle cohorts renewing through UC (May 2026 and Aug 2026 calls); but there is no discussion of deferred revenue, advance billing or negative working capital, and it is confined to one small segment.
RECURRING.quote: about 75% of them are renewing filters through us, which adds a recurring, higher-margin revenue stream

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The service professional is the face of the transaction and UC invests heavily in selection, onboarding, training and SOPs to make that expert the differentiator, but the customer still chooses and pays UC directly rather than being steered by an independent professional.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: the quality of the service professional, the training, the effort that you put into selection, onboarding, the details that you go in into SOPs

TOLLROAD.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of certification, standards, industry-body anchoring, or a product that is a tiny-but-critical share of a customer's cost base.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The 'faster, cheaper, better' densification flywheel explicitly lowers cost-to-serve and passes value to customers while margins expand (core adj. EBITDA 3.3%→4.1%→6.9% of NTV across FY26–Q1FY27), but current low prices in InstaHelp come from subsidy rather than a replicable cost culture — management admits it is 'artificially subsidising orders'.
LOWPRICE.quote: the cost to serve for the entire business comes down. Some of these benefits can also be enjoyed by the customer in terms of better value

PRICING.rationale: The evidence points the other way in the fastest-growing segment: InstaHelp AOVs keep falling, discounts have at times equalled NTV, and management concedes prices must eventually 'correct' upward with likely volume loss — the opposite of pricing power.
PRICING.quote: average order value continues to, you know, get lower... When will the pricing correct to its full potential? Very difficult for us to say

BRAND.rationale: Trust and consistency are the stated core asset (4.8/5 ratings, 'in businesses of trust, it's a winner-take-all') and the name has been stretched into Native, Revamp and InstaHelp with brand-marketing spend behind new user acquisition; but there is no heritage story and no evidence of premium pricing — the opposite in InstaHelp.
BRAND.quote: Generally speaking, I'm of the view that in businesses of trust, It's a winner-take-all

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches each year (Native water purifiers and smart locks, Revamp, UC Instant) with disclosed revenue impact, and Native's elevated losses are explicitly attributed to R&D for new products, plus a broad AI layer (100% image audits, 55% of partner support, 90%+ of code); but R&D spend is not quantified and margins are thin rather than high-gross-margin-funded.
INNOVATION.quote: Some of the elevated losses are on the count of R&D for new products

FORWARD.rationale: UC designs its own Native products and sells and services them entirely through its own app and service network, owning the customer journey end to end, with AI-driven filter-replacement outreach; but there is no store/franchise economics or D2C-share disclosure of the classic forward-integrator kind.
FORWARD.quote: a clear ability to have a connectedness back with the Urban Company app and own the consumer journey throughout the usage lifecycle

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Core India NTV growth accelerated four straight quarters (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%) with margins simultaneously expanding, management claims 'the lion's share' of the core market and 'clear market leadership' in InstaHelp, and international grew 75-84% with a localised playbook; the caveat is that InstaHelp share is being bought with ₹132cr/quarter of subsidy, which management openly calls artificial.
SHAREGAIN.quote: In our Core business, we have th lion's share of the market

CULTURE.rationale: Across all four calls management set explicit guardrails (FY26 margins flat vs FY25, breakeven by Q3 FY28, ₹1,000cr adj. EBITDA by FY31) and reiterated them while delivering the promised core margin expansion; they own bad news plainly — failed Australia/US entries, past products like Cooks that 'did not work', and their own subsidy behaviour — hold a ₹2,000cr net-cash balance sheet, and name free cash flow per share as the North Star.
CULTURE.quote: And Urban Company is as guilty of doing this as everybody else

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barrier is 12 years of supply density built across 50-60 service categories times hundreds of micro-markets, which management calls simple in concept but 'very hard to execute' and which enables UC Instant 30-60 minute fulfilment; but well-funded competitors are actively contesting InstaHelp with the same playbook, so the barrier is demonstrated rather than proven un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: seems like a simple playbook, but it's very hard to execute across so many services and so many micro-markets

RECURRING.rationale: Wire ropes are consumables with repeat/replacement demand, and management points to rigging shops and value-added services raising 'customer stickiness' plus repeat orders in Saudi and Ocean Fibre; but there are no attach rates, AMC/renewal metrics or customer advances, and working capital is heavily positive (194-209 days), the opposite of a customer-funded model.
RECURRING.quote: Focus on value-added services for customers through our dedicated rigging shops in Europe, Middle East, Southeast Asia, thereby also improving customer stickiness and margins.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is largely specified through OEMs and channel partners rather than end-user marketing — OEM approvals in elevators and cranes, European OEMs generating orders for ropes used worldwide — but there is no professional training programme or trade-channel investment of the classic dentist/installer type.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we are also working on more OEM approvals in the value-added segment, which is our focus, for example, in elevators, cranes

TOLLROAD.rationale: Across all 12 calls the value-added rope business is described as safety-critical, engineering-specified and approval-gated, with long qualification cycles and low price sensitivity once converted — plasticated LRPC needs approvals from 'two or three big players', mining ropes converted trials into a three-year contract, and Q3 FY26 explicitly calls the demand 'less price led'.
TOLLROAD.quote: higher traction in elevator ropes, crane ropes and oil and offshore ropes, where requirements are more engineering-driven and less price led... customer qualification cycles are longer, but once established, they tend to be more stable and recurring

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is real cost obsession under 'One Usha Martin' (fixed employee costs -3%, admin -7% in FY26), but it is deployed to widen margins on premium products, not to pass savings to price; management deliberately walks away from low-price general-purpose ropes rather than competing on cost.
LOWPRICE.quote: there are certain low-value general purpose Wire Ropes where realizations are not as attractive and because our focus is on the value-added side, that is some area that we have seen volumes stay stable or decreasing

PRICING.rationale: Realisations rose even when steel prices fell (Nov 2023), and in FY26 rising steel, gas and logistics costs were passed through across wire, LRPC and rope while margins still expanded — EBITDA/ton went from ~INR 31,178 (Q2 FY24) to ~INR 39,500 (Q4 FY26) and margin guidance was raised from 18-19% to a 20% minimum.
PRICING.quote: we have been able to pass on a large part of the increases combined with better product mix. So... we have been able to expand our margins even in this situation where prices have been increasing

BRAND.rationale: The Brunton Shaw UK brand is used as a premium wrapper for Ranchi-made ropes and management says this integrated model lifted share with premium OEMs, and 'Ocean Fibre' has been established as a new brand; but there is no meaningful A&P spend, heritage narrative or consumer-style distributor leverage discussed.
BRAND.quote: All of the changes we made in terms of the integrated model between the Ranchi manufacturing and the Brunton Shaw brand, have started giving us dividends... It has helped us increase our share with the premium customers

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady cadence of named new products with revenue impact — GALSTAR coated wire, plasticated LRPC, Ocean Fibre synthetic slings (cash positive in year one) — plus a Global Development Centre R&D setup and R&D teams co-developing with customers; but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and gross margins fund capex more than research.
INNOVATION.quote: Our commercial production of ocean fiber has begun, making our entry into the synthetic sling space for offshore lifting... reflects our long-term commitment to product innovation

FORWARD.rationale: The company is moving toward the end customer — dedicated rigging shops in Europe, the Middle East and South-East Asia, direct exports from Ranchi to European customers bypassing the BSUK plant, and inorganic plans in 'rigging and helping us to get close to the customers' — but there are no own stores, franchising or D2C economics disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: we have commenced direct exports from India to the European customers, enabling improved service levels, and enhanced cost efficiency

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit share figures are given and some rise — domestic 65-70%, US moved from 2-3% to 'sub 5%' with US revenue share going 7%→9%, Europe from 8-9% — and 60 new Saudi customers were added; but consolidated rope volumes have been broadly flat to +5% for three years with Europe flat, so share gain is not yet persistent or volume-evident.
SHAREGAIN.quote: still our market share in the U.S. is sub 5%. So, there is tremendous opportunity for growth

CULTURE.rationale: Rajeev Jhawar has led throughout with family ownership and a stable team, bad news is disclosed promptly and quantified (INR 4 crore redundancy, INR 13 crore Wage Code cost, the 900-ton Middle East volume miss, admitted margin shortfalls versus the 18% target), and multi-year promises were delivered: Ranchi capex completed, working capital reversed from 209 to 194 days, net debt of INR 124 crore turned into net cash of INR 332 crore, ROCE explicitly tracked at 20.6%.
CULTURE.quote: we closed the year with a consolidated net cash position of INR 332 crore and with standalone operations now entirely debt free... ROCE improved to 20.6% from 19.3%

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuine time-based barriers exist in the value-added niches — multi-year OEM approval cycles, accumulated field-performance references, and equipment capability such as the largest single-reel rope run at Ranchi — but management concedes Asian competitors pressure the general-purpose end on price, so the un-replicable portion covers only part of the business.
MOATTEST.quote: We have built references and field performance data in these segments over time, and the track record now lets us approach a wider set of customers.

RECURRING.rationale: AMC revenue is an annuity on installed AUM and the SIP book behaves like a subscription that management tracks closely across all 12 calls (SIP AUM Rs 17,788 cr in Q1FY23 to Rs 45,595 cr by Q1FY27, 29.53 lakh active SIP folios), but there is no upfront product sale, no deferred revenue/customer-advance funding, and yields on the base keep eroding.
