RECURRING.quote: Our SIP AUM witnessed a growth of 5.91% over the corresponding quarter of last year, reaching to Rs. 39,813 crores as of March '26

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are overwhelmingly intermediated — MFDs, banks and national distributors choose the scheme while the investor pays — and management repeatedly describes distributor engagement, 106 fund-manager meetings, and distributor education programmes as the core channel investment across FY24–FY27 calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: 30% is direct, while 60% to 70% comes from the MFD

TOLLROAD.rationale: The management fee is the customer's cost, not a trivial input, and even the institutional mandates (EPFO, CMPFO) are re-won through open competitive bidding every five years; TER cuts and a 5 bps exit-load change are absorbed and pushed onto intermediaries rather than ignored by customers.
TOLLROAD.quote: both the EPFO and CMPFO concluded the process of appointing new portfolio managers through an open bidding system

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine, itemised cost obsession — VRS, headcount down from 1,402 (Mar-24) to 1,248 (Mar-26), supervisor-to-feet-on-street from 1:1 to 1:5, 31% lower cost per transaction, branch expansion at 'net zero incremental cost' — and a large low-fee passive book, but scale advantage is absent since the firm is losing share rather than converting cost into volume.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our total employee strength, which stood at 1,402 employees as of March 2024, is now at 1,248 as of March 2026

PRICING.rationale: The record is one of persistent price deflation: blended yield fell from 40–41 bps in FY23 with guided further dilution, equity/hybrid yield went from 76 bps (FY25 guidance) to 72–73 bps in Q1FY27, and mix shift into 8 bps ETFs drags realisation further.
PRICING.quote: we may see some bit of dilu tion in the management yield number going forward

BRAND.rationale: UTI has real, un-replicable heritage — 60+ years, EPFO/NPS institutional trust, 699-district reach — and stretches the name across MF, pension, alternatives and international, but the brand delivers neither premium pricing nor share gain, which is the pattern's proof test.
BRAND.quote: speaks back to the origins of UTI more than 60 years ago

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur annually (Balanced Advantage FY24, smart beta suite, G-Sec ETFs, Multicap FY26 raising ~Rs 1,000 cr, SDOF III/IV, MOF II) alongside heavy digital build — VAANI AI contact centre, WhatsApp payments, robo-advisory — but there is no disclosed R&D-style spend, no pricing power from it, and gross margins are compressing rather than funding dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: we recently launched one of the industry's first AI -powered contact centre solutions , VAANI , which has already automated 59% of our inbound calls

FORWARD.rationale: UTI does own its route to the investor — ~270 branches/UFCs with ~90 added in 18 months, 108 of 167 UFCs in B30 back in FY23, direct digital platform 'UTI HART' with 60.9 lakh digital purchase transactions in June 2026 and 76% of new SIPs registered digitally — but direct remains only ~30% of equity/hybrid AUM and the economics still run through distributors.
FORWARD.quote: since we have expanded close to around 90 UFCs in the last one and a half years

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share has drifted down across the whole four-year window rather than up: gross-sales share fell from 8.5% (Q1FY23) to 7.79% (FY24) to 6.1% (FY26) and 5.5% in Q4FY26, while NPS share slid from 27.37% (FY22) to 24.16% (Q1FY27) — the new CEO's own framing is that growth is still an aspiration.
SHAREGAIN.quote: UTI was able to capture a market share of 5.5% of the gross sales of the industry during this quarter

CULTURE.rationale: Positives are real — specific, quantified disclosure of one-offs (Rs 130 cr VRS, Rs 25 cr family pension, Rs 4 cr Labour Code), a ~95% dividend payout, cost promises actually delivered — but leadership has churned heavily (three chairmen and multiple MD/CEO/CFO changes over FY22–FY26) and the repeated promise across calls to grow high-yield assets and regain equity share has not been delivered.
CULTURE.quote: there is a one -off on account of VR S and family pension. The total quantum of that is close to around Rs. 130 crores

MOATTEST.rationale: Some hard-to-rebuild assets exist — a 699-district distribution footprint, 60-year brand, and repeat institutional mandates (EPFO third consecutive term, CMPFO second) — yet a well-funded new AMC has demonstrably been taking share and yield from UTI over these four years, so the barrier is not proving durable in practice.
MOATTEST.quote: For the third consecutive term, UTI AMC was selected as one of the portfolio managers for EPFO

RECURRING.rationale: Management explicitly disclaims recurring service/AMC income, handing annual maintenance economics to dealers instead, and working capital is inventory-heavy (83 days in FY26, inventory 108 days) rather than customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: the company does not focus much on its revenue page that we earn on yearly maintenance

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all three calls sales run through distributors/dealers/Shoppe franchisees who also do installation, supported by 600+ field service engineers who train the trade, and margin on AMC is deliberately left to the channel to keep partners loyal.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The installation is done by the dealer distributor... we keep the earnings in the scope of the dealer distributor. So that they can earn some money and they can continue to trust us.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is the customer's whole capital purchase — a rooftop solar power generating system for a middle-class household — not a tiny, critical share of a customer's cost base, and there is no certification/standards anchoring beyond mandatory BIS/DCR compliance (where the company is itself under BIS question on 10-15 SKUs).
TOLLROAD.quote: our customers are middle class, lower middle class basically

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost discipline is real and itemised — cell line delivered for ~Rs.300cr against a Rs.400cr budget, employee costs down 0.6% and other opex down 0.1% of revenue, backward integration lifting material margin 1.6% in FY26 — but the model is value-for-money at ~18.5% EBITDA margins, not a no-frills low-price scale play.
LOWPRICE.quote: we had targeted total budget of solar cell line was around Rs. 400 crores, while we completed this line in around Rs. 300 crores

PRICING.rationale: Management states input cost moves are simply passed through, and confirms FY26's 70% revenue growth was entirely volume with no price realisation — margin gains came from backward integration, not pricing.
PRICING.quote: if our revenue is gone up 70%, then in gigawatt also it is around 70% up

BRAND.rationale: 30-year heritage, ~1 million customers, twin UTL Solar/Fujiyama brands and a new cricketer brand ambassador point to real consumer trust and A&P investment, but the brand delivers word-of-mouth and distribution rather than any price premium (management calls price 'competitive').
BRAND.quote: This reflects brand equity that we have built in the market, where word-of-mouth and local reputation drive purchase decisions

INNOVATION.rationale: 500+ SKUs, a service-engineer-to-R&D feedback loop and three years of AI in the sales network show incremental product breadth, but no R&D spend is disclosed, no named launches with revenue impact, and the Mono-PERC-over-TOPCon choice was explicitly a speed/cost decision on established technology rather than technology leadership.
INNOVATION.quote: the rest of the innovation is that we are adopting AI in our sales network. We have been working on AI for 3 years

FORWARD.rationale: The exclusive Shoppe format is a genuine move toward the customer — 20 added in Q3 and 30 in Q4 within an 8,900-strong partner network — but no own-store share of sales, franchise royalty economics or D2C revenue is disclosed, and online is described as immaterial.
FORWARD.quote: we added over 80 distributors, more than 450 dealers, and 30 exclusive Shoppe outlets

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth of 72-88% YoY against an industry CAGR management itself puts at 40-43% implies share gain, and 400,000+ households were added in FY26, but no explicit share numbers are given and the Chairman candidly attributed past growth to market expansion rather than share.
SHAREGAIN.quote: I mean, market share did not increase, the market increased

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on the Dec call were delivered by Feb (Dadri 1GW cell line commissioned in six months, under budget), and bad news is disclosed promptly and specifically — the Bawal fire, BIS seizures on 10-15 SKUs, and the Ratlam battery/inverter delays with reasons — alongside a conservative 0.25 net debt/equity and founder-led continuity.
CULTURE.quote: the commissioning of power electronics and battery capacities saw some delays

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulated barrier — a channel of 8,900 partners plus 600+ service engineers built over 30 years in Tier 2/3 towns, now paired with cell-to-system integration — is a plausible time-based moat, but management openly concedes the field is wide open to well-funded entrants like Tata Power.
MOATTEST.quote: We believe this structure, developed over the years, remains a key differentiator that is difficult to duplicate

RECURRING.rationale: Across all nine calls V2 Retail's revenue is purely transactional apparel sales through own stores — no licence, AMC, subscription or renewal stream is ever mentioned, and management explicitly confirms there is no loyalty/recurring construct. Negative working capital comes from vendor credit and bill discounting, not customer advances.
RECURRING.quote: We don't have a loyalty program per se, but we have a database of about 8 crore customers

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct-to-consumer in company-operated value-fashion stores; there is no prescriber, installer or trade professional in the chain, and the only trade-channel investment described is vendor training on delivery reliability, not demand recommendation.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we did a lot of knowledge transfer and training to our vendors. So earlier our on-time delivery used to be just 40%

TOLLROAD.rationale: Apparel is a discretionary end-consumer purchase, not a small-but-critical input to a customer's cost base, and management describes an openly contested market rather than a rational oligopoly with switching inertia.
TOLLROAD.quote: out of 304 stores that we have now, there would be less than 20 stores where we do not have any organized competition. Because competition has become the new reality

LOWPRICE.rationale: The entire model is low price plus quality and variety, with gross margin deliberately capped at 28–29% and benefits passed to the customer while returns come from asset turns (PSF rising Rs 854 → Rs 1,017 → Rs 1,200; breakeven at Rs 500 PSF) and tight cost lines (rent Rs 52/sqft, total cost Rs 190/sqft, marketing <1% of sales). ROE improved 10.7% (FY24) → 23.2% (FY25) → 26% (FY26) on this formula, repeated consistently across FY25–FY26 calls.
LOWPRICE.quote: our gross margin strategy is by design. We want to pass on most of the benefits to the consumer... all the margin expansion should happen from operating leverage and from higher sales per square feet

PRICING.rationale: V2 can pass raw-material inflation through (3–4% MRP increase on yarn costs while holding gross margin) without expected volume loss, but it explicitly refuses price-led margin expansion and competes on being the cheapest at its quality benchmark with ASP of about Rs 300 — the opposite of premiumisation.
PRICING.quote: we won't absorb it in gross margins because 3%-4% increase is not significant and if our average selling price is Rs. 300 that translates to about Rs. 10-Rs. 12 additional MRP

BRAND.rationale: Management is deliberately building private-label brands (40% → 60% → 85%, targeting 100%) with size standardisation and quality trust, and the V2 name carries a stated value/variety promise, but there is no heritage story, no premium pricing, and A&P is under 1% of sales — brand is a by-product of price-value delivery rather than a pricing lever.
BRAND.quote: each brand will have their own story and each brand will have their own identity... so that whatever product they're buying of that brand will be of a certain quality or a certain standard

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a real, repeatedly-delivered capability build — own-design share targeted 35–40% (FY25) → 60% by summer 2026 → 80% by 2027, analytics-driven merchandising, supply-chain and technology investment — but no disclosed R&D spend, no high gross margins funding it, and innovation is design/process refresh rather than product dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: Our own design products contributed about 35% to 40% this year and we target it to reach around 60% by the summer of 2026 and 80% by 2027

FORWARD.rationale: V2 controls the full path to the customer through 100% company-owned stores (127 → 325 in eight quarters, 3.5 mn sqft) selling 85%+ own-label merchandise, giving it complete pricing and experience control, but it moved the other way on manufacturing (three units shut, exiting in-house production) and there is no franchising, royalty or D2C e-commerce economics discussed.
FORWARD.quote: We are now focusing on retail business only and have moved away from in-house manufacturing operations.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, profitable share gain: revenue grew 62% (FY25) and 63% (FY26) with management claiming it 'significantly outpaces the broader market', store count went 127 → 325 with entry into seven new states in FY26, and productivity is claimed well ahead of peers — gains funded by internal accruals with ROE rising to 26%, not bought with margin.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we now hold a leadership position in this price segment which is an ASP of about 300 because our per square feet sales are at least 25% to 30% higher than our nearest competition

CULTURE.rationale: The 2024–2026 record shows promises kept and bad news owned: guidance of 40–50% growth was beaten twice, the 100-store FY26 plan was exceeded (136 added), old inventory came down 23% → 7% → 5% exactly as promised, the audit qualification was resolved via physical PPE verification and a Rs 5–5.8 crore write-off, pre-IndAS numbers are volunteered for transparency, and management openly cites the Vishal Mega Mart failure as its own learning. Offsets: chairman churn, a small pledge, and a visible key-man dependence on Akash Agarwal.
CULTURE.quote: one of the biggest learnings was not chasing growth blindly by compromising on profitability... we have learned from those mistakes and implemented a lot of checks and balances

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in the calls describes a barrier a well-funded copycat could not rebuild — no finite locations, no proprietary data scale, no time-based asset; management itself frames the advantage as execution and admits organised competition is already present at nearly every store, with Zudio, Vishal, V-Mart and Style Baazar named as peers.
MOATTEST.quote: The only thing that can go wrong is poor execution and we not sticking to our strengths

RECURRING.rationale: Across all calls VGL describes one-off retail transactions with repeat-purchase metrics (retention ~38-40%, 22-23 pieces/year), never licence, AMC, subscription or deferred-revenue streams; its 'Budget Pay' EMI scheme is the opposite of customer-funded working capital, and Q1 FY25 cash flow was flat on inventory build for the festive season.
RECURRING.quote: Budget Pay option allowing customers to purchase products on EMI basis, has proven valuable and contributing 38% of our B2C revenue

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: VGL sells direct to end consumers via its own TV channels, websites, apps and paid social; there is no prescriber, installer or trade professional in the chain, and acquisition spend is aimed at consumers (Meta, TikTok, Google) rather than at training a channel.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Customers are increasingly discovering, evaluating and purchasing through platforms like Meta, Apple, TikTok and Google

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is discretionary consumer jewellery and lifestyle goods, not a critical low-cost input; management repeatedly reports consumers deferring purchases when metal prices rise, the opposite of a customer who pays without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: consumer confidence, combined with steeply higher precious metal prices, consumer deferred their purchases

LOWPRICE.rationale: Deep-discount value positioning backed by Jaipur low-cost manufacturing and a 30-country sourcing network is the stated core model from Aug 2022 through May 2026, and the cost culture shows up in itemised leverage (120bps employee cost, 60bps airtime in Q3 FY26, AI-driven HR efficiency).
LOWPRICE.quote: All these years, our deep discounts and value positioning worked well in various kinds of economic cycles

PRICING.rationale: Gross margin has held 60%+ and improved (61.2%→66.1% in Q1 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26) on 'focused pricing efforts', in-house brands and higher-ASP lab-grown diamonds, but volumes fell 9-10% YoY in FY26 and customers openly defer purchases when prices rise — mix-led realisation, not price increases without volume loss.
PRICING.quote: volumes have declined across the board in both TV and digital by about 9% to 10% Y-o-Y

BRAND.rationale: In-house/proprietary brands rose to over 50% of B2C sales by FY26, a year ahead of target, and management links this to sourcing efficiency and gross margin; but these are private labels on a discount platform with no heritage narrative, no disclosed A&P-led brand premium, and no pricing premium — brand here is a margin lever, not a moat.
BRAND.quote: in-house brands have crossed 50% of our B2C sales, a year ahead of our earlier target

INNOVATION.rationale: Continuous product newness (50-100 new products daily), the lab-grown diamond ramp to ~11% of retail revenue at $250 ASP, and AI adoption across marketing/merchandising are real and margin-accretive, but no R&D spend is disclosed and none of it is proprietary technology a competitor could not source.
INNOVATION.quote: we offer every day a new product of 50 to 100 every time based on customer need or market trend

FORWARD.rationale: VGL is a Jaipur manufacturer that owns the whole route to the customer — proprietary TV channels on cable/OTA/Freeview, own website and apps, OTT and social commerce, plus acquisitions of Ideal World and digital-first Mindful Souls; it even added US in-house jewellery casting in FY26 to defend margins against tariffs.
FORWARD.quote: Shop LC GmbH expanded its presence by launching its proprietary TV channel on nation-wide OTA platform 'Freenet TV'

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Geographic expansion with local adaptation is genuine (Germany from launch to EBITDA breakeven in FY26, Ideal World growing 12-15% in the UK), but there are no market-share figures in any call and the base business is barely growing — unique customers up just 2% YoY to 706,000, US +3%, UK -1.8%, with guidance cut from mid-teens to 9-11%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our unique customer base stood at 706,000, up 2% Y-o-Y

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured founder-MD Sunil Agrawal, a net-cash balance sheet through the cycle (INR296 crore at FY26), consistent dividends, and candid disclosure of Germany's losses and the airtime cost overrun point one way; but promises have repeatedly slipped — mid-teens revenue growth guided in FY23 became 9-11% by FY27, mid-teens EBITDA 'in the medium term' is still 10.8% four years later, and Germany breakeven moved from H2 FY24 to H2 FY25 to FY26.
CULTURE.quote: we reiterate our previously provided guidance of mid-single-digit revenue growth, while maintaining mid-teens revenue growth in the long run

MOATTEST.rationale: The 30-country sourcing network, 127 million TV household reach and hard-won airtime/channel positions took years to assemble, but management itself says the manufacturing base needs almost no capital to replicate, and the company has been exiting broadcast slots over price — the advantage is operational scale rather than an un-replicable barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: Jewelry manufacturing is a low capex model, to increase the production capacity for future growth, we can do that with very little capex

RECURRING.rationale: The only annuity-like stream is the aftermarket division, described across calls as faster-growing and higher-margin at ~10% of continuing-operations revenue; there is no discussion of licences, AMCs, renewal/attach rates or customer advances funding the business — working capital is a recurring stress point, not a source of funding.
RECURRING.quote: The aftermarket business... is paying a much faster growth and the profitability margins there is also pretty good. So that has now reached almost 10% of revenue

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Varroc sells directly to OEMs who both specify and pay; there is no professional/installer channel, no trade training programme, and pricing is explicitly negotiated cost-compensation with the OEM rather than reputation-driven insensitivity (Feb 2026, Jun 2026 calls).
MIDDLEMAN.quote: there is strong commitment from OEMs and understanding with OEMs that inflation will be compensated

TOLLROAD.rationale: Content is a material, negotiated share of vehicle cost — traction motor plus controller alone is over Rs 15,000 per vehicle — and every call discusses commodity/FOREX pass-through with a quarter's lag; there is no certification, standards or 'don't switch once converted' language anywhere in 17 calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: the value of these two products put together is more than Rs. 15,000 per vehicle

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real, itemised cost programme across the years — renewable-energy projects, backward integration via SMT lines, and a FY26 VRS costing INR 799 million for ~INR 20 crore annual savings on a 4-year payback — but nothing suggests savings are passed to price to win volume, and asset turns/margins remain modest (group EBITDA 9.4% in FY26).
LOWPRICE.quote: more than 400 employees opted for the benefits of the scheme, and this resulted in a separation cost of INR 799 million

PRICING.rationale: Across all 17 calls pricing is a lagged cost-recovery mechanism from OEMs, not a lever: management repeatedly explains margin moves by RM/FOREX pass-through timing and in Feb 2026 attributes gross-margin decline to mix while confirming inflation is 'largely passed through' rather than priced above.
PRICING.quote: there could be in some of the cases, there would be probably a lag of at least a quarter, but we are expecting to be compensated in full despite this lag

BRAND.rationale: A B2B tier-1 supplier with 42–46% of revenue from a single customer (Bajaj) and zero A&P, heritage, premiumisation or consumer-brand discussion in any call; demand is won through RFQ order wins, not brand pull.
BRAND.quote: customer segmentation, if you really see Bajaj adds up to 46%

INNOVATION.rationale: Genuine and repeated engineering output — traction motors/controllers industrialised 'first time right', EFI developed in record time (Aug 2022), 130+ patents with 15 filed in 9MFY26, R&D spend now disclosed as a separate reporting box, and record EV order wins (75% of FY26 intake) — but gross margins are thin and R&D is not funding pricing dominance, it is funding qualification for OEM programmes.
INNOVATION.quote: In the 9 months, we filed close to 15 patents, taking the tally to 130 plus.

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C in any call; the business remains a component maker selling into OEM assembly lines, with the only channel-side presence being a distributor-led aftermarket arm whose store count or D2C share is never discussed.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: India operations outgrew the industry in FY24 (14.5% vs industry) and EV-model revenue rose from 5.3% (FY24) to ~13–14% (FY26) with record order intake of INR 33 billion, but management conceded India growth of 12.3% lagged a 15–20% industry in Q3FY26, and no explicit market-share percentages versus named competitors are ever given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: For the full financial year '24, our India operations continued to outperform the industry growth with a growth of over 14.5%

CULTURE.rationale: Promise-keeping is real on the balance sheet — the European four-wheeler lighting divestment closed on schedule, net debt fell from ~INR 2,700 crore (FY23) to ~INR 495 crore (FY26), ROCE reached 24.4%, dividend was raised, and bad news (EV customer receivable provision, overseas losses, VRS, net-debt increase) is disclosed promptly — but the Aug 2022 promise of 12% group EBITDA is still unmet four years later at 9.4%, and the overseas turnaround has been pushed out repeatedly ('1 to 2 years' in FY24, now H2FY27).
CULTURE.quote: We remain committed to take the EBITDA margin to 12% and ROCE above 20% over the medium term.

MOATTEST.rationale: There are genuine but limited barriers — model-life programme lock-in once an order reaches SOP, 130+ patents, e-powertrain and lighting qualification with global OEMs, and speed from win to SOP — yet the economics (46% single-customer dependence, cost pass-through pricing, sub-10% group EBITDA, Romania/Italy still loss-making) show nothing a well-funded competitor could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: our strength really is the ability to ramp from business win to SOP very quickly

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 18 calls the revenue model is one-off case sales of beverages/snacks; there is no license, AMC, subscription or renewal stream, and deferred revenue/customer advances are never cited as a funding source — working capital is discussed only as inventory/receivable days (~17 days in Aug 2022).
RECURRING.quote: working capital days reduced to ~17 days as on June 30, 2022

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through distributors and retail outlets, but the end consumer chooses the brand off the shelf; the only channel-loyalty language is defensive discounting/price points to retain distributors, not professional prescribers or trade training creating switching costs.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We are using it only to make sure our distributors remain with us

TOLLROAD.rationale: Carbonated drinks and water are discretionary consumer purchases, not a sub-1% critical input into a business customer's cost base; management itself calls water 'like a commodity' where volume can be bought with discounts, the opposite of toll-road economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: Water is like a commodity, you can increase your sales as much as you want by offering discounts

LOWPRICE.rationale: Repeated, itemised cost engineering across the years — lightweighting, removal of corrugated pads, sugar reduction (46% low/no-sugar in 2024 rising to ~63% by Q1 2026), 13+ backward-integrated plants, larger low-cost greenfield plants — with savings passed to consumers via pack upsizing and Rs.10/Rs.20 price points while EBITDA margins were held (23.3% CY2025, India ~26%).
LOWPRICE.quote: our focus on reducing sugar content and the lightweighting packaging material... contributed to this improvement

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory runs the wrong way: after price hikes in 2022, India realization per case fell ~4% in Q4 CY2025 and 1.5% in Q1 CY2026 as management upsized the Rs.20 pack from 250ml to 400ml and launched Rs.10 packs, with FY2025 consolidated realization up just 0.5% — volume bought with effective price cuts, plus admitted industry discounting.
PRICING.quote: In India, realization per case declined by a marginal 1.5%, primarily due to volume growth initiatives such as upsizing of packs

BRAND.rationale: VBL sells powerful brands (Pepsi, Sting, Tropicana, Gatorade, Rockstar) and cites 'strong brand portfolio' behind its 2025 recovery, but it is the licensed bottler — the heritage, A&P and brand equity belong to PepsiCo, and the brand has not translated into premium pricing (realization is falling).
BRAND.quote: reflecting the strength of our wide distribution network and strong brand portfolio

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year with real revenue impact (Sting scaling from 7.2% of volume in 2022, then Sting Classic, Adrenaline Rush at Rs.60, Nimbooz, Tropicana PET +100%, dairy +60-70% in Q1 CY2026), but VBL discloses no R&D spend and the product innovation originates with PepsiCo, so this is execution of a licensor's pipeline rather than R&D-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: 'Ad-Rush' has done phenomenally well... The demand for both these products is much higher than what we anticipated

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing income or D2C build-out in any call; e-commerce is explicitly described as too small to track, and integration investment runs backward (preform/PET, 13 integrated plants) rather than toward the end customer.
FORWARD.quote: the e-commerce contribution in our category is very small. Consequently, we do not track it extensively

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share and reach gains over the whole period: outlets from ~2mn to 3mn in 2022 and adding 300,000-500,000 outlets a year by 2026; internationally PepsiCo share taken from near-zero to 71% in Zimbabwe, replicated in Zambia/Morocco, and South Africa entered at 1.8% share via BevCo, then Twizza and Crickley Dairy — expansion funded from cash with the India business net-debt-free.
SHAREGAIN.quote: PepsiCo had no share in the past in Zimbabwe, but as we've mentioned in past calls, we achieved 71% market share

CULTURE.rationale: Family-led with stable leadership across all 18 calls, promises repeatedly delivered — capacity commissioned on time, BevCo/CAPEX debt repaid as guided, India net debt-free with Rs.12,250mn cash and a CRISIL AAA upgrade by CY2025 — plus prompt bad news (RGB asset write-offs taken immediately, calling 2025 'the worst year we have ever seen'); the one blemish is withdrawing distribution/visi-cooler disclosure in Feb 2026 on competitive grounds.
CULTURE.quote: If there would have been any further write-offs, we would have done right away

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuine barriers exist — exclusive PepsiCo franchise territories, ~1mn+ visi-coolers, millions of outlets, backward-integrated plants and 6-month international raw-material cover — but the calls themselves show a well-funded copycat closing in: Reliance's Campa is adding capacity, discounting and chilling equipment, and management concedes it cannot say whether it is growing faster.
MOATTEST.quote: there is Campa in the market, they are growing the volumes in the market, and even Coke is growing. We do not know if we are growing faster

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 15 calls the discussion is entirely about commodity volumes, cost per tonne, LME prices and capex; there is no mention of attach rates, AMC/service revenue, renewals, installed base or customer advances funding the business.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No evidence either way — sales are of bulk commodities (alumina, aluminium ingots/billets, zinc, silver, crude, power) with no professional/installer channel, training programmes or prescriber dynamics discussed on any call.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Vedanta's products are large, negotiable inputs priced off exchange benchmarks, not tiny-but-critical spend; management explicitly runs 'dynamic commodity hedging' and locks in LME on alumina purchases because it cannot set price, the opposite of toll-road economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: We have started dynamic commodity hedging for proactive risk management amidst unprecedented price volatility

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, sustained and itemised cost obsession — aluminium hot metal cost falling to a five-year low of $1,752/t (Q3FY26 $1,674/t) and Zinc India to $959/t, with management claiming top-quartile/top-decile positions on the global cost curve — but this is low-cost commodity production, not low price plus differentiation, and returns still swing with LME.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our aluminium and zinc operations consistently outperformed industry benchmarks, ranking in the top quartile and top decile respectively of the global cost curve

PRICING.rationale: Every call attributes revenue swings to exchange prices and currency rather than to price increases Vedanta initiates; FY26's record EBITDA is explicitly credited to 'positive prices, record production, and lower COP', and Q1FY23 profitability was hostage to LME at ~$2,400 vs $2,653/t cost — a pure price-taker.
PRICING.quote: driven again by positive prices, record production, and lower COP

BRAND.rationale: The only 'brand' economics discussed is the ~$400m brand fee Vedanta India pays up to parent VRL to service holdco debt — a cash drain, not consumer brand power; there is no A&P spend, heritage/premium-pricing story or distributor leverage anywhere in the 15 calls.
BRAND.quote: the brand fee is more or less same, so it is 400 and the balance 600 receipt

INNOVATION.rationale: There are named product launches with a differentiation angle — Restora and Restora Ultra low-carbon aluminium and EcoZen, 'Asia's first low-carbon zinc product' — plus a 90% value-added product target, but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and no revenue impact from innovation is given across any call.
INNOVATION.quote: Vedanta proudly has a portfolio of three low-carbon products, two in aluminium named Restora and Restora Ultra, and now one in zinc named EcoZen

FORWARD.rationale: The direction of travel is downstream — 90% value-added products and alloys, new billet lines at Jharsuguda/BALCO, a 420 KTPA DI pipe plant in Goa, copper rod at Silvassa/Fujairah, and the Jan-2026 Incab Industries acquisition 'aligned with our vision of unlocking downstream synergies' — but this is product-mix integration, not own stores, franchising or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: approval to acquire Incab Industries, another strategic move aligned with our vision of unlocking downstream synergies

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume and position claims recur — global leader in aluminium wire rod, target of second-largest billet producer, India's largest private oil producer, India's largest ferro alloys producer, aluminium output up to 2.46 Mt in FY26 — but explicit market-share percentages rising over time versus named competitors are never given, and oil & gas volumes fell for years (85 kboepd in Q3FY26 against a 150 kboepd 'near-term target').
SHAREGAIN.quote: We are already the global leader in wire rod production

CULTURE.rationale: Genuinely mixed: management discloses fatalities and safety failures candidly (three deaths to Q3FY26, the April 2026 Athena boiler incident) and did deliver the multi-year deleveraging, demerger and FY26 record ($6bn+ EBITDA, 0.95x leverage) it promised, but the record also shows repeatedly missed long-dated targets (the FY25 '$10 billion EBITDA' and 300 kboepd oil vision), constant leadership churn (Duggal → Navin Agarwal → Naidoo), and capital allocation bent toward upstreaming dividends and brand fees to service parent VRL debt.
CULTURE.quote: Sadly, we lost three of our colleagues in this year, ending Quarter 3. This is incredibly painful for the team and I

MOATTEST.rationale: The one pattern with a concrete, articulable barrier: finite, permitted, world-scale orebodies and fully backward-integrated infrastructure that a funded newcomer cannot rebuild — 662 Mt zinc R&R at Zinc International, 3,000 Mt at Liberia, 1.4 bn barrels R&R, a 5 Mtpa single-location alumina refinery, captive bauxite and coal — which management frames as a >$50bn replacement cost.
MOATTEST.quote: most of our assets now cannot be replicated... the replacement cost is in excess of $50 billion

TOLLROAD.rationale: Across all 17 calls the products are discretionary retail consumer goods sold in competitive categories where price transmission depends on what rivals and retailers accept, the opposite of a small-share-of-cost critical input paid without negotiation; management repeatedly waits for industry-wide action before landing hikes.
TOLLROAD.quote: our ability to pass on pricing can only be there after the leaders in the segment pass on pricing

PRICING.rationale: Pricing actions are frequent (Aug 2022, May 2024, Feb 2026, May 2026) and gross margin was rebuilt from 29.8% in Q1FY23 to ~35.3-35.7% by FY26, but every increase is cost-recovery driven by copper/aluminium inflation, is dependent on industry cohesion, and in FY26 fans/coolers still degrew — this is pass-through, not pricing above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: We have probably landed about 75% of what price increases are required so far

BRAND.rationale: V-Guard has genuine South-India heritage stretched into many adjacent categories under one name (wires, pumps, switchgear, fans, water heaters, kitchen, inverters) with non-South rising from 43% of revenue in FY23 to 48% in FY26 and A&P spend called out; but management itself concedes low share and weak pricing leadership in newer durables categories, so brand does not yet deliver premium pricing.
BRAND.quote: we are a relatively newer brand if you look at Fans, Kitchen Appliances. Apart from Water Heaters, our market share in Consumer Durables is quite low

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent incremental product-led moves are visible across the years — premium BLDC fan launch in Q3FY24, BLDC reaching ~40% of ceiling-fan sales by FY26 after catching the trend '3-4 years back', BLDC chimneys and a Sunflame portfolio refresh — but no R&D spend, pipeline economics or share-of-industry-R&D is ever disclosed, and the Gegadyne battery bet is still pre-commercial after years.
INNOVATION.quote: V-Guard is well equipped. We caught this trend at least 3 - 4 years back, and we have very good offerings in the BLDC segment

FORWARD.rationale: The integration story runs the other way — backward into manufacturing (own share ~45% in FY19 to 60% in FY23 to 65% in FY24, with battery, kitchen, fan and TPW factories added); there is no own-store count, franchise royalty or D2C build discussed in any call, with e-commerce run through third-party platforms.
FORWARD.quote: own manufacturing was your question, we are at about 65% now

SHAREGAIN.rationale: There is repeated directional share gain — non-South rising to 48% of revenue, water-heater share regained after FY21 losses, switches/switchgear guided to 25-30% growth, inverters from a 3% base — but management explicitly refuses to give share numbers, and FY26 full-year growth was only 7% with fans and Sunflame degrowing, so persistence is not demonstrated.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we do not want to give out any market share numbers

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is exceptionally stable (Mithun MD, Ramachandran COO, Sudarshan Kasturi CFO across all 17 calls, promoter family ownership), the balance sheet moved to net cash of INR231 crore by FY26 with debt repaid, and bad news (copper write-off, Sunflame CSD weakness, labour-code charge, fan degrowth) is disclosed promptly — but the 10-10.5% EBITDA margin promise made in FY24 was still unmet at 8.8% in FY26 and keeps being pushed out.
CULTURE.quote: bringing EBITDA margins back to the range of 10% to 10.5% that we have indicated earlier

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barrier is the multi-decade South-India distribution and service network plus discerning-consumer trust that Sunflame is now being plugged into, but the COO concedes organized retail and e-commerce have made category entry relatively easy and competitive intensity has been rising since 2016-17 — nothing here a well-funded copycat could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: market entry is easy, relatively... It's not that easy to build a healthy franchise

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all calls the model is explicitly direct-to-consumer (B2C 92-95% of revenue), and management stated it deliberately avoids doctor-referral arrangements; no trade training or prescriber-channel investment is ever discussed.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: there is no arrangement where we send these patients to any doctors

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly positions Vijaya as offering high-end technology and quality at market-level prices (Q4 FY26), and defends against deep-discounting aggregators without cutting its own package prices (Q1 FY23) — but there is no cost-obsession culture or itemised savings narrative, and margins are high (41-43%) rather than thin-margin/high-turn.
LOWPRICE.quote: While maintaining all this, we are not charging anything extra. So more or less, we match the market rates, maybe 2%, 3% here and there.

PRICING.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume- and mix-led, not price-led: PH revenue was flat because 'we did not do any price increase', wellness package prices were held unchanged through competitive intensity, and in May 2026 management guided to only 1-1.5% realisation growth with volume the focus for 2-3 years.
PRICING.quote: the major focus for the next 2 to 3 years is capacity addition and volume-driven revenue growth

BRAND.rationale: A 40-year Hyderabad heritage and trust story recurs from Aug 2022 to May 2026, with brand recall cited as the defence against discounting entrants, the acquired PH assets rebranded to Vijaya, and the brand successfully stretched into Kolkata, Pune and Bangalore where new hubs broke even ahead of guidance.
BRAND.quote: accelerating traction of the Vijaya brand in new markets supported by our differentiated service proposition

INNOVATION.rationale: Continuous investment in advanced modalities (3.0 Tesla MRI, 160-slice cardiac CT, PET-CT), an automated-track lab at Panjagutta and a new Genomics offering (Q4 FY26) drive mix/realisation, but there is no disclosed R&D spend, no share-of-industry-R&D framing, and management concedes Genomics is a long-term play with no near-term revenue.
INNOVATION.quote: Genomics is a long-term play. I don't think we'll see any significant revenue coming in the next years.

FORWARD.rationale: Vijaya owns and operates its entire network (81 to 162 centres over five years) and sells direct to the end consumer at 92% B2C, giving it full control of experience and pricing — but it is a service operator rather than a manufacturer integrating forward, with no franchising, royalty or licensing model.
FORWARD.quote: we have doubled our centers from 81 to 162, expanded our footprint from 2 states to 6 states

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent above-industry growth across the record — 17% revenue CAGR since listing versus 15% guidance, Hyderabad's mature core still compounding 15-20% off existing capacity, and repeated claims of taking share from peers — plus geographic expansion into Kolkata, Pune and Bangalore with locally adapted hubs; explicit share percentages are never quantified.
SHAREGAIN.quote: whenever the season is favorable, Vijaya not only outpaces the industry growth, but also incrementally gains market share from the competitors

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on early calls were delivered later: the FY23 hub pipeline, the guided 39-40% margins, and breakeven timelines that were consistently beaten (Kolkata in 3 quarters, Khammam/Nandyal in 2), all funded from internal accruals with ~INR260-305 crore net cash and disciplined M&A screening; management is candid about setbacks (April dip on PH system migration, no GLP-1 demand yet) though CFO and board seats did turn over in FY23-FY26.
CULTURE.quote: we have delivered a revenue CAGR of 17%, exceeding our guidance of 15%... without any dilution in the EBITDA margin

MOATTEST.rationale: Real time-and-capital barriers exist — a 40-year reputation, a dense integrated radiology-plus-pathology network and INR12-19 crore per hub of advanced imaging that pathology-only chains lack — but management's own answer to new entrants is confidence rather than a structural impossibility, and well-funded chains are already piloting radiology.
MOATTEST.quote: these are like the objects that we see in the side mirror... They appear to be closer, but they're very far away

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is one-time capital-goods module sales — LC-backed shipments against an order book — with no licence fees, AMC, subscription or service attach discussed across any of the four calls; the only 'recurring' element cited is repeat ordering by customers, not a recurring revenue stream, and working capital is funded by payables/credit rather than customer advances.
RECURRING.quote: We operate in capital goods segment. Our customers, while undertaking large capital expenditure, value long-term performance and bankability over upfront cost.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: There is a real professional channel — 98 authorised distributors, 375+ dealers and 76 system integrators feeding a distribution segment that was ~13% of the 9M FY26 order book — but the dominant buyers are IPPs (55–69%) and EPCs who negotiate hard on price, and no trade-training or channel-loyalty programme is described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: 98 authorised distributors, over 375 dealers, and more than 76 system integrators

TOLLROAD.rationale: The module is the single largest cost line of a solar project, not a sub-1% critical ingredient, and pricing is openly negotiated and volatile — non-DCR realisation fell 30–40% in Q3 FY26 and cell-cost changes are contractually passed to developers, hitting their IRRs; certification (BNEF Tier 1, PVEL) is a bankability badge, not a standards toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: So, if the change in cell cost is a pass-through, then the developers will be impacted... their IRRs for the project will get impacted

LOWPRICE.rationale: Genuine, itemised cost obsession runs through all four calls — cost of poor quality down 53.33%, only 800 extra staff for a 5GW line, per-watt overhead down 16% in FY26, finance cost down to 6.5% — but this is a highly capital-intensive business (INR600 crore/GW cell capex) with low asset turns, and the savings are automation-and-scale driven rather than an unreplicable cost culture.
LOWPRICE.quote: as volumes scaled, per-watt overhead came down 16% on a full-year basis

PRICING.rationale: The evidence is of price deflation and a declared cost-plus model, not pricing power: non-DCR realisation dropped from ~INR18/Wp to INR14–14.5/Wp, Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 18.5% and Q4 to 16%, and ~80–88% of the order book merely passes through cell cost rather than raising price for value.
PRICING.quote: we operate in a cost-plus business model

BRAND.rationale: There is durable third-party validation — India's first company in the PVEL top-performer list, featured 8 times, BNEF Tier 1 bankability for 8 consecutive quarters, 20-year provenance and 70%+ repeat business from top-10 customers — but no premium pricing results from it (realisations track cell prices) and there is no A&P spend or consumer-brand economics.
BRAND.quote: India's first solar company to feature in the reliability test gold standards, Kiwa PVEL, top performer list in 2017, and have consistently featured 8 times since then

INNOVATION.rationale: A 200-member NABL/ILAC-accredited R&D team, a named annual launch (Hypersol Pro, 23.7% efficiency, 640Wp), a full transition to N-type TOPCon and a 'technology-first' capex philosophy show incremental innovation culture; but R&D spend is never disclosed, the core cell technology and equipment are bought from Chinese suppliers, and silver-reduction advances are credited to peers like Jinko and AIKO rather than in-house work.
INNOVATION.quote: global peers like that have successfully run commercial tests as well

FORWARD.rationale: The entire strategic direction is backward, not forward — modules, then cells, then wafer/ingot, plus BESS cells — and management explicitly ruled out forward integration when asked directly; there are no owned stores, franchises or D2C channel.
FORWARD.quote: At this point of time, we are completely focused on backward integration on the module and expanding into BESS. At this point of time, we are not thinking anything beyond.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volumes grew 76% to 3.3GW in FY26 with capacity going 4.5GW→9.5GW→15.5GW and cumulative deployment crossing 10GW, but no explicit market-share percentage or comparison versus named domestic competitors is ever given, and India's own market roughly doubled (45GW added in FY26), so absolute growth does not demonstrate persistent share gain.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We have scaled from 5 gigawatt to 10 gigawatts in just two years

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on the Sep 2025 call were largely delivered — Vallam 5GW commissioned in Q3 as guided, ratings upgraded to Ind A+/A1+, working capital cut 82→44 days, zero long-term debt with stated guardrails — and the 17.5GW→15.5GW module cut and the cell-plant rephasing (12GW by FY27 → 9GW by Q4 FY27 plus 3GW in FY28) were disclosed rather than buried; against that, the leadership record is unstable (an interim CEO in Q1 FY26, a new external CEO by Q4, heavy board churn) and the company is simultaneously entering an unrelated 15GWh BESS build while its solar capex is still unfunded.
CULTURE.quote: we have retained it at 15.5 for the time being to ensure 75% backward integration

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing described would stop a well-funded newcomer: the company itself built a 5GW greenfield plant from ideation to commissioning in under nine months with off-the-shelf Chinese equipment, and its own thesis admits capacity is being replicated industry-wide toward an 80–100GW shake-out — the barrier is access to capital and ALMM policy, both of which peers already have.
MOATTEST.quote: We took the 5-gigawatt facility from ideation to commissioning in under nine months.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 13 calls the discussion is one-time luggage sales through trade, EBO and e-commerce channels; there is no mention of attach rates, service/AMC revenue, renewals, installed base or deferred revenue as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Channel discussion is about dealers, modern-trade doors, e-commerce portals and franchisees who resell, not professionals who prescribe or specify the product to an end payer; dealer conferences are trade promotion, not expert lock-in.

TOLLROAD.rationale: This is a discretionary consumer product where the buyer is acutely price-sensitive — management repeatedly attributes de-growth to price wars and Rs.1,100 cabin bags — the opposite of a critical, un-negotiated, tiny-share-of-cost input.
TOLLROAD.quote: High heat competition has fueled price war in our segment, especially in the mid-price segment.

LOWPRICE.rationale: VIP did backward-integrate (79% own/controlled manufacturing in FY23, Bangladesh capacity, manpower cost down 16% and 7 lakh sq ft of warehousing surrendered in FY25), but the cost actions are remedial repair, not a copy-proof cost culture — by FY26 it is being undercut at the low end and admits it 'did not exist' at the absolute bottom where 80% of the market sits.
LOWPRICE.quote: Like cabin luggage are getting sold at less than Rs. 1,100.

PRICING.rationale: The record is one of price deflation, not pricing power: no price increases taken in FY24, ASP dragged down by inventory liquidation, and FY25 value growth flat versus 11% volume growth after netting off e-commerce price support.
PRICING.quote: Heavy discounting initiated by online brands and e-commerce platform has also put some pressure on realization, not only for us, but across the industry.

BRAND.rationale: Genuine heritage and recall exist (VIP since 1968, 'even small kids know VIP', high-decibel TV campaigns, Carlton premium adjacency), but the brand delivers neither premium pricing nor share gain — management itself concedes people know VIP 'but they are not buying it', and A&P spend has been sporadic ('for last few years we have not spent').
BRAND.quote: VIP is still a household name and the most reliable brand in the category due to its quality

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady cadence of named launches with revenue impact (37 new ranges Dec–Mar FY24, Lexus/Paradise/Gemma with stock-outs and 22,000 pieces in 30 days, the Smart Bag Tag), but no R&D disclosure or industry-R&D share, and gross margins fell from 55-56% to 48% rather than being funded by innovation.
INNOVATION.quote: we are about to launch a first-time in industry Smart Bag Tag

FORWARD.rationale: Real forward integration is visible — franchise-route EBOs, airport stores, Carlton exclusive stores with 80% of Carlton billed direct to consumer, and e-commerce at ~31% of revenue — but the economics failed the test, with 133 stores closed against 32 opened in FY25 and e-commerce de-growing 17% in Q1FY26.
FORWARD.quote: 80% of the Carlton revenue comes from our stores, which is direct billing to consumer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share moves the wrong way across the trajectory: general-trade share down from 21% to 17%, modern-trade salience from 26% to 23%, and the e-commerce channel de-growing after eight or nine quarters of growth, with new online entrants taking the volume.
SHAREGAIN.quote: get back our GT market share which has reduced from 21 % to 17 %

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on calls were not delivered — the 18-20% EBITDA guidance reaffirmed in Jan 2024 gave way to 4% reported (10% adjusted) by Q1FY26 — alongside four MDs and multiple chairmen/CFOs in five years, repeated refusals to quantify costs on calls, and a promoter exit; credit is due for candidly owning the poor quarter in Jan 2024, but delivery-versus-promise fails.
CULTURE.quote: We still maintain our guidance of 18%-20% over next 12 to 18 months.

MOATTEST.rationale: Management explicitly describes the category as having low entry barriers, and the calls show funded newcomers rebuilding the position within a couple of years via exclusive e-commerce tie-ups — there is no articulable reason a well-capitalised copycat could not catch up.
MOATTEST.quote: High growth rates, positive travel macros, low entry barriers have attracted multiple new entrants.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Animal health formulations are sold through vets/distributors and pushed by own field forces (India field force scaled to ~200; direct field force added in Spain/Benelux/Sweden), and the company now distributes Boehringer Ingelheim's companion-animal products in India — but no calls describe trade training programmes or prescriber loyalty economics.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: expansion of markets with direct field force in Spain and few countries like Benelux, Sweden

LOWPRICE.rationale: A consistent cost culture runs through the Viyash-era calls — India low-cost manufacturing for mature products, backward integration into intermediates, network optimisation, plant shutdowns and a Mangalore site divestment saving ~$1mn/year — but this is margin repair in a leveraged, mid-turns pharma asset, not low-price-plus-scale as a customer proposition.
LOWPRICE.quote: with the small markets, $100 markets, we are able to compete with our cost efficiencies

PRICING.rationale: The Aug-2022 call shows the opposite: management could only pass on cost inflation slowly and contractually, and the FY26 calls describe US price competition from Indian entrants forcing a strategy change; gross margin expansion (51%→54%) came from mix and backward integration, not price increases.
PRICING.quote: in many of these markets, distributors tend to hold significantly higher amount of inventory and over there it takes more time to pass on some of the prices

BRAND.rationale: Management claims branded-generic positions in Turkey, Brazil and India animal health that allow some price pass-through, but across 17 calls there is no heritage story, no A&P disclosure and no brand-led adjacency — the merged entity is positioned on R&D/manufacturing, not brand.
BRAND.quote: We have in most of our markets now substantially strong branded product business.

INNOVATION.rationale: Repeatedly positions itself as "an R&D first organization" — 200+ scientists incl. 20+ doctorates, 10-12 products developed a year, ~60 commercial products plus 30 NDAs, a new oncology potent lab, and a move up the curve into complex/high-potent APIs — but R&D spend is never quantified and this is generic/CDMO development capability rather than proprietary innovation driving pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Roughly we have 200 plus scientists including 20 plus doctorates

FORWARD.rationale: Integration is mostly backward (intermediates, in-housing APIs), but there is genuine forward movement: intermediates→API→finished dosage, own front-end field forces in Spain/Turkey/India, and in-licensed distribution (Boehringer Ingelheim in India). No own-store, franchise or D2C economics are discussed.
FORWARD.quote: wherever we are strong on the Internet, we are able to do forward integration

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Claims of leadership in 5-10 API products "sustainable... not a one-year market leader", strengthening in-market share in Turkey/Brazil (Call 1) and a Turkey turnaround with large volume growth by FY26 — but share is asserted qualitatively, never quantified or tracked against named competitors over time.
SHAREGAIN.quote: at least I can say 5 to 10 products we are the market leader

CULTURE.rationale: Under Hari Babu the calls show candour (admitting animal health was flat at ~INR350cr for five years, that they were "struggling" on innovator delivery and in the US, and disclosing merger one-offs of INR41cr and the MAT reversal) and promises delivered — margins up 8-9 straight quarters, net debt/EBITDA <4x, rating upgrade to AA-, synergies "tracking better than what we anticipated"; against that sits extraordinary churn (six chairmen, three MDs and a CFO exiting FY2022-24) and PE rather than family ownership.
CULTURE.quote: It's easy to say CDMO can work with innovators but I don't want to go into that. Whatever we say we follow.

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but rebuildable barriers: nine USFDA-approved sites, EU/CEP approvals, 25 US VMFs, decade-old innovator relationships and 18-24 month regulatory requalification cycles that deter customer switching — yet Hari Babu himself calls the market "so crowded", and a well-funded copycat (as Viyash itself did via acquisitions and Carlyle capital in 2019-21) can assemble the same platform in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: we ended up having nine high quality USFDA approved facilities

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 17 calls there is no discussion of licence fees, AMC/service contracts, subscriptions, attach rates, renewals or deferred revenue as a funding source; the only recurring-ish line is LimeRoad marketplace commission income, which is transaction-based, not a contracted stream.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: V-Mart sells value fashion directly to end consumers in its own 591 stores and on limeroad.com — no prescriber, installer or trade professional stands between product and payer, and management explicitly frames the customer as the household earning INR 20,000–35,000 who judges price and quality herself.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Affordability is still very important. The value has to be visible and convincing.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Apparel is a discretionary consumer purchase, not a small-but-critical input to a business customer; management repeatedly describes consumers comparing prices and holding back spend, the opposite of pay-without-negotiating toll economics.
TOLLROAD.quote: There is sensitivity on the household budget, no doubt about it. There are definitely comparisons that people are doing in both prices as well as the quality.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The whole model is low price plus acceptable quality at scale: the FY24-25 calls describe a deliberate downward price correction in the South, sustained cost obsession (marketing spend cut 44-59%, expenses +8% vs sales +24% in Q4FY26, +15% vs +23% in Q1FY27), asset-light debt-free balance sheet, and growth driven by volume/throughput rather than unit margin — culminating in PAT up 6x to INR124 crore in FY26.
LOWPRICE.quote: the ASP degrowth was a fallout of the strategic shift towards sharper and more value-driven product pricing that we have been trying to incorporate in the last two years

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory shows the opposite of pricing power — a multi-year deliberate price correction downward (ASP -3% in Q1FY25), and when yarn/crude inflation hit in FY26 management absorbed 1-2% of cost itself and passed on only a sliver; later ASP gains are explicitly attributed to mix and lower discounting, not price increases.
PRICING.quote: in certain cases, we have also passed it on to the consumers, but very, very controlled way

BRAND.rationale: There is real trust equity — NPS consistently above 60, 5 lakh Google reviews at 4.4+, and marketing spend cut ~44% offline without losing growth — but management itself admits brand 'baggage' on V-Mart/Unlimited (piloting LimeRoad-branded stores to escape it), and there is no heritage premium or sustained A&P story.
BRAND.quote: more than five lakh Google reviews averaging 4.4 plus, and that is a strong testimony to the value proposition and the brand trust

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend is ever disclosed, there is no named-product pipeline with revenue impact, and gross margins are drifting down (34.5%, -80bps in Q1FY27; -100bps in Q4FY26) rather than funding outsized innovation — the tech work described is AI-for-operations (forecasting, replenishment, assortment), i.e. efficiency, not innovation-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: we are applying data and technology across a lot of areas, demand forecasting, design, trend identification, or even assortment planning or replenishment

FORWARD.rationale: V-Mart designs/sources its own private label and controls the whole path to the customer — 591 own stores across 335 cities plus the LimeRoad acquisition to own the digital arm and build genuine omni (online-to-offline discovery, One Click) — but it is a retailer by origin rather than a manufacturer integrating forward, and there is no franchising or royalty economics funding growth.
FORWARD.quote: our vmartretail.com will get merged into the limeroad.com and limeroad.com becomes our digital arm for both the brands

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is the explicit strategy and the delivery is visible across the record: 11 consecutive quarters of positive LTL, 92 stores opened in FY26 and 23-24% revenue growth with footfalls +39%, Unlimited South at 33% revenue growth, all while management notes premium and rival value retailers are struggling — and it is profitable share, with PAT at a record and no long-term debt.
SHAREGAIN.quote: What our strategy will be largely to increase our own market share from the earlier times.

CULTURE.rationale: Stable family leadership (Lalit Agarwal MD throughout, Anand Agarwal CFO since FY22, orderly COO transition in Jul 2026), candid admission of failure on the earlier in-house online attempt, and promises delivered years later — the 2022 pledge to make LimeRoad sustainable within 2-3 years within a capped 15-20% of EBITDA produced CM3-positive economics and losses down ~39-70%, alongside a consistently conservative debt-free balance sheet and consistent inventory provisioning policy.
CULTURE.quote: We also launched 3 years back, we made teams and stuff. I would not call myself too successful on that front. We also failed there.

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barriers — early store density in underserved Tier 2-4 catchments, site-selection discipline, a low-cost supply chain and the omni customer base — are real but replicable: management concedes competitors and 'rational regional players' are opening stores in the same towns, and the defence offered is market saturation rather than something a funded newcomer could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: One additional store or 2 additional stores now opening up doesn't give any more big impact on our existing store sales.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Across all four calls management describes low price plus own-brand quality at ~40% discount to leader brands, funded by itemised cost engineering (polybags removed, gunny bags instead of cartons, shoes shipped tied by laces, CAD fabric cutting, RFID for shrink) and by passing 100% of GST cuts on; scale-driven buying efficiency is explicitly reinvested into price rather than margin, with 20%+ revenue growth and rising PAT margin (5.9%→6.5%).
LOWPRICE.quote: we get better and better buying efficiencies. And the margins, which may come because of better buying efficiencies, we have a plan to reinvest that either in product quality or in better pricing.

PRICING.rationale: The trajectory is the opposite of pricing power: in FY26–FY27 inflation they absorbed input costs, refused hikes on opening and mid price points, passed all GST rationalisation to customers, and committed to widening rather than narrowing the discount to leader brands; only high-fashion price points show low elasticity.
PRICING.quote: Under no circumstances, would we allow a price discount to the market leader become lesser than before.

BRAND.rationale: Own brands have scaled steadily (73.1% of revenue FY25 → 74.1% FY26 → 75.2% Q1FY27, two brands above INR 1,000 crores and six above INR 500 crores) and are described as the key differentiator, but the positioning is value/discount rather than heritage or premium pricing, and no A&P or brand-stretch programme is discussed.
BRAND.quote: Two of our private brands are now INR 1,000 crores plus in revenue, and another 6 private brands are INR 500 crores plus in revenue.

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is operational rather than R&D-led: quick commerce scaled from 656 to 767 stores and 8.7m to 1.4 crore registered users, a small-format store was piloted then validated on revenue/sq ft and ROCE, and RFID moved from a two-store pilot to a state-by-state rollout — but no R&D spend, pipeline or share-of-industry-R&D is ever disclosed.
INNOVATION.quote: we have quite clearly established all these benefits in our pilot and experimentation. And we are progressing with RFID maximum possible speed.

FORWARD.rationale: VMM is a retailer that has integrated backwards into own brands rather than a manufacturer moving forward, but it does own its entire 819-store network, controls shelf space and pricing, and has built its own D2C quick-commerce channel plus a 600,000 sq ft automated warehouse; there is no franchising or royalty model.
FORWARD.quote: Our quick commerce expanded to 767 stores across 520 cities in the country.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent double-digit SSSG (12.3% FY25, 11% FY26, 10% in a weak Q1FY27) alongside 90→105 store additions a year and city count rising 458→535→559, with new-state entries (Kerala, Gujarat, Maharashtra) delivering the same store EBITDA and ROCE — share gain is implied and profitable, but management never cites explicit market-share numbers versus named competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our outcomes in Kerala and in Gujarat and Maharashtra have been similar to the rest of the network

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in the May 2025 call were delivered in later ones — Kerala 'full speed', Maharashtra/Gujarat pilots (6 stores each by May 2026), the Haryana automated warehouse, the small-format and RFID pilots — while management refuses forward guidance, discloses bad news promptly (Assam mourning shutdown, extended monsoon, Q1FY27 inflation drag), publicly re-issued a corrected transcript, caps its own margin expectations, and measures the new format on return on capital with a debt-light, cash-rich balance sheet.
CULTURE.quote: I do not either commit to or in any which way forecast that the margin improvements that we've seen thus far will necessarily continue in the future.

MOATTEST.rationale: The replication barrier is real but not un-buildable: 819 stores across 559 mostly Tier-2/3 cities, a 75% own-brand supply chain with multiple INR 500–1,000 crore brands, and dedicated automated warehousing would take a well-funded entrant many years — yet management articulates no finite-resource, data-scale or time-based lock, and the advantage rests on cost culture and property access that capital can eventually assemble.
MOATTEST.quote: 75%... of our revenue is now from private brands. And that gives us an ability to cushion our customers and consumers from the impact of very serious inflation.

RECURRING.rationale: AMC/after-sales streams recur across calls — CAC growth is repeatedly attributed partly to AMC, mining equipment to O&M 'service annuities', and textile machinery to after-sales — but management never quantifies attach rates, renewal rates, deferred revenue or customer advances as a funding source, and the bulk of revenue remains one-time product sales.
RECURRING.quote: supported by corporate, commercial and industrial demand with healthy traction across product categories and AMC business

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is created by mass end-consumer marketing (IPL/TV spends of ~3% of revenue, celebrity ambassadors, 'Har Ghar Voltas'), not by an expert who prescribes while someone else pays; dealers are volume distributors bought with schemes and discounts, and end-customer price sensitivity is explicitly high.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: IPL and a move towards TV advertisements and higher sales and promotion expenses kept our margins in line

TOLLROAD.rationale: An air conditioner is a large, discretionary purchase for the buyer, not a sub-1% critical input; the calls repeatedly describe demand collapsing with inflation and discretionary spending cuts, the opposite of toll-road inelasticity.
TOLLROAD.quote: the fear of rising inflation brought about a cut in the discretionary spend by the consumers

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a consistent cost narrative across all 16 calls — value engineering, cost austerity, localisation at Chennai/Pantnagar/Sanand, sourcing efficiencies — and competitive pricing with a large SKU range, but savings are never itemised, and margins fell (FY26 PBT Rs 557cr vs Rs 1,191cr) rather than being defended by volume and asset turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: various value engineering initiatives and cost austerity drives have kept the margins stable

PRICING.rationale: The record across the period is the opposite of pricing power: in Aug 2022 no hike could be taken despite a heatwave because competitors withheld, and by Jan 2026 management still cannot say whether copper/currency/BEE-table costs can be passed on, while giving trade discounts to clear channel inventory.
PRICING.quote: all competitors have withheld increase in the prices and nobody has thought to pass on this increase input cost to the consumers

BRAND.rationale: Genuine Tata heritage and consumer trust, sustained A&P, and successful stretch into adjacencies (Voltbek washing machines/refrigerators reaching 8.2%/6.2% share), but the brand has not delivered the pattern's other half — share eroded from 24.1% (Jun 2022) to 17.9% (Dec 2025) and no premium pricing was sustainable.
BRAND.quote: the faith, love, affection and trust which we got from our consumers was enormous

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches do appear each year (inverter SKUs, coolers, cold room/medical refrigeration, the AI-powered Vertis series in FY26), but R&D spend is never disclosed or discussed, gross margins are compressing rather than funding innovation, and much technology is sourced from partners (Arçelik/Beko, OEMs).
INNOVATION.quote: Voltas launched its Summer 2026 portfolio led by AI-powered Vertis Split AC Series

FORWARD.rationale: The calls discuss dealer/distribution reach, channel schemes and omni-channel development but never own-store counts, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share, so there is no basis to judge forward integration.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share is explicitly tracked against named competitors every quarter and Voltbek is gaining (refrigerators 5.2%→6.2%, washers 7.8%→8.2%), but core RAC share fell from 24.1% in Jun 2022 to 21.2% in Jun 2024 to 17.9% YTD Dec 2025, and the recent 15.8%→17.9% recovery was supported by channel schemes and discounts that hit margins.
SHAREGAIN.quote: over the last 12 months, we gained market share of roughly 2.1%

CULTURE.rationale: Management does disclose bad news candidly (MEP cost overruns and conservative provisions in FY23, market-share loss, QCO inventory drag) and keeps a conservative, low-borrowing balance sheet, but promises have slipped — Voltbek EBITDA breakeven was 'in near future' in Aug 2024 and still unachieved in Feb 2026 — and leadership has turned over (Bakshi to Menon, new CFO) rather than being long-tenured.
CULTURE.quote: Voltbek continues to reduce loss per units and move towards our goal of achieving EBITDA breakeven in near future

MOATTEST.rationale: Management's stated moat is distribution reach and brand, yet the record shows a well-funded copycat field eroding it — 'more than 65 brands' including private labels, disruptive competitor pricing, and a 6-point share loss over the period — with no time-, R&D-, data- or location-based barrier a new entrant could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: our very strong moat, which is our distribution and understanding the Indian market

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls there is no discussion of licence fees, AMC/service attach rates, renewals, installed base or customer advances as a funding source — the evidence is simply silent on recurring revenue.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are B2B to garment exporters, home-textile makers and brands; the calls never describe professional/installer specifiers, trade training programmes or channel-expert lock-in, so there is no evidence either way.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Yarn and fabric are the dominant input cost for VTL's customers, not a sub-1% critical ingredient, and pricing is set externally by cotton and international benchmarks rather than by the supplier — the opposite of toll-road economics (Jan 2026, May 2026 calls).
TOLLROAD.quote: the yarn prices are determined by the international cotton

LOWPRICE.rationale: Repeated cost-culture evidence across the years — internal cost-saving initiatives, ~INR2,500 crore modernisation/debottlenecking capex, biomass boilers and green power targeted at cost, and scale as one of India's largest efficient mills (Aug 2024, Jan 2026, May 2026) — but the low-cost position is undermined by India's structural cotton-price disadvantage, and management concedes margins depend on industry utilisation, not a copy-proof cost edge.
LOWPRICE.quote: in terms of the cost efficiency, in terms of the product, in terms of the internal cost saving initiatives

PRICING.rationale: Management states explicitly and repeatedly that realisations follow cotton and international benchmarks, that expensive Indian cotton 'has to be borne by us', and that fabric/garment price increases come only with a 2–3 month lag against customer resistance — the price-deflation opposite of pricing power (Jul 2022, Jan 2026, May 2026).
PRICING.quote: even if our cotton is expensive, we can’t pass it on because that’s a Indian phenomena only

BRAND.rationale: There is a genuine reputational franchise — 'Delivering Excellence. Since 1965.', a diversified blue-chip customer base and brands preferring large organised vendors under China+1 (Aug 2024) — but no A&P spend, no premium pricing and no consumer brand; the reputation buys order flow, not price.
BRAND.quote: the customer wants to deal with the better companies -- better organized companies and we definitely fall into that

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular named capability additions — Vardhman Performance Fabrics for technical/performance wear commissioned FY26, multi-fibre flexibility, contamination-free and value-added yarns, Budhni fabric line (Aug 2024, Jan 2026, May 2026) — but no R&D spend disclosure, no share-of-industry-R&D, and gross margins are commodity-set rather than innovation-funded.
INNOVATION.quote: A key strategic milestone during the period was the commissioning of Vardhman Performance Fabrics

FORWARD.rationale: Movement downstream is real but small and hesitant: vertical integration fibre→yarn→fabric→garment, and the FY26 reversal of its earlier stance to double garment capacity on the back of the EU FTA — yet management itself calls it 'very, very miniscule', and there are no own stores, franchising or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: we are likely to enhance the capacity of Garment division. We intend to make it to the double from the current capacity

SHAREGAIN.rationale: VTL keeps utilisation at 89–95% and adds capacity while ~11–12 million Indian spindles shut permanently and China+1 shifts brand sourcing to organised Indian vendors — structural share gain by survivorship (Aug 2024, Jan 2026, May 2026) — but no explicit share numbers are given and FY26 fabric utilisation fell 10 points on tariffs.
SHAREGAIN.quote: 11, 12 million spindles got permanently stopped into the system

CULTURE.rationale: Consistent long-tenured team (Neeraj Jain, Jhamb, Thapar, Bansal, Malhotra on every call from 2022 to 2026), candid bad news — hedging losses, stopped spindles, tariff hit, 'margins remain under pressure' — explicit conservatism in capex sizing, and promises delivered: the FY24-announced INR2,000–2,500 crore programme reported on-track in Aug 2024 and ~90% of spinning modernisation completed by May 2026.
CULTURE.quote: I’m happy to share almost 90% of the modernization got completed in this period

MOATTEST.rationale: Management's own account shows no un-replicable barrier: capacity is fungible, competitors return the moment margins improve, and the cost position depends on government cotton/MSP/import-duty policy rather than anything a funded newcomer could not buy (Aug 2024, Jan 2026).
MOATTEST.quote: Whenever we look at the margins are improving, a lot of those players who are stuck today, they'll also start coming back to the system

RECURRING.rationale: Advances from customers are explicitly discussed as a balance-sheet funding item (~INR3,200 crores, Oct 2025) and the group carries O&M/service revenue via WRTL and 'retail, service and overseas' segments, but management never quantifies attach rates, AMC share or renewals — the model is overwhelmingly one-off product sale.
RECURRING.quote: the typically the advance which is sitting on the balance sheet roughly is about INR 3,200 crores

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Retail sales run through ~370+ franchisee/channel-partner counters and installers who specify the brand to rooftop customers (20–25% of revenue, and price-insensitive per Feb 2026), but the calls show no trade-training programmes or professional-prescriber lock-in of the classic kind.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: roughly one-fourth, 20% to 25% of our revenue are coming only from the retail counters

TOLLROAD.rationale: The module is the single largest cost line of a solar project, not a sub-1% critical input, and management's own charts show sustained 80% price deflation with margins managed against input costs — the opposite of an un-negotiated toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: it shows the amount of decline in the prices that have happened on the solar as well as battery side

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost culture shows in backward integration explicitly aimed at undercutting Chinese landed cost (PV glass, polysilicon via Oman, ingot-wafer) and cheap capex (1GW HJT plant in Arizona for $20mn vs the Texas build), but Waaree runs high margins (22–25% EBITDA) rather than the low-margin/high-turn economics of the pattern.
LOWPRICE.quote: our target is our landed cost undercut by Chinese supply

PRICING.rationale: Retail counters fetch a stated 1–1.5 cent/panel premium and exports/DCR carry 300–350bps higher spreads, with EBITDA margin expanding from 17% to 25% over FY25–FY26; but this is mix and cost management ('we are always managing Waaree at the gross margin level'), in an industry with structural price deflation and a GST-driven price cut — not repeated price increases above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: that's a market which pays a premium of 1 to 1 and a half cent of every panel that we sell
